speaker: Vaishampayana
context: The narrator sets the scene: sleepless King Dhritarashtra sends his doorkeeper to fetch his wise brother Vidura.
devanagari:
द्वाःस्थं प्राह महाप्राज्ञो धृतराष्ट्रो महीपतिः ।
विदुरं द्रष्टुमिच्छामि तमिहानय माचिरम् ॥
iast:
dvāḥsthaṃ prāha mahāprājño dhṛtarāṣṭro mahīpatiḥ |
viduraṃ draṣṭumicchāmi tamihānaya māciram ||
english: Dhritarashtra, the very wise king, said to the doorkeeper: 'I wish to see Vidura. Bring him here without delay.'
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vaishampayana
context: The messenger delivers the king's summons to Vidura.
devanagari:
प्रहितो धृतराष्ट्रेण दूतः क्षत्तारमब्रवीत् ।
ईश्वरस्त्वां महाराजो महाप्राज्ञ दिदृक्षति ॥
iast:
prahito dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa dūtaḥ kṣattāramabravīt |
īśvarastvāṃ mahārājo mahāprājña didṛkṣati ||
english: Sent by Dhritarashtra, the messenger said to the steward: 'The great king, your lord, wishes to see you, wise one.'
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vaishampayana
context: Vidura arrives at the palace and asks to be announced.
devanagari:
एवमुक्तस्तु विदुरः प्राप्य राजनिवेशनम् ।
अब्रवीद्धृतराष्ट्राय द्वाःस्थ मां प्रतिवेदय ॥
iast:
evamuktastu viduraḥ prāpya rājaniveśanam |
abravīddhṛtarāṣṭrāya dvāḥstha māṃ prativedaya ||
english: Told this, Vidura went to the king's dwelling and said: 'Doorkeeper, announce me to Dhritarashtra.'
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: doorkeeper
context: The doorkeeper announces Vidura's arrival to the king.
devanagari:
विदुरोऽयमनुप्राप्तो राजेन्द्र तव शासनात् ।
द्रष्टुमिच्छति ते पादौ किं करोतु प्रशाधि माम् ॥
iast:
viduro'yamanuprāpto rājendra tava śāsanāt |
draṣṭumicchati te pādau kiṃ karotu praśādhi mām ||
english: Vidura has come at your command, lord of kings. He wishes to see your feet. Tell me, what shall he do?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra orders Vidura admitted at once.
devanagari:
प्रवेशय महाप्राज्ञं विदुरं दीर्घदर्शिनम् ।
अहं हि विदुरस्यास्य नाकाल्यो जातु दर्शने ॥
iast:
praveśaya mahāprājñaṃ viduraṃ dīrghadarśinam |
ahaṃ hi vidurasyāsya nākālyo jātu darśane ||
english: Bring in the wise, far-seeing Vidura. I am never unwilling to see this Vidura at any time.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: doorkeeper
context: The doorkeeper invites Vidura in.
devanagari:
प्रविशान्तः पुरं क्षत्तर्महाराजस्य धीमतः ।
न हि ते दर्शनेऽकाल्यो जातु राजा ब्रवीति माम् ॥
iast:
praviśāntaḥ puraṃ kṣattarmahārājasya dhīmataḥ |
na hi te darśane'kālyo jātu rājā bravīti mām ||
english: Enter the inner palace of the wise great king, steward. The king tells me that seeing you is never untimely.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vaishampayana
context: The narrator describes Vidura entering and speaking with folded hands to the anxious king.
devanagari:
ततः प्रविश्य विदुरो धृतराष्ट्र निवेशनम् ।
अब्रवीत्प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यं चिन्तयानं नराधिपम् ॥
iast:
tataḥ praviśya viduro dhṛtarāṣṭra niveśanam |
abravītprāñjalirvākyaṃ cintayānaṃ narādhipam ||
english: Then Vidura entered Dhritarashtra's chamber and, with folded hands, spoke to the king, who was lost in thought:
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura offers himself to the king (the source has no speaker line here; the words are Vidura's).
devanagari:
विदुरोऽहं महाप्राज्ञ सम्प्राप्तस्तव शासनात् ।
यदि किं चन कर्तव्यमयमस्मि प्रशाधि माम् ॥
iast:
viduro'haṃ mahāprājña samprāptastava śāsanāt |
yadi kiṃ cana kartavyamayamasmi praśādhi mām ||
english: I am Vidura, very wise one, come at your command. If there is anything to be done, here I am: command me.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra explains his worry: the envoy Sanjaya has returned from the Pandavas and will speak in the assembly tomorrow.
devanagari:
सञ्जयो विदुर प्राप्तो गर्हयित्वा च मां गतः ।
अजातशत्रोः श्वो वाक्यं सभामध्ये स वक्ष्यति ॥
iast:
sañjayo vidura prāpto garhayitvā ca māṃ gataḥ |
ajātaśatroḥ śvo vākyaṃ sabhāmadhye sa vakṣyati ||
english: Sanjaya came, Vidura, rebuked me and left. Tomorrow, in the middle of the assembly, he will speak Ajatashatru's message.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra admits that not knowing what will be said keeps him awake and burning.
devanagari:
तस्याद्य कुरुवीरस्य न विज्ञातं वचो मया ।
तन्मे दहति गात्राणि तदकार्षीत्प्रजागरम् ॥
iast:
tasyādya kuruvīrasya na vijñātaṃ vaco mayā |
tanme dahati gātrāṇi tadakārṣītprajāgaram ||
english: I have not learned today what that Kuru hero said. That burns my limbs; that has made me sleepless.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: The sleepless king asks Vidura for whatever counsel will do him good.
devanagari:
जाग्रतो दह्यमानस्य श्रेयो यदिह पश्यसि ।
तद्ब्रूहि त्वं हि नस्तात धर्मार्थकुशलो ह्यसि ॥
iast:
jāgrato dahyamānasya śreyo yadiha paśyasi |
tadbrūhi tvaṃ hi nastāta dharmārthakuśalo hyasi ||
english: Tell me what you see as good for one who lies awake, burning like this; for you, dear one, are skilled in dharma and in worldly affairs.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra describes his anxiety since Sanjaya's return: his senses are disturbed and his mind will not settle.
devanagari:
यतः प्राप्तः सञ्जयः पाण्डवेभ्यो
न मे यथावन्मनसः प्रशान्तिः ।
सवेन्द्रियाण्यप्रकृतिं गतानि
किं वक्ष्यतीत्येव हि मेऽद्य चिन्ता ॥
iast:
yataḥ prāptaḥ sañjayaḥ pāṇḍavebhyo
na me yathāvanmanasaḥ praśāntiḥ |
savendriyāṇyaprakṛtiṃ gatāni
kiṃ vakṣyatītyeva hi me'dya cintā ||
english: Since Sanjaya came back from the Pandavas, my mind has had no real peace. All my senses are out of order; my only thought today is, what will he say?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: The king asks Vidura to tell him what the Pandavas intend, and what would be good for him and his people.
devanagari:
तन्मे ब्रूहि विदुर त्वं यथावन्
मनीषितं सर्वमजातशत्रोः ।
यथा च नस्तात हितं भवेच्च
प्रजाश्च सर्वाः सुखिता भवेयुः ॥
iast:
tanme brūhi vidura tvaṃ yathāvan
manīṣitaṃ sarvamajātaśatroḥ |
yathā ca nastāta hitaṃ bhavecca
prajāśca sarvāḥ sukhitā bhaveyuḥ ||
english: So tell me truly, Vidura, everything Ajatashatru has in mind, and what would be good for us, dear one, so that all the people may be happy.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names who is kept awake at night: the weak under attack by the strong, those who have lost everything, the lustful and the thief.
devanagari:
अभियुक्तं बलवता दुर्बलं हीनसाधनम् ।
हृतस्वं कामिनं चोरमाविशन्ति प्रजागराः ॥
iast:
abhiyuktaṃ balavatā durbalaṃ hīnasādhanam |
hṛtasvaṃ kāminaṃ coramāviśanti prajāgarāḥ ||
english: Sleeplessness takes hold of a weak person without resources who is attacked by a strong one, of one whose wealth has been taken, of one full of desire, and of a thief.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura asks the king whether such faults, such as coveting others' wealth, are behind his sleeplessness.
devanagari:
कच्चिदेतैर्महादोषैर्न स्पृष्टोऽसि नराधिप ।
कच्चिन्न परवित्तेषु गृध्यन्विपरितप्यसे ॥
iast:
kaccidetairmahādoṣairna spṛṣṭo'si narādhipa |
kaccinna paravitteṣu gṛdhyanviparitapyase ||
english: I hope you are not touched by these great faults, lord of men. I hope you are not tormented by longing for others' wealth.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura for teaching that is righteous and leads to the highest good.
devanagari:
श्रोतुमिच्छामि ते धर्म्यं परं नैःश्रेयसं वचः ।
अस्मिन्राजर्षिवंशे हि त्वमेकः प्राज्ञसंमतः ॥
iast:
śrotumicchāmi te dharmyaṃ paraṃ naiḥśreyasaṃ vacaḥ |
asminrājarṣivaṃśe hi tvamekaḥ prājñasaṃmataḥ ||
english: I wish to hear from you words that are righteous and lead to the highest good, for in this line of royal sages you alone are held to be wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura tells Dhritarashtra that Yudhishthira, though fit to rule the world, was sent away by him.
devanagari:
रजा लक्षणसंपन्नस्त्रैलोक्यस्याधिपो भवेत् ।
प्रेष्यस्ते प्रेषितश्चैव धृतराष्ट्र युधिष्ठिरः ॥
iast:
rajā lakṣaṇasaṃpannastrailokyasyādhipo bhavet |
preṣyaste preṣitaścaiva dhṛtarāṣṭra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ||
english: A king endowed with every mark would be lord of the three worlds; yet Yudhishthira, your servant, was sent away by you, Dhritarashtra.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says Dhritarashtra, though righteous, has acted against what was right because of his blindness.
devanagari:
विपरीततरश्च त्वं भागधेये न संमतः ।
अर्चिषां प्रक्षयाच्चैव धर्मात्मा धर्मकोविदः ॥
iast:
viparītataraśca tvaṃ bhāgadheye na saṃmataḥ |
arciṣāṃ prakṣayāccaiva dharmātmā dharmakovidaḥ ||
english: You are quite the opposite, not counted worthy of a share, though righteous and learned in dharma, because of the loss of your eyesight.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says Yudhishthira bears many hardships out of gentleness, compassion and respect for the king.
devanagari:
आनृशंस्यादनुक्रोशाद्धर्मात्सत्यात्पराक्रमात् ।
गुरुत्वात्त्वयि संप्रेक्ष्य बहून्क्लेषांस्तितिक्षते ॥
iast:
ānṛśaṃsyādanukrośāddharmātsatyātparākramāt |
gurutvāttvayi saṃprekṣya bahūnkleṣāṃstitikṣate ||
english: Out of kindness, compassion, righteousness, truth and courage, and seeing you as his elder, he bears many hardships.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura asks how the king can hope to prosper while placing power in the hands of Duryodhana and his allies.
devanagari:
दुर्योधने सौबले च कर्णे दुःशासने तथा ।
एतेष्वैश्वर्यमाधाय कथं त्वं भूतिमिच्छसि ॥
iast:
duryodhane saubale ca karṇe duḥśāsane tathā |
eteṣvaiśvaryamādhāya kathaṃ tvaṃ bhūtimicchasi ||
english: Having placed your sovereignty in Duryodhana, Shakuni, Karna and Duhshasana, how can you hope for prosperity?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura gives an image: from the same tree come implements for different uses, just as both good and bad come from one source.
devanagari:
एकस्मात्वृक्षाद्यज्ञपत्राणि राजन्
स्रुक्च द्रौणी पेठनीपीडने च ।
एतस्माद्राजन्ब्रुवतो मे निबोध
एकस्माद्वै जायतेऽसच्च सच्च ॥
iast:
ekasmātvṛkṣādyajñapatrāṇi rājan
srukca drauṇī peṭhanīpīḍane ca |
etasmādrājanbruvato me nibodha
ekasmādvai jāyate'sacca sacca ||
english: From one tree, king, come the vessels for sacrifice, the ladle, the trough and the press. From this, king, learn from me as I speak: from one source arise both the bad and the good.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura begins describing the wise person: one whom self-knowledge, effort, patience and steadiness in dharma keep from straying.
devanagari:
आत्मज्ञानं समारंभस्तितिक्षा धर्मनित्यता ।
यमर्थान्नापकर्षन्ति स वै पण्दित उच्यते ॥
iast:
ātmajñānaṃ samāraṃbhastitikṣā dharmanityatā |
yamarthānnāpakarṣanti sa vai paṇdita ucyate ||
english: One whom self-knowledge, right effort, endurance and constancy in dharma do not drag away from their aims is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues describing the wise: they pursue what is praiseworthy, avoid what is condemned, and have faith.
devanagari:
निषेवते प्रशस्तानि निन्दितानि न सेवते ।
अनास्तिकः श्रद्दधान एतत्पण्डित लक्षणम् ॥
iast:
niṣevate praśastāni ninditāni na sevate |
anāstikaḥ śraddadhāna etatpaṇḍita lakṣaṇam ||
english: One who pursues what is praiseworthy and does not pursue what is condemned, who is not a disbeliever and has faith: these are the marks of the wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise are not carried away by anger, elation, pride, shame, stubbornness or vanity.
devanagari:
क्रोधो हर्षश्च दर्पश्च ह्रीस्तम्भो मान्यमानिता ।
यमर्थान्नापकर्षन्ति स वै पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
krodho harṣaśca darpaśca hrīstambho mānyamānitā |
yamarthānnāpakarṣanti sa vai paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One whom anger, elation, arrogance, shame, stubbornness and conceit do not drag away from their aims is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise keep their plans to themselves; others learn of them only when they are done.
devanagari:
यस्य कृत्यं न जानन्ति मन्त्रं वा मन्त्रितं परे ।
कृतमेवास्य जानन्ति स वै पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
yasya kṛtyaṃ na jānanti mantraṃ vā mantritaṃ pare |
kṛtamevāsya jānanti sa vai paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One whose plans and counsels others do not know, and whose work they know only once it is done, is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise are not stopped by cold, heat, fear, pleasure, prosperity or poverty.
devanagari:
यस्य कृत्यं न विघ्नन्ति शीतमुष्णं भयं रतिः ।
समृद्धिरसमृद्धिर्वा स वै पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
yasya kṛtyaṃ na vighnanti śītamuṣṇaṃ bhayaṃ ratiḥ |
samṛddhirasamṛddhirvā sa vai paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One whose work is not hindered by cold or heat, fear or pleasure, prosperity or adversity, is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise person's understanding follows dharma and true benefit, and chooses real benefit over mere pleasure.
devanagari:
यस्य संसारिणी प्रज्ञा धर्मार्थावनुवर्तते ।
कामादर्थं वृणीते यः स वै पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
yasya saṃsāriṇī prajñā dharmārthāvanuvartate |
kāmādarthaṃ vṛṇīte yaḥ sa vai paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One whose practical understanding follows dharma and true benefit, and who chooses real benefit over pleasure, is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise aim and act according to their capacity and look down on nothing.
devanagari:
यथाशक्ति चिकीर्षन्ति यथाशक्ति च कुर्वते ।
न किं चिदवमन्यन्ते पण्डिता भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
yathāśakti cikīrṣanti yathāśakti ca kurvate |
na kiṃ cidavamanyante paṇḍitā bharatarṣabha ||
english: The wise want to do what they can, and do what they can; and they despise nothing, best of the Bharatas.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names the first sign of wisdom: quick understanding, patient listening and not meddling unasked.
devanagari:
क्षिप्रं विजानाति चिरं शृणोति
विज्ञाय चार्थं भजते न कामात् ।
नासम्पृष्टो व्यौपयुङ्क्ते परार्थे
तत्प्रज्ञानं प्रथमं पण्डितस्य ॥
iast:
kṣipraṃ vijānāti ciraṃ śṛṇoti
vijñāya cārthaṃ bhajate na kāmāt |
nāsampṛṣṭo vyaupayuṅkte parārthe
tatprajñānaṃ prathamaṃ paṇḍitasya ||
english: Understanding quickly, listening long, acting on a matter only after grasping it and not out of desire, not offering opinions on others' affairs unasked: this is the first mark of the wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise do not long for the unattainable, do not grieve over what is lost, and do not lose their heads in trouble.
devanagari:
नाप्राप्यमभिवाञ्छन्ति नष्टं नेच्छन्ति शोचितुम् ।
आपत्सु च न मुह्यन्ति नराः पण्डित बुद्धयः ॥
iast:
nāprāpyamabhivāñchanti naṣṭaṃ necchanti śocitum |
āpatsu ca na muhyanti narāḥ paṇḍita buddhayaḥ ||
english: People of wise understanding do not long for what cannot be had, do not wish to grieve over what is lost, and are not bewildered in misfortune.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise decide, then act, and do not stop halfway; they do not waste time and are self-controlled.
devanagari:
निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः ।
अवन्ध्य कालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
niścitya yaḥ prakramate nāntarvasati karmaṇaḥ |
avandhya kālo vaśyātmā sa vai paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One who decides and then begins, who does not stop in the middle of a task, who does not waste time and has self-control, is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise delight in noble deeds, do what brings prosperity, and do not resent good advice.
devanagari:
आर्य कर्मणि राज्यन्ते भूतिकर्माणि कुर्वते ।
हितं च नाभ्यसूयन्ति पण्डिता भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
ārya karmaṇi rājyante bhūtikarmāṇi kurvate |
hitaṃ ca nābhyasūyanti paṇḍitā bharatarṣabha ||
english: The wise take delight in noble work, do what brings welfare, and do not find fault with what is good for them, best of the Bharatas.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise are not elated by honour or pained by dishonour, but stay undisturbed like a deep pool of the Ganga.
devanagari:
न हृष्यत्यात्मसंमाने नावमानेन तप्यते ।
गाङ्गो ह्रद इवाक्षोभ्यो यः स पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
na hṛṣyatyātmasaṃmāne nāvamānena tapyate |
gāṅgo hrada ivākṣobhyo yaḥ sa paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One who is not elated when honoured nor pained by dishonour, who is unruffled like a deep pool of the Ganga, is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise know the nature of all beings, the way of all actions and how to deal with people.
devanagari:
तत्त्वज्ञः सर्वभूतानां योगज्ञः सर्वकर्मणाम् ।
उपायज्ञो मनुष्याणां नरः पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
tattvajñaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ yogajñaḥ sarvakarmaṇām |
upāyajño manuṣyāṇāṃ naraḥ paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One who knows the truth of all beings, the method of all actions and the right approach to people is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise speak fluently and well, reason well, and grasp and explain texts quickly.
devanagari:
प्रवृत्त वाक्चित्रकथ ऊहवान्प्रतिभानवान् ।
आशु ग्रन्थस्य वक्ता च स वै पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
pravṛtta vākcitrakatha ūhavānpratibhānavān |
āśu granthasya vaktā ca sa vai paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One who speaks freely and engagingly, who reasons and has quick insight, and who can explain a text quickly, is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise person's learning follows understanding and understanding follows learning, without breaking noble bounds.
devanagari:
श्रुतं प्रज्ञानुगं यस्य प्रज्ञा चैव श्रुतानुगा ।
असम्भिन्नार्य मर्यादः पण्डिताख्यां लभेत सः ॥
iast:
śrutaṃ prajñānugaṃ yasya prajñā caiva śrutānugā |
asambhinnārya maryādaḥ paṇḍitākhyāṃ labheta saḥ ||
english: One whose learning follows understanding and whose understanding follows learning, who never breaks the bounds of the noble, earns the name of wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise stay humble even after gaining great wealth, learning or power.
devanagari:
अर्थं महान्तमासद्य विद्यामैश्वर्यमेव च ।
विचरत्यसमुन्नद्धो यस्य पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
arthaṃ mahāntamāsadya vidyāmaiśvaryameva ca |
vicaratyasamunnaddho yasya paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One who, having gained great wealth, learning or power, moves about without arrogance is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura begins describing the fool: unlearned yet proud, poor yet extravagant, wanting wealth without work.
devanagari:
अश्रुतश्च समुन्नद्धो दरिद्रश्च महामनाः ।
अर्थांश्चाकर्मणा प्रेप्सुर्मूढ इत्युच्यते बुधैः ॥
iast:
aśrutaśca samunnaddho daridraśca mahāmanāḥ |
arthāṃścākarmaṇā prepsurmūḍha ityucyate budhaiḥ ||
english: Puffed up though unlearned, grand in ideas though poor, wanting wealth without working: such a person the wise call a fool.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a fool neglects their own affairs for others' and acts falsely towards friends.
devanagari:
स्वमर्थं यः परित्यज्य परार्थमनुतिष्ठति ।
मिथ्या चरति मित्रार्थे यश्च मूढः स उच्यते ॥
iast:
svamarthaṃ yaḥ parityajya parārthamanutiṣṭhati |
mithyā carati mitrārthe yaśca mūḍhaḥ sa ucyate ||
english: One who gives up their own business to pursue another's, and who behaves falsely in matters concerning friends, is called a fool.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a fool desires those who do not want them, rejects those who do, and hates the powerful.
devanagari:
अकामां कामयति यः कामयानां परित्यजेत् ।
बलवन्तं च यो द्वेष्टि तमाहुर्मूढचेतसम् ॥
iast:
akāmāṃ kāmayati yaḥ kāmayānāṃ parityajet |
balavantaṃ ca yo dveṣṭi tamāhurmūḍhacetasam ||
english: One who desires those who do not desire them and rejects those who do, and who hates the powerful, they call a fool.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura repeats the point (a variant line in the source): a fool desires the unwilling and hates those who want them.
devanagari:
अकामान्कामयति यः कामयानान्परिद्विषन् ।
बलवन्तं च यो द्वेष्टि तमाहुर्मूढचेतसम् ॥
iast:
akāmānkāmayati yaḥ kāmayānānparidviṣan |
balavantaṃ ca yo dveṣṭi tamāhurmūḍhacetasam ||
english: One who desires those who do not desire them, hates those who do, and hates the powerful, they call a fool.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a fool makes enemies into friends, hates and harms friends, and starts wicked projects.
devanagari:
अमित्रं कुरुते मित्रं मित्रं द्वेष्टि हिनस्ति च ।
कर्म चारभते दुष्टं तमाहुर्मूढचेतसम् ॥
iast:
amitraṃ kurute mitraṃ mitraṃ dveṣṭi hinasti ca |
karma cārabhate duṣṭaṃ tamāhurmūḍhacetasam ||
english: One who makes an enemy a friend, hates and harms a friend, and begins wicked undertakings, they call a fool.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a fool spreads tasks everywhere, doubts everything, and is slow where speed is needed.
devanagari:
संसारयति कृत्यानि सर्वत्र विचिकित्सते ।
चिरं करोति क्षिप्रार्थे स मूढो भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
saṃsārayati kṛtyāni sarvatra vicikitsate |
ciraṃ karoti kṣiprārthe sa mūḍho bharatarṣabha ||
english: One who drags out tasks, doubts everything, and takes long over what needs to be done quickly is a fool, best of the Bharatas.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a fool neglects the ancestors and the gods, and finds no good friend.
devanagari:
श्राद्धं पितृभ्यो न ददाति दैवतानि नार्चति ।
सुहृन्मित्रं न लभते तमाहुर्मूढचेतसम् ॥
iast:
śrāddhaṃ pitṛbhyo na dadāti daivatāni nārcati |
suhṛnmitraṃ na labhate tamāhurmūḍhacetasam ||
english: One who does not offer to the ancestors, does not worship the gods, and finds no well-wishing friend, they call a fool.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the lowest fool enters uninvited, talks a lot unasked and trusts the untrustworthy.
devanagari:
अनाहूतः प्रविशति अपृष्टो बहु भाषते ।
विश्वसत्यप्रमत्तेषु मूढ चेता नराधमः ॥
iast:
anāhūtaḥ praviśati apṛṣṭo bahu bhāṣate |
viśvasatyapramatteṣu mūḍha cetā narādhamaḥ ||
english: Entering uninvited, talking much without being asked, and trusting the untrustworthy: such a person is a fool and the lowest of people.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the greatest fool blames others for faults they share, and gets angry without power.
devanagari:
परं क्षिपति दोषेण वर्तमानः स्वयं तथा ।
यश्च क्रुध्यत्यनीशः सन्स च मूढतमो नरः ॥
iast:
paraṃ kṣipati doṣeṇa vartamānaḥ svayaṃ tathā |
yaśca krudhyatyanīśaḥ sansa ca mūḍhatamo naraḥ ||
english: One who blames another for a fault while committing it themselves, and who gets angry while powerless, is the greatest fool.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a fool, not knowing their own strength, seeks the unattainable without dharma, benefit or effort.
devanagari:
आत्मनो बलमाज्ञाय धर्मार्थपरिवर्जितम् ।
अलभ्यमिच्छन्नैष्कर्म्यान्मूढ बुद्धिरिहोच्यते ॥
iast:
ātmano balamājñāya dharmārthaparivarjitam |
alabhyamicchannaiṣkarmyānmūḍha buddhirihocyate ||
english: Not knowing their own strength, wanting what cannot be had without dharma or real benefit and without effort: such a person is called a fool.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a fool teaches those who cannot be taught, serves emptiness and attends the miserly.
devanagari:
अशिष्यं शास्ति यो राजन्यश्च शून्यमुपासते ।
कदर्यं भजते यश्च तमाहुर्मूढचेतसम् ॥
iast:
aśiṣyaṃ śāsti yo rājanyaśca śūnyamupāsate |
kadaryaṃ bhajate yaśca tamāhurmūḍhacetasam ||
english: One who instructs those who cannot be instructed, who serves what is empty, and who attends on a miser, they call a fool, king.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura repeats that the wise stay humble with great wealth, learning or power (repeating verse 37).
devanagari:
अर्थं महान्तमासाद्य विद्यामैश्वर्यमेव वा ।
विचरत्यसमुन्नद्धो यः स पण्डित उच्यते ॥
iast:
arthaṃ mahāntamāsādya vidyāmaiśvaryameva vā |
vicaratyasamunnaddho yaḥ sa paṇḍita ucyate ||
english: One who, having gained great wealth, learning or power, moves about without arrogance is called wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura condemns one who eats well and dresses finely alone without sharing with those who depend on him.
devanagari:
एकः सम्पन्नमश्नाति वस्ते वासश्च शोभनम् ।
योऽसंविभज्य भृत्येभ्यः को नृशंसतरस्ततः ॥
iast:
ekaḥ sampannamaśnāti vaste vāsaśca śobhanam |
yo'saṃvibhajya bhṛtyebhyaḥ ko nṛśaṃsatarastataḥ ||
english: Who is crueller than one who alone eats rich food and wears fine clothes without sharing with those who serve him?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one person may commit a wrong while many enjoy its fruits, but the doer alone bears the guilt.
devanagari:
एकः पापानि कुरुते फलं भुङ्क्ते महाजनः ।
भोक्तारो विप्रमुच्यन्ते कर्ता दोषेण लिप्यते ॥
iast:
ekaḥ pāpāni kurute phalaṃ bhuṅkte mahājanaḥ |
bhoktāro vipramucyante kartā doṣeṇa lipyate ||
english: One person commits wrongs and many enjoy the fruit; those who enjoy it go free, but the doer is stained by the fault.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says an arrow may kill one person, but a clever mind's plan can destroy a kingdom with its king.
devanagari:
एकं हन्यान्न वाहन्यादिषुर्मुक्तो धनुष्मता ।
बुद्धिर्बुद्धिमतोत्सृष्टा हन्याद्राष्ट्रं सराजकम् ॥
iast:
ekaṃ hanyānna vāhanyādiṣurmukto dhanuṣmatā |
buddhirbuddhimatotsṛṣṭā hanyādrāṣṭraṃ sarājakam ||
english: An arrow shot by an archer may kill one person or none; but a plan let loose by a clever mind can destroy a kingdom together with its king.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura gives a numbered riddle of self-mastery: decide the two by the one, control the three by the four, and be happy.
devanagari:
एकया द्वे विनिश्चित्य त्रींश्चतुर्भिर्वशे कुरु ।
पञ्च जित्वा विदित्वा षट्सप्त हित्वा सुखी भव ॥
iast:
ekayā dve viniścitya trīṃścaturbhirvaśe kuru |
pañca jitvā viditvā ṣaṭsapta hitvā sukhī bhava ||
english: Deciding the two by the one, bring the three under control by the four; conquering the five, knowing the six and giving up the seven, be happy.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says poison or a weapon kills one, but a leaked secret plan destroys king, kingdom and people.
devanagari:
एकं विषरसो हन्ति शस्त्रेणैकश्च वध्यते ।
सराष्ट्रं स प्रजं हन्ति राजानं मन्त्रविस्रवः ॥
iast:
ekaṃ viṣaraso hanti śastreṇaikaśca vadhyate |
sarāṣṭraṃ sa prajaṃ hanti rājānaṃ mantravisravaḥ ||
english: Poison kills one person, and a weapon kills one; but leaking a secret counsel destroys the king along with his kingdom and his people.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises against doing certain things alone: eating delicacies, deciding matters, travelling, and keeping watch.
devanagari:
एकः स्वादु न भुञ्जीत एकश्चार्थान्न चिन्तयेत् ।
एको न गच्छेदध्वानं नैकः सुप्तेषु जागृयात् ॥
iast:
ekaḥ svādu na bhuñjīta ekaścārthānna cintayet |
eko na gacchedadhvānaṃ naikaḥ supteṣu jāgṛyāt ||
english: One should not eat delicacies alone, nor deliberate on matters alone, nor travel a road alone, nor stay awake alone among those asleep.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura tells the king that truth, the one without a second, is the stairway to heaven, like a boat across the sea.
devanagari:
एकमेवाद्वितीयं तद्यद्राजन्नावबुध्यसे ।
सत्यं स्वर्गस्य सोपानं पारावारस्य नौरिव ॥
iast:
ekamevādvitīyaṃ tadyadrājannāvabudhyase |
satyaṃ svargasya sopānaṃ pārāvārasya nauriva ||
english: That which you do not recognise, king, is one alone, without a second: truth is the stairway to heaven, like a boat to cross the sea.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the forgiving have only one fault: people think them weak.
devanagari:
एकः क्षमावतां दोषो द्वितीयो नोपलभ्यते ।
यदेनं क्षमया युक्तमशक्तं मन्यते जनः ॥
iast:
ekaḥ kṣamāvatāṃ doṣo dvitīyo nopalabhyate |
yadenaṃ kṣamayā yuktamaśaktaṃ manyate janaḥ ||
english: The forgiving have one fault, and no second is found: people think one who is forgiving is weak.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says that fault should not count, for forgiveness is the highest strength.
devanagari:
सोऽस्य दोषो न मन्तव्यः क्षमा हि परमं बलम् ।
क्षमा गुणो ह्यशक्तानां शक्तानां भूषणं तथा ॥
iast:
so'sya doṣo na mantavyaḥ kṣamā hi paramaṃ balam |
kṣamā guṇo hyaśaktānāṃ śaktānāṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ tathā ||
english: That should not be counted as a fault, for forgiveness is the highest strength. Forgiveness is a virtue of the weak and an ornament of the strong.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says forgiveness wins people over; what can the wicked do to one who holds the conch of peace?
devanagari:
क्षमा वशीकृतिर्लोके क्षमया किं न साध्यते ।
शान्तिशङ्खः करे यस्य किं करिष्यति दुर्जनः ॥
iast:
kṣamā vaśīkṛtirloke kṣamayā kiṃ na sādhyate |
śāntiśaṅkhaḥ kare yasya kiṃ kariṣyati durjanaḥ ||
english: Forgiveness wins over the world; what cannot be achieved by forgiveness? What can a wicked person do to one who holds the conch of peace in his hand?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says fire falling where there is no grass dies out by itself; the unforgiving entangle both others and themselves in faults.
devanagari:
अतृणे पतितो वह्निः स्वयमेवोपशाम्यति ।
अक्षमावान्परं दोषैरात्मान्ं चैव योजयेत् ॥
iast:
atṛṇe patito vahniḥ svayamevopaśāmyati |
akṣamāvānparaṃ doṣairātmānṃ caiva yojayet ||
english: Fire falling where there is no grass goes out by itself; but one without forgiveness entangles others, and themselves too, in faults.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names the single best of several things: dharma, forgiveness, knowledge and non-violence.
devanagari:
एको धर्मः परं श्रेयः क्षमैका शान्तिरुत्तमा ।
विद्यैका परमा दृष्टिरहिंसैका सुखावहा ॥
iast:
eko dharmaḥ paraṃ śreyaḥ kṣamaikā śāntiruttamā |
vidyaikā paramā dṛṣṭirahiṃsaikā sukhāvahā ||
english: Dharma alone is the highest good; forgiveness alone is the best peace; knowledge alone is the highest vision; non-violence alone brings happiness.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names two the earth swallows like a snake swallows creatures in their holes: a king who does not resist and a brahmin who never travels.
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ ग्रसते भूमिः सर्पो बिलशयानिव ।
राजानं चाविरोद्धारं ब्राह्मणं चाप्रवासिनम् ॥
iast:
dvāvimau grasate bhūmiḥ sarpo bilaśayāniva |
rājānaṃ cāviroddhāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ cāpravāsinam ||
english: The earth swallows these two as a snake swallows creatures lying in their holes: a king who does not resist, and a brahmin who never leaves home.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says two practices make a person shine: never speaking harshly and never asking favours of the wicked.
devanagari:
द्वे कर्मणी नरः कुर्वन्नस्मिँल्लोके विरोचते ।
अब्रुवन्परुषं किं चिदसतो नार्थयंस्तथा ॥
iast:
dve karmaṇī naraḥ kurvannasmim̐lloke virocate |
abruvanparuṣaṃ kiṃ cidasato nārthayaṃstathā ||
english: A person who does two things shines in this world: speaking nothing harsh, and asking nothing of the wicked.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names two who rely on others' opinions, including a stereotype about women.
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषव्याघ्र परप्रत्यय कारिणौ ।
स्त्रियः कामित कामिन्यो लोकः पूजित पूजकः ॥
iast:
dvāvimau puruṣavyāghra parapratyaya kāriṇau |
striyaḥ kāmita kāminyo lokaḥ pūjita pūjakaḥ ||
english: These two, tiger among men, act on the belief of others: women who desire those desired by others, and people who honour whoever is honoured.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names two sharp thorns that wither the body: desire without means and anger without power.
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ कण्टकौ तीक्ष्णौ शरीरपरिशोषणौ ।
यश्चाधनः कामयते यश्च कुप्यत्यनीश्वरः ॥
iast:
dvāvimau kaṇṭakau tīkṣṇau śarīrapariśoṣaṇau |
yaścādhanaḥ kāmayate yaśca kupyatyanīśvaraḥ ||
english: These two are sharp thorns that wither the body: one who is poor yet full of desires, and one who is powerless yet angry.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names two who do not shine because they act against their role: an idle householder and a busy mendicant.
devanagari:
द्वावेव न विराजेते विपरीतेन कर्मणा ।
गृहस्थश्च निरारंभः कार्यवांश्चैव भिक्षुकः ॥
iast:
dvāveva na virājete viparītena karmaṇā |
gṛhasthaśca nirāraṃbhaḥ kāryavāṃścaiva bhikṣukaḥ ||
english: These two do not shine, acting against their role: a householder without enterprise, and a mendicant busy with worldly affairs.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names two who stand above heaven: a powerful person who forgives and a poor person who gives.
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ राजन्स्वर्गस्य परि तिष्ठतः ।
प्रभुश्च क्षमया युक्तो दरिद्रश्च प्रदानवान् ॥
iast:
dvāvimau puruṣau rājansvargasya pari tiṣṭhataḥ |
prabhuśca kṣamayā yukto daridraśca pradānavān ||
english: These two, king, stand above heaven: a powerful person endowed with forgiveness, and a poor person who gives.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names two misuses of honestly earned wealth: giving to the unworthy and not giving to the worthy.
devanagari:
न्यायागतस्य द्रव्यस्य बोद्धव्यौ द्वावतिक्रमौ ।
अपात्रे प्रतिपत्तिश्च पात्रे चाप्रतिपादनम् ॥
iast:
nyāyāgatasya dravyasya boddhavyau dvāvatikramau |
apātre pratipattiśca pātre cāpratipādanam ||
english: Of wealth honestly gained, two misuses should be understood: giving it to the unworthy, and not giving it to the worthy.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura, in a hyperbole, names two who deserve to be drowned with a stone round their neck: the rich who never give and the poor who never strive.
devanagari:
द्वावंभसि निवेष्टव्यौ गले बद्ध्वा दृढं शिलाम् ।
धनवन्तमदातारं दरिद्रं चातपस्विनम् ॥
iast:
dvāvaṃbhasi niveṣṭavyau gale baddhvā dṛḍhaṃ śilām |
dhanavantamadātāraṃ daridraṃ cātapasvinam ||
english: These two should be thrown into the water with a stone tied firmly to the neck: a rich person who does not give, and a poor person who does not practise austerity.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names two who pierce the sun's disc (reach the highest): the renunciant joined in yoga and one killed facing the enemy in battle.
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषव्याघ्र सुर्यमण्डलभेदिनौ ।
परिव्राड्योगयुक्तश्च रणे चाभिमुखो हतः ॥
iast:
dvāvimau puruṣavyāghra suryamaṇḍalabhedinau |
parivrāḍyogayuktaśca raṇe cābhimukho hataḥ ||
english: These two, tiger among men, pierce the disc of the sun: a wandering ascetic joined in yoga, and one slain in battle while facing the enemy.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura notes three grades of conduct taught by those who know the Veda: lowest, middling and best.
devanagari:
त्रयो न्याया मनुष्याणां श्रूयन्ते भरतर्षभ ।
कनीयान्मध्यमः श्रेष्ठ इति वेदविदो विदुः ॥
iast:
trayo nyāyā manuṣyāṇāṃ śrūyante bharatarṣabha |
kanīyānmadhyamaḥ śreṣṭha iti vedavido viduḥ ||
english: Three courses of conduct are spoken of among people, best of the Bharatas: the lesser, the middling and the best. So the knowers of the Veda say.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says people are of three grades and should be given work that matches.
devanagari:
त्रिविधाः पुरुषा राजन्नुत्तमाधममध्यमाः ।
नियोजयेद्यथावत्तांस्त्रिविधेष्वेव कर्मसु ॥
iast:
trividhāḥ puruṣā rājannuttamādhamamadhyamāḥ |
niyojayedyathāvattāṃstrividheṣveva karmasu ||
english: People are of three kinds, king: the best, the lowest and the middling. One should assign them properly to the three kinds of work.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura states the old rule that a wife, a slave and a son own nothing of their own.
devanagari:
त्रय एवाधना राजन्भार्या दासस्तथा सुतः ।
यत्ते समधिगच्छन्ति यस्य ते तस्य तद्धनम् ॥
iast:
traya evādhanā rājanbhāryā dāsastathā sutaḥ |
yatte samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya taddhanam ||
english: Three own no wealth, king: a wife, a slave and a son. Whatever they earn belongs to the one they belong to.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names three faults that bring ruin: stealing others' property, violating others' wives and abandoning a friend.
devanagari:
हरणं च परस्वानां परदाराभिमर्शनम् ।
सुहृदश्च परित्यागस्त्रयो दोषा क्षयावहः ॥
iast:
haraṇaṃ ca parasvānāṃ paradārābhimarśanam |
suhṛdaśca parityāgastrayo doṣā kṣayāvahaḥ ||
english: Taking what belongs to others, assaulting another's wife and abandoning a friend: these three faults bring ruin.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names desire, anger and greed as the threefold gate to hell that destroys the self (compare Gita 16.21).
devanagari:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
iast:
trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ |
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
english: This threefold gate of hell destroys the self: desire, anger and greed. So one should give up these three.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says rescuing an enemy from distress is as great as gaining a boon, a kingdom or a son.
devanagari:
वरप्रदानं राज्यां च पुत्रजन्म च भारत ।
शत्रोश्च मोक्षणं कृच्छ्रात्त्रीणि चैकं च तत्समम् ॥
iast:
varapradānaṃ rājyāṃ ca putrajanma ca bhārata |
śatrośca mokṣaṇaṃ kṛcchrāttrīṇi caikaṃ ca tatsamam ||
english: Receiving a boon, gaining a kingdom and the birth of a son, Bharata: these three, and a fourth, rescuing an enemy from distress, are equal.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says three who seek refuge must never be abandoned, even in hard times: the devoted, the one who serves, and the one who says 'I am yours'.
devanagari:
भक्तं च बजमानं च तवास्मीति वादिनम् ।
त्रीनेतान् शरणं प्राप्तान्विषमेऽपि न सन्त्यजेत् ॥
iast:
bhaktaṃ ca bajamānaṃ ca tavāsmīti vādinam |
trīnetān śaraṇaṃ prāptānviṣame'pi na santyajet ||
english: The devoted, the one who serves you, and the one who says 'I am yours': these three, having come for refuge, should not be abandoned even in hard times.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns a powerful ruler not to take counsel from the dull, the procrastinating, the lazy or flatterers.
devanagari:
चत्वारि राज्ञा तु महाबलेन
वर्ज्यान्याहुः पण्डितस्तानि विद्यात् ।
अल्पप्रज्ञैः सह मन्त्रं न कुर्यान्
न दीर्घसूत्रैरलसैश्चारणैश्च ॥
iast:
catvāri rājñā tu mahābalena
varjyānyāhuḥ paṇḍitastāni vidyāt |
alpaprajñaiḥ saha mantraṃ na kuryān
na dīrghasūtrairalasaiścāraṇaiśca ||
english: The wise say a mighty king should avoid four; let him know them: he should not take counsel with those of little understanding, with procrastinators, with the lazy, or with flatterers.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names four who should live in a prosperous householder's home: an aged relative, a fallen noble, a poor friend and a childless sister.
devanagari:
चत्वारि ते तात गृहे वसन्तु
श्रियाभिजुष्टस्य गृहस्थ धर्मे ।
वृद्धो ज्ञातिरवसन्नः कुलीनः
सखा दरिद्रो भगिनी चानपत्या ॥
iast:
catvāri te tāta gṛhe vasantu
śriyābhijuṣṭasya gṛhastha dharme |
vṛddho jñātiravasannaḥ kulīnaḥ
sakhā daridro bhaginī cānapatyā ||
english: Dear one, let four live in your house, you who are blessed with fortune and follow the householder's dharma: an aged relative, a person of good family fallen on hard times, a poor friend, and a sister without children.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura introduces four things Brihaspati told Indra bear fruit at once.
devanagari:
चत्वार्याह महाराज सद्यस्कानि बृहस्पतिः ।
पृच्छते त्रिदशेन्द्राय तानीमानि निबोध मे ॥
iast:
catvāryāha mahārāja sadyaskāni bṛhaspatiḥ |
pṛcchate tridaśendrāya tānīmāni nibodha me ||
english: Brihaspati, great king, spoke of four things that bear fruit at once, when asked by the lord of the gods. Learn them from me:
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists them: the gods' resolve, the influence of the wise, the humility of the learned and the ruin of evildoers.
devanagari:
देवतानां च सङ्कल्पमनुभावं च धीमताम् ।
विनयं कृतविद्यानां विनाशं पापकर्मणाम् ॥
iast:
devatānāṃ ca saṅkalpamanubhāvaṃ ca dhīmatām |
vinayaṃ kṛtavidyānāṃ vināśaṃ pāpakarmaṇām ||
english: the resolve of the gods, the power of the wise, the humility of the learned, and the ruin of those who do evil.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says four rites that remove fear bring fear when done wrongly, out of vanity.
devanagari:
चत्वारि कर्माण्यभयङ्कराणि
भयं प्रयच्छन्त्ययथाकृतानि ।
मानाग्निहोत्रं उत मानमौनं
मानेनाधीतमुत मानयज्ञः ॥
iast:
catvāri karmāṇyabhayaṅkarāṇi
bhayaṃ prayacchantyayathākṛtāni |
mānāgnihotraṃ uta mānamaunaṃ
mānenādhītamuta mānayajñaḥ ||
english: Four acts that remove fear bring fear when not done properly: the fire offering done for pride, silence kept for pride, study done for pride, and sacrifice done for pride.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names five 'fires' a person must serve with care: father, mother, the sacred fire, oneself and the teacher.
devanagari:
पञ्चाग्नयो मनुष्येण परिचर्याः प्रयत्नतः ।
पिता माताग्निरात्मा च गुरुश्च भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
pañcāgnayo manuṣyeṇa paricaryāḥ prayatnataḥ |
pitā mātāgnirātmā ca guruśca bharatarṣabha ||
english: Five fires should be tended by a person with care: father, mother, the sacred fire, oneself and the teacher, best of the Bharatas.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says honouring five (gods, ancestors, people, mendicants and guests) brings pure fame.
devanagari:
पञ्चैव पूजयँल्लोके यशः प्राप्नोति केवलम् ।
देवान्पितॄन्मनुष्यांश्च भिक्षूनतिथिपञ्चमान् ॥
iast:
pañcaiva pūjayam̐lloke yaśaḥ prāpnoti kevalam |
devānpitṝnmanuṣyāṃśca bhikṣūnatithipañcamān ||
english: Honouring five alone, one gains fame in the world: the gods, the ancestors, people, mendicants, and guests as the fifth.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says five will follow you wherever you go: friends, enemies, the neutral, those who depend on you and those you depend on.
devanagari:
पञ्च त्वानुगमिष्यन्ति यत्र यत्र गमिष्यसि ।
मित्राण्यमित्रा मध्यस्था उपजीव्योपजीविनः ॥
iast:
pañca tvānugamiṣyanti yatra yatra gamiṣyasi |
mitrāṇyamitrā madhyasthā upajīvyopajīvinaḥ ||
english: Five will follow you wherever you go: friends, enemies, the neutral, those who live on you and those you live on.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says if even one of the five senses is unguarded, wisdom leaks away like water from a hole in a water skin.
devanagari:
पञ्चेन्द्रियस्य मर्त्यस्य छिद्रं चेदेकमिन्द्रियम् ।
ततोऽस्य स्रवति प्रज्ञा दृतेः पादादिवोदकम् ॥
iast:
pañcendriyasya martyasya chidraṃ cedekamindriyam |
tato'sya sravati prajñā dṛteḥ pādādivodakam ||
english: If one of a mortal's five senses has a hole, through it their wisdom flows out, like water from the foot of a leather bag.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names six faults to drop for anyone who wants to prosper: sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.
devanagari:
षड्दोषाः पुरुषेणेह हातव्या भूतिमिच्छता ।
निद्रा तन्द्री भयं क्रोध आलस्यं दीर्घसूत्रता ॥
iast:
ṣaḍdoṣāḥ puruṣeṇeha hātavyā bhūtimicchatā |
nidrā tandrī bhayaṃ krodha ālasyaṃ dīrghasūtratā ||
english: Six faults should be given up here by a person who wants to prosper: too much sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names those to leave like a leaking boat: a teacher who will not teach and a priest who has not studied (1.88-1.89).
devanagari:
षडिमान्पुरुषो जह्याद्भिन्नां नावमिवार्णवे ।
अप्रवक्तारमाचार्यमनधीयानमृत्विजम् ॥
iast:
ṣaḍimānpuruṣo jahyādbhinnāṃ nāvamivārṇave |
apravaktāramācāryamanadhīyānamṛtvijam ||
english: A person should give up these six, like a leaking boat at sea: a teacher who does not teach, a priest who has not studied,
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura completes the list, including a wife who speaks unkindly, in terms of his time.
devanagari:
अरक्षितारं राजानं भार्यां चाप्रिय वादिनीम् ।
ग्रामकारं च गोपालं वनकामं च नापितम् ॥
iast:
arakṣitāraṃ rājānaṃ bhāryāṃ cāpriya vādinīm |
grāmakāraṃ ca gopālaṃ vanakāmaṃ ca nāpitam ||
english: a king who does not protect, a wife who speaks unkindly, a cowherd who wants to live in the village, and a barber who wants to live in the forest.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names six qualities never to give up: truth, generosity, diligence, freedom from envy, forbearance and steadiness.
devanagari:
षडेव तु गुणाः पुंसा न हातव्याः कदाचन ।
सत्यं दानमनालस्यमनसूया क्षमा धृतिः ॥
iast:
ṣaḍeva tu guṇāḥ puṃsā na hātavyāḥ kadācana |
satyaṃ dānamanālasyamanasūyā kṣamā dhṛtiḥ ||
english: Six qualities a person should never give up: truthfulness, generosity, diligence, freedom from envy, forbearance and steadiness.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names six joys of life: steady income, health, a loving spouse, an obedient son and useful knowledge.
devanagari:
अर्थागमो नित्यमरोगिता च
प्रिया च भार्या प्रियवादिनी च ।
वश्यश्च पुत्रोऽर्थकरी च विद्या
षट् जीवलोकस्य सुखानि राजन् ॥
iast:
arthāgamo nityamarogitā ca
priyā ca bhāryā priyavādinī ca |
vaśyaśca putro'rthakarī ca vidyā
ṣaṭ jīvalokasya sukhāni rājan ||
english: A steady income, constant good health, a beloved and sweet-spoken wife, an obedient son and knowledge that earns a living: these, king, are the six joys of the world of the living.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who masters the six inner enemies is touched by no sin, let alone misfortune.
devanagari:
षण्णामात्मनि नित्यानामैश्वर्यं योऽधिगच्छति ।
न स पापैः कुतोऽनर्थैर्युज्यते विजितेन्द्रियः ॥
iast:
ṣaṇṇāmātmani nityānāmaiśvaryaṃ yo'dhigacchati |
na sa pāpaiḥ kuto'narthairyujyate vijitendriyaḥ ||
english: One who gains mastery over the six that always dwell within, having conquered the senses, is not touched by sins, let alone by misfortunes.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists six who live off others' weaknesses: thieves off the careless, doctors off the sick (1.93-1.94).
devanagari:
षडिमे षट्सु जीवन्ति सप्तमो नोपलभ्यते ।
चोराः प्रमत्ते जीवन्ति व्याधितेषु चिकित्सकाः ॥
iast:
ṣaḍime ṣaṭsu jīvanti saptamo nopalabhyate |
corāḥ pramatte jīvanti vyādhiteṣu cikitsakāḥ ||
english: These six live off six; a seventh is not found: thieves live off the careless, doctors off the sick,
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura completes the list of those who live off others, including a stereotype of women.
devanagari:
प्रमदाः कामयानेषु यजमानेषु याजकाः ।
राजा विवदमानेषु नित्यं मूर्खेषु पण्डिताः ॥
iast:
pramadāḥ kāmayāneṣu yajamāneṣu yājakāḥ |
rājā vivadamāneṣu nityaṃ mūrkheṣu paṇḍitāḥ ||
english: women off the lustful, priests off those who sacrifice, the king off those who quarrel, and the learned always off fools.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists things ruined by a moment's neglect, in the terms of his time, including a wife and caste company.
devanagari:
षडिमानि विनश्यन्ति मुहूर्तमनवेक्षणात् ।
गावः सेवा कृषिर्भार्या विद्या वृषलसंगतिः ॥
iast:
ṣaḍimāni vinaśyanti muhūrtamanavekṣaṇāt |
gāvaḥ sevā kṛṣirbhāryā vidyā vṛṣalasaṃgatiḥ ||
english: These six are ruined by a moment's neglect: cows, service, farming, a wife, learning and company with a shudra.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists those who scorn a past benefactor: students their teacher, a married man his mother (1.96-1.97).
devanagari:
षडेते ह्यवमन्यन्ते नित्यं पूर्वोपकारिणम् ।
आचार्यं शिक्षिता शिष्याः कृतदारश्च मातरम् ॥
iast:
ṣaḍete hyavamanyante nityaṃ pūrvopakāriṇam |
ācāryaṃ śikṣitā śiṣyāḥ kṛtadāraśca mātaram ||
english: These six always disregard one who once helped them: students, once taught, their teacher; a married man his mother;
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura completes the list of ingratitude: the satisfied lover, those who have crossed the forest and the cured patient.
devanagari:
नारिं विगतकामस्तु कृतार्थाश्च प्रयोजकम् ।
नावं निस्तीर्णकान्तारा नातुराश्च चिकित्सकम् ॥
iast:
nāriṃ vigatakāmastu kṛtārthāśca prayojakam |
nāvaṃ nistīrṇakāntārā nāturāśca cikitsakam ||
english: a man whose desire is spent, the woman; those whose aim is achieved, the one who helped; those who have crossed the wilderness, the boat; and the cured, their doctor.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names six other joys of life: health, freedom from debt, living at home, good company, an independent living and living without fear.
devanagari:
आरोग्यमानृण्यमविप्रवासः
सद्भिर्मनुष्यैः सह संप्रयोगः ।
स्वप्रत्यया वृत्तिरभीतवासः
षट् जीवलोकस्य सुखानि राजन् ॥
iast:
ārogyamānṛṇyamavipravāsaḥ
sadbhirmanuṣyaiḥ saha saṃprayogaḥ |
svapratyayā vṛttirabhītavāsaḥ
ṣaṭ jīvalokasya sukhāni rājan ||
english: Health, freedom from debt, not living abroad, the company of good people, a livelihood of one's own, and living without fear: these, king, are the six joys of the world of the living.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names six who are always unhappy: the envious, the disgusted, the discontented, the angry, the suspicious and those who live off others.
devanagari:
ईर्षुर्घृणी नसन्तुष्टः क्रोधनो नित्यशङ्कितः ।
परभाग्योपजीवी च षडेते नित्यदुःखिताः ॥
iast:
īrṣurghṛṇī nasantuṣṭaḥ krodhano nityaśaṅkitaḥ |
parabhāgyopajīvī ca ṣaḍete nityaduḥkhitāḥ ||
english: The envious, the fastidious, the discontented, the quick to anger, the always suspicious, and the one who lives on another's fortune: these six are always unhappy.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names seven vices a king must give up, by which even well-rooted rulers are ruined (1.100-1.101).
devanagari:
सप्त दोषाः सदा राज्ञा हातव्या व्यसनोदयाः ।
प्रायशो यैर्विनश्यन्ति कृतमूलाश्च पार्थिवाः ॥
iast:
sapta doṣāḥ sadā rājñā hātavyā vyasanodayāḥ |
prāyaśo yairvinaśyanti kṛtamūlāśca pārthivāḥ ||
english: A king should always give up seven faults that give rise to calamity, by which even firmly rooted rulers are mostly destroyed:
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists the royal vices, counting women among them along with gambling, hunting, drink and harshness.
devanagari:
स्त्रियोऽक्षा मृगया पानं वाक्पारुष्यं च पञ्चमम् ।
महच्च दण्डपारुष्यमर्थदूषणमेव च ॥
iast:
striyo'kṣā mṛgayā pānaṃ vākpāruṣyaṃ ca pañcamam |
mahacca daṇḍapāruṣyamarthadūṣaṇameva ca ||
english: women, dice, hunting, drinking, harsh speech as the fifth, great harshness in punishment, and misuse of wealth.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists signs of a man headed for ruin, centred on hostility to brahmins (1.102-1.104).
devanagari:
अष्टौ पूर्वनिमित्तानि नरस्य विनशिष्यतः ।
ब्राह्मणान्प्रथमं द्वेष्टि ब्राह्मणैश्च विरुध्यते ॥
iast:
aṣṭau pūrvanimittāni narasya vinaśiṣyataḥ |
brāhmaṇānprathamaṃ dveṣṭi brāhmaṇaiśca virudhyate ||
english: There are eight signs of a man about to be destroyed: first, he hates brahmins and is at odds with brahmins;
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues the signs of ruin: seizing brahmins' property and delighting in their blame.
devanagari:
ब्राह्मण स्वानि चादत्ते ब्राह्मणांश्च जिघांसति ।
रमते निन्दया चैषां प्रशंसां नाभिनन्दति ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇa svāni cādatte brāhmaṇāṃśca jighāṃsati |
ramate nindayā caiṣāṃ praśaṃsāṃ nābhinandati ||
english: he takes brahmins' property and wishes to kill brahmins; he delights in blaming them and does not welcome their praise;
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura completes the signs of ruin and says the wise should recognise and avoid them.
devanagari:
नैतान्स्मरति कृत्येषु याचितश्चाभ्यसूयति ।
एतान्दोषान्नरः प्राज्ञो बुद्ध्या बुद्ध्वा विवर्जयेत् ॥
iast:
naitānsmarati kṛtyeṣu yācitaścābhyasūyati |
etāndoṣānnaraḥ prājño buddhyā buddhvā vivarjayet ||
english: he does not remember them in his rites, and resents them when asked. A wise person, understanding these faults, should avoid them.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura introduces eight sources of joy that are present here and now.
devanagari:
अष्टाविमानि हर्षस्य नव नीतानि भारत ।
वर्तमानानि दृश्यन्ते तान्येव सुसुखान्यपि ॥
iast:
aṣṭāvimāni harṣasya nava nītāni bhārata |
vartamānāni dṛśyante tānyeva susukhānyapi ||
english: These eight, Bharata, are the very cream of joy, seen in the present, and they are true happiness:
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists joys: meeting friends, great gain, embracing one's son and union in love.
devanagari:
समागमश्च सखिभिर्महांश्चैव धनागमः ।
पुत्रेण च परिष्वङ्गः संनिपातश्च मैथुने ॥
iast:
samāgamaśca sakhibhirmahāṃścaiva dhanāgamaḥ |
putreṇa ca pariṣvaṅgaḥ saṃnipātaśca maithune ||
english: meeting with friends, a great gain of wealth, embracing one's son, union in love-making,
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura completes the joys: kind words at the right time, standing among one's own, getting what one wants and honour in public.
devanagari:
समये च प्रियालापः स्वयूथेषु च संनतिः ।
अभिप्रेतस्य लाभश्च पूजा च जनसंसदि ॥
iast:
samaye ca priyālāpaḥ svayūtheṣu ca saṃnatiḥ |
abhipretasya lābhaśca pūjā ca janasaṃsadi ||
english: kind conversation at the right time, standing high among one's own people, gaining what one wishes, and honour in an assembly.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names eight qualities that make a person shine: wisdom, good family, self-control, learning, courage, few words, generosity and gratitude.
devanagari:
अष्टौ गुणाः पुरुषं दीपयन्ति
प्रज्ञा च कौल्यं च दमः श्रुतं च ।
पराक्रमश्चाबहुभाषिता च
दानं यथाशक्ति कृतज्ञता च ॥
iast:
aṣṭau guṇāḥ puruṣaṃ dīpayanti
prajñā ca kaulyaṃ ca damaḥ śrutaṃ ca |
parākramaścābahubhāṣitā ca
dānaṃ yathāśakti kṛtajñatā ca ||
english: Eight qualities make a person shine: wisdom, good family, self-control, learning, courage, not talking too much, giving according to one's means, and gratitude.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura describes the body as a house with nine doors, three pillars and five witnesses, presided over by the knower.
devanagari:
नवद्वारमिदं वेश्म त्रिस्थूणं पञ्च साक्षिकम् ।
क्षेत्रज्ञाधिष्ठितं विद्वान्यो वेद स परः कविः ॥
iast:
navadvāramidaṃ veśma tristhūṇaṃ pañca sākṣikam |
kṣetrajñādhiṣṭhitaṃ vidvānyo veda sa paraḥ kaviḥ ||
english: This house has nine doors, three pillars and five witnesses, and the knower of the field presides over it. The wise one who knows this is the supreme seer.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names ten who cannot see dharma: the drunk, the careless, the mad, the tired, the angry, the hungry (1.110-1.111).
devanagari:
दश धर्मं न जानन्ति धृतराष्ट्र निबोध तान् ।
मत्तः प्रमत्त उन्मत्तः श्रान्तः क्रुद्धो बुभुक्षितः ॥
iast:
daśa dharmaṃ na jānanti dhṛtarāṣṭra nibodha tān |
mattaḥ pramatta unmattaḥ śrāntaḥ kruddho bubhukṣitaḥ ||
english: Ten do not know dharma, Dhritarashtra; learn them: the drunk, the careless, the mad, the exhausted, the angry, the hungry,
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura completes the ten and advises the wise not to get caught up in these states.
devanagari:
त्वरमाणश्च भीरुश्च लुब्धः कामी च ते दश ।
तस्मादेतेषु भावेषु न प्रसज्जेत पण्डितः ॥
iast:
tvaramāṇaśca bhīruśca lubdhaḥ kāmī ca te daśa |
tasmādeteṣu bhāveṣu na prasajjeta paṇḍitaḥ ||
english: the hasty, the timid, the greedy and the lustful: these are the ten. So the wise should not get attached to these states.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura introduces an old story, sung by the demon king for his son's sake, together with Sudhanva.
devanagari:
अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
पुत्रार्थमसुरेन्द्रेण गीतं चैव सुधन्वना ॥
iast:
atraivodāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam |
putrārthamasurendreṇa gītaṃ caiva sudhanvanā ||
english: On this they cite an ancient story, sung by the lord of the asuras for his son's sake, and by Sudhanva.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the king whom everyone trusts gives up desire and anger, gives wealth to the worthy and acts quickly and knowledgeably.
devanagari:
यः काममन्यू प्रजहाति राजा
पात्रे प्रतिष्ठापयते धनं च ।
विशेषविच्छ्रुतवान्क्षिप्रकारी
तं सर्वलोकः कुरुते प्रमाणम् ॥
iast:
yaḥ kāmamanyū prajahāti rājā
pātre pratiṣṭhāpayate dhanaṃ ca |
viśeṣavicchrutavānkṣiprakārī
taṃ sarvalokaḥ kurute pramāṇam ||
english: The king who gives up desire and anger, places wealth with the worthy, discerns differences, is learned and acts quickly, is taken as an authority by all.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says full prosperity comes to one who can win people's trust, punishes only proven faults and knows measure and forgiveness.
devanagari:
जानाति विश्वासयितुं मनुष्यान्
विज्ञात दोषेषु दधाति दण्डम् ।
जानाति मात्रां च तथा क्षमां च
तं तादृशं श्रीर्जुषते समग्रा ॥
iast:
jānāti viśvāsayituṃ manuṣyān
vijñāta doṣeṣu dadhāti daṇḍam |
jānāti mātrāṃ ca tathā kṣamāṃ ca
taṃ tādṛśaṃ śrīrjuṣate samagrā ||
english: One who knows how to win people's trust, punishes only where faults are proven, and knows both measure and forgiveness: such a person full prosperity attends.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura describes the steady person: despises no one, deals wisely even with an enemy, avoids fights with the strong and acts at the right time.
devanagari:
सुदुर्बलं नावजानाति कंचिद्-
युक्तो रिपुं सेवते बुद्धिपूर्वम् ।
न विग्रहं रोचयते बलस्थैः
काले च यो विक्रमते स धीरः ॥
iast:
sudurbalaṃ nāvajānāti kaṃcid-
yukto ripuṃ sevate buddhipūrvam |
na vigrahaṃ rocayate balasthaiḥ
kāle ca yo vikramate sa dhīraḥ ||
english: One who despises no one, however weak, deals with an enemy thoughtfully and carefully, does not seek conflict with the strong, and shows courage at the right time, is steadfast.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who is not shaken in misfortune, keeps working diligently and bears pain patiently overcomes all rivals.
devanagari:
प्राप्यापदं न व्यथते कदा चिद्
उद्योगमन्विच्छति चाप्रमत्तः ।
दुःखं च काले सहते जितात्मा
धुरन्धरस्तस्य जिताः सपत्नाः ॥
iast:
prāpyāpadaṃ na vyathate kadā cid
udyogamanvicchati cāpramattaḥ |
duḥkhaṃ ca kāle sahate jitātmā
dhurandharastasya jitāḥ sapatnāḥ ||
english: One who, meeting misfortune, is never shaken, keeps seeking to act with care, and bears suffering in its season with self-mastery: that bearer of burdens has conquered his rivals.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one is always happy who avoids pointless exile, bad alliances, adultery, hypocrisy, theft, slander and drink.
devanagari:
अनर्थकं विप्र वासं गृहेभ्यः
पापैः सन्धिं परदाराभिमर्शम् ।
दम्भं स्तैन्यं पैशुनं मद्य पानं
न सेवते यः स सुखी सदैव ॥
iast:
anarthakaṃ vipra vāsaṃ gṛhebhyaḥ
pāpaiḥ sandhiṃ paradārābhimarśam |
dambhaṃ stainyaṃ paiśunaṃ madya pānaṃ
na sevate yaḥ sa sukhī sadaiva ||
english: One who does not indulge in pointless living away from home, alliances with the wicked, adultery, hypocrisy, theft, slander or drinking, is always happy.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise do not pursue wealth in a rage, speak only the truth when asked, avoid petty disputes and do not anger when unhonoured.
devanagari:
न संरम्भेणारभतेऽर्थवर्गम्
आकारितः शंसति तथ्यमेव ।
न मात्रार्थे रोचयते विवादं
नापूजितः कुप्यति चाप्यमूढः ॥
iast:
na saṃrambheṇārabhate'rthavargam
ākāritaḥ śaṃsati tathyameva |
na mātrārthe rocayate vivādaṃ
nāpūjitaḥ kupyati cāpyamūḍhaḥ ||
english: One who does not pursue wealth in haste and agitation, speaks only the truth when called upon, does not seek a quarrel over a trifle, and is not angry when not honoured, is no fool.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who is not envious, is compassionate, does not overreach, does not speak excessively and tolerates disagreement is praised everywhere.
devanagari:
न योऽभ्यसूयत्यनुकम्पते च
न दुर्बलः प्रातिभाव्यं करोति ।
नात्याह किं चित्क्षमते विवादं
सर्वत्र तादृग्लभते प्रशंसाम् ॥
iast:
na yo'bhyasūyatyanukampate ca
na durbalaḥ prātibhāvyaṃ karoti |
nātyāha kiṃ citkṣamate vivādaṃ
sarvatra tādṛglabhate praśaṃsām ||
english: One who is not envious and is compassionate, who, being weak, does not stand surety for others, does not overstate anything and tolerates disputes, wins praise everywhere.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says people love one who never dresses arrogantly, never boasts of his own valour and never speaks bitterly even when provoked.
devanagari:
यो नोद्धतं कुरुते जातु वेषं
न पौरुषेणापि विकत्थतेऽन्यान् ।
न मूर्च्छितः कटुकान्याह किं चित्
प्रियं सदा तं कुरुते जनोऽपि ॥
iast:
yo noddhataṃ kurute jātu veṣaṃ
na pauruṣeṇāpi vikatthate'nyān |
na mūrcchitaḥ kaṭukānyāha kiṃ cit
priyaṃ sadā taṃ kurute jano'pi ||
english: One who never adopts a haughty manner, does not boast of his prowess to others, and, even when beside himself, says nothing bitter, is always loved by people.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the best conduct does not rekindle settled enmity, is neither arrogant nor despondent, and does not rage over its own misfortune.
devanagari:
न वैरमुद्दीपयति प्रशान्तं
न दर्ममारोहति नास्तमेति ।
न दुर्गतोऽस्मीति करोति मन्युं
तमार्य शीलं परमाहुरग्र्यम् ॥
iast:
na vairamuddīpayati praśāntaṃ
na darmamārohati nāstameti |
na durgato'smīti karoti manyuṃ
tamārya śīlaṃ paramāhuragryam ||
english: One who does not rekindle enmity that has died down, does not climb into arrogance nor sink down, and does not turn resentful saying 'I am in a bad way': that noble conduct they call the highest.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the noble do not exult in their own happiness, rejoice in others' pain, regret their gifts or boast.
devanagari:
न स्वे सुखे वै कुरुते प्रहर्षं
नान्यस्य दुःखे भवति प्रतीतः ।
दत्त्वा न पश्चात्कुरुतेऽनुतापं
न कत्थते सत्पुरुषार्य शीलः ॥
iast:
na sve sukhe vai kurute praharṣaṃ
nānyasya duḥkhe bhavati pratītaḥ |
dattvā na paścātkurute'nutāpaṃ
na katthate satpuruṣārya śīlaḥ ||
english: One who does not exult in his own happiness, does not rejoice at another's sorrow, does not regret having given, and does not boast: that is a good person of noble conduct.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who learns the customs of regions, conventions and communities leads people wherever he goes.
devanagari:
देशाचारान्समयाञ्जातिधर्मान्
बुभूषते यस्तु परावरज्ञः ।
स तत्र तत्राधिगतः सदैव
महाजनस्याधिपत्यं करोति ॥
iast:
deśācārānsamayāñjātidharmān
bubhūṣate yastu parāvarajñaḥ |
sa tatra tatrādhigataḥ sadaiva
mahājanasyādhipatyaṃ karoti ||
english: One who knows high and low and seeks to understand the customs of regions, conventions and the duties of communities, wherever he goes, always rises to leadership of the people.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise person avoids hypocrisy, delusion, envy, wrongdoing, slander, feuds and arguments with the drunk and wicked.
devanagari:
दम्भं मोहं मत्सरं पापकृत्यं
राजद्विष्टं पैशुनं पूगवैरम् ।
मत्तोन्मत्तैर्दुर्जनैश्चापि वादं
यः प्रज्ञावान्वर्जयेत्स प्रधानः ॥
iast:
dambhaṃ mohaṃ matsaraṃ pāpakṛtyaṃ
rājadviṣṭaṃ paiśunaṃ pūgavairam |
mattonmattairdurjanaiścāpi vādaṃ
yaḥ prajñāvānvarjayetsa pradhānaḥ ||
english: The wise one who avoids hypocrisy, delusion, envy, wrong deeds, what the king hates, slander, feuds with groups, and disputes with the drunk, the mad and the wicked, is foremost.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the gods favour the rise of one who daily practises self-control, purity, worship and good rites.
devanagari:
दमं शौचं दैवतं मङ्गलानि
प्रायश्चित्तं विविधाँल्लोकवादान् ।
एतानि यः कुरुते नैत्यकानि
तस्योत्थानं देवता राधयन्ति ॥
iast:
damaṃ śaucaṃ daivataṃ maṅgalāni
prāyaścittaṃ vividhām̐llokavādān |
etāni yaḥ kurute naityakāni
tasyotthānaṃ devatā rādhayanti ||
english: One who daily practises self-control, purity, worship of the gods, auspicious rites, atonement and the various customs of the world: the gods favour that person's rise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises marriage, friendship and dealings with equals, reflecting his era's view of social rank.
devanagari:
समैर्विवाहं कुरुते न हीनैः
समैः सख्यं व्यवहारं कथाश्च ।
गुणैर्विशिष्टांश्च पुरो दधाति
विपश्चितस्तस्य नयाः सुनीताः ॥
iast:
samairvivāhaṃ kurute na hīnaiḥ
samaiḥ sakhyaṃ vyavahāraṃ kathāśca |
guṇairviśiṣṭāṃśca puro dadhāti
vipaścitastasya nayāḥ sunītāḥ ||
english: One who marries among equals and not among inferiors, who makes friends, does business and converses with equals, and puts those of superior qualities first: that wise person's policies are well guided.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says misfortunes leave one who eats moderately after sharing, sleeps little after working much, and gives even to enemies who ask.
devanagari:
मितं भुङ्क्ते संविभज्याश्रितेभ्यो
मितं स्वपित्यमितं कर्मकृत्वा ।
ददात्यमित्रेष्वपि याचितः सं-
स्तमात्मवन्तं प्रजहात्यनर्थाः ॥
iast:
mitaṃ bhuṅkte saṃvibhajyāśritebhyo
mitaṃ svapityamitaṃ karmakṛtvā |
dadātyamitreṣvapi yācitaḥ saṃ-
stamātmavantaṃ prajahātyanarthāḥ ||
english: One who eats in moderation after sharing with dependants, sleeps little after much work, and gives when asked even to enemies: misfortunes leave such a self-possessed person.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says no undertaking fails for one whose plans others do not know, whose counsel is kept and carried out well.
devanagari:
चिकीर्षितं विप्रकृतं च यस्य
नान्ये जनाः कर्म जानन्ति किं चित् ।
मन्त्रे गुप्ते सम्यगनुष्ठिते च
स्वल्पो नास्य व्यथते कश्चिदर्थः ॥
iast:
cikīrṣitaṃ viprakṛtaṃ ca yasya
nānye janāḥ karma jānanti kiṃ cit |
mantre gupte samyaganuṣṭhite ca
svalpo nāsya vyathate kaścidarthaḥ ||
english: When others know nothing of what one intends or has done, and counsel is kept secret and properly carried out, not even the smallest of one's aims miscarries.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one devoted to the peace of all beings, truthful, gentle, generous and pure, shines among kin like a fine gem.
devanagari:
यः सर्वभूतप्रशमे निविष्टः
सत्यो मृदुर्दानकृच्छुद्ध भावः ।
अतीव सञ्ज्ञायते ज्ञातिमध्ये
महामणिर्जात्य इव प्रसन्नः ॥
iast:
yaḥ sarvabhūtapraśame niviṣṭaḥ
satyo mṛdurdānakṛcchuddha bhāvaḥ |
atīva sañjñāyate jñātimadhye
mahāmaṇirjātya iva prasannaḥ ||
english: One devoted to the calm of all beings, truthful, gentle, generous and pure in heart, is highly respected among kin, like a great gem of fine origin, clear and bright.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who feels deep shame before his own conscience becomes a teacher to all, shining by his own light.
devanagari:
य आत्मनापत्रपते भृशं नरः
स सर्वलोकस्य गुरुर्भवत्युत ।
अनन्त तेजाः सुमनाः समाहितः
स्वतेजसा सूर्य इवावभासते ॥
iast:
ya ātmanāpatrapate bhṛśaṃ naraḥ
sa sarvalokasya gururbhavatyuta |
ananta tejāḥ sumanāḥ samāhitaḥ
svatejasā sūrya ivāvabhāsate ||
english: The person who feels deeply ashamed before himself becomes the teacher of all the world; of endless radiance, glad of heart and collected, he shines by his own light like the sun.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura reminds Dhritarashtra that he raised the five Pandavas, sons of Pandu, who obey him.
devanagari:
वने जाताः शापदग्धस्य राज्ञः
पाण्डोः पुत्राः पञ्च पञ्चेन्द्र कल्पाः ।
त्वयैव बाला वर्धिताः शिक्षिताश्च
तवादेशं पालयन्त्याम्बिकेय ॥
iast:
vane jātāḥ śāpadagdhasya rājñaḥ
pāṇḍoḥ putrāḥ pañca pañcendra kalpāḥ |
tvayaiva bālā vardhitāḥ śikṣitāśca
tavādeśaṃ pālayantyāmbikeya ||
english: Born in the forest to King Pandu, who was burnt by a curse, the five sons of Pandu, like five Indras, were raised and taught by you as boys, and they follow your command, son of Ambika.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura urges the king to give the Pandavas their rightful kingdom and live happily with his sons.
devanagari:
प्रदायैषामुचितं तात राज्यं
सुखी पुत्रैः सहितो मोदमानः ।
न देवानां नापि च मानुषाणां
भविष्यसि त्वं तर्कणीयो नरेन्द्र ॥
iast:
pradāyaiṣāmucitaṃ tāta rājyaṃ
sukhī putraiḥ sahito modamānaḥ |
na devānāṃ nāpi ca mānuṣāṇāṃ
bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ tarkaṇīyo narendra ||
english: Give them their due kingdom, dear one, and be happy, rejoicing with your sons. Then, lord of men, you will be blamed by neither gods nor humans.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra, still sleepless, asks Vidura again what should be done.
devanagari:
जाग्रतो दह्यमानस्य यत्कार्यमनुपश्यसि ।
तद्ब्रूहि त्वं हि नस्तात धर्मार्थकुशलः शुचिः ॥
iast:
jāgrato dahyamānasya yatkāryamanupaśyasi |
tadbrūhi tvaṃ hi nastāta dharmārthakuśalaḥ śuciḥ ||
english: Tell me what you see as needing to be done by one who lies awake, burning; for you, dear one, are skilled in dharma and worldly affairs, and pure.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura to advise him rightly about what Yudhishthira intends and what is good for the Kurus.
devanagari:
त्वं मां यथावद्विदुर प्रशाधि
प्रज्ञा पूर्वं सर्वमजातशत्रोः ।
यन्मन्यसे पथ्यमदीनसत्त्व
श्रेयः करं ब्रूहि तद्वै कुरूणाम् ॥
iast:
tvaṃ māṃ yathāvadvidura praśādhi
prajñā pūrvaṃ sarvamajātaśatroḥ |
yanmanyase pathyamadīnasattva
śreyaḥ karaṃ brūhi tadvai kurūṇām ||
english: Instruct me properly, Vidura, about everything in Ajatashatru's mind. Whatever you think beneficial, you of undaunted spirit, tell me what will bring good to the Kurus.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra admits he fears wrongdoing and sees only evil, and asks with an anxious mind.
devanagari:
पापाशङ्गी पापमेव नौपश्यन्
पृच्छामि त्वां व्याकुलेनात्मनाहम् ।
कवे तन्मे ब्रूहि सर्वं यथावन्
मनीषितं सर्वमजातशत्रोः ॥
iast:
pāpāśaṅgī pāpameva naupaśyan
pṛcchāmi tvāṃ vyākulenātmanāham |
kave tanme brūhi sarvaṃ yathāvan
manīṣitaṃ sarvamajātaśatroḥ ||
english: Fearing wrong, I see nothing but wrong; I ask you with a troubled mind. Seer, tell me everything truly that Ajatashatru intends.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one should tell someone the truth, good or bad, pleasant or not, even unasked, if one does not wish their downfall.
devanagari:
शुभं वा यदि वा पापं द्वेष्यं वा यदि वा प्रियम् ।
अपृष्टस्तस्य तद्ब्रूयाद्यस्य नेच्छेत्पराभवम् ॥
iast:
śubhaṃ vā yadi vā pāpaṃ dveṣyaṃ vā yadi vā priyam |
apṛṣṭastasya tadbrūyādyasya necchetparābhavam ||
english: Whether good or bad, hateful or pleasant, one should say it even unasked to anyone whose downfall one does not wish.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says that is why he will speak words that are good and righteous, wishing the Kurus well.
devanagari:
तस्माद्वक्ष्यामि ते राजन्भवमिच्छन्कुरून्प्रति ।
वचः श्रेयः करं धर्म्यं ब्रुवतस्तन्निबोध मे ॥
iast:
tasmādvakṣyāmi te rājanbhavamicchankurūnprati |
vacaḥ śreyaḥ karaṃ dharmyaṃ bruvatastannibodha me ||
english: So, king, wishing the Kurus well, I will speak to you words that are beneficial and righteous; listen as I speak.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns not to set one's mind on deeds done by deceit or wrong means, even if they succeed.
devanagari:
मिथ्योपेतानि कर्माणि सिध्येयुर्यानि भारत ।
अनुपाय प्रयुक्तानि मा स्म तेषु मनः कृथाः ॥
iast:
mithyopetāni karmāṇi sidhyeyuryāni bhārata |
anupāya prayuktāni mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
english: Do not set your mind on undertakings that are joined with falsehood and pursued by wrong means, Bharata, even if they might succeed.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says if a well-planned and rightly pursued action fails, the wise should not let it weigh on them.
devanagari:
तथैव योगविहितं न सिध्येत्कर्म यन्नृप ।
उपाययुक्तं मेधावी न तत्र ग्लपयेन्मनः ॥
iast:
tathaiva yogavihitaṃ na sidhyetkarma yannṛpa |
upāyayuktaṃ medhāvī na tatra glapayenmanaḥ ||
english: Likewise, king, if an undertaking pursued with the right means and proper method does not succeed, the wise should not let their mind be downcast over it.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
