context: Vidura advises considering the consequences of actions that have consequences, and acting after reflection, not in haste.
devanagari:
अनुबन्धानवेक्षेत सानुबन्धेषु कर्मसु ।
सम्प्रधार्य च कुर्वीत न वेगेन समाचरेत् ॥
iast:
anubandhānavekṣeta sānubandheṣu karmasu |
sampradhārya ca kurvīta na vegena samācaret ||
english: In actions that have consequences, one should consider the consequences; and act only after deliberation, not on impulse.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the steady person weighs the consequences and results of an action, and their own capacity, before deciding whether to act.
devanagari:
अनुबन्धं च सम्प्रेक्ष्य विपाकांश्चैव कर्मणाम् ।
उत्थानमात्मनश्चैव धीरः कुर्वीत वा न वा ॥
iast:
anubandhaṃ ca samprekṣya vipākāṃścaiva karmaṇām |
utthānamātmanaścaiva dhīraḥ kurvīta vā na vā ||
english: Considering the consequences and the results of actions, and also one's own resources, the steady person should act or not act.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a ruler who does not understand the measures of growth, decline, treasury, people and justice will not last.
devanagari:
यः प्रमाणं न जानाति स्थाने वृद्धौ तथा क्षये ।
कोशे जनपदे दण्डे न स राज्यावतिष्ठते ॥
iast:
yaḥ pramāṇaṃ na jānāti sthāne vṛddhau tathā kṣaye |
kośe janapade daṇḍe na sa rājyāvatiṣṭhate ||
english: One who does not know the right measure in stability, growth and decline, in the treasury, the countryside and punishment, does not remain in his kingdom.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who grasps these measures and knows dharma and true benefit gains the kingdom.
devanagari:
यस्त्वेतानि प्रमाणानि यथोक्तान्यनुपश्यति ।
युक्तो धर्मार्थयोर्ज्ञाने स राज्यमधिगच्छति ॥
iast:
yastvetāni pramāṇāni yathoktānyanupaśyati |
yukto dharmārthayorjñāne sa rājyamadhigacchati ||
english: But one who observes these measures as described, and is versed in knowledge of dharma and true benefit, gains the kingdom.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns that gaining power is no licence for bad behaviour; arrogance destroys fortune as age destroys beauty.
devanagari:
न राज्यं प्राप्तमित्येव वर्तितव्यमसाम्प्रतम् ।
श्रियं ह्यविनयो हन्ति जरा रूपमिवोत्तमम् ॥
iast:
na rājyaṃ prāptamityeva vartitavyamasāmpratam |
śriyaṃ hyavinayo hanti jarā rūpamivottamam ||
english: One should not behave improperly just because one has gained a kingdom. Arrogance destroys good fortune as old age destroys the finest beauty.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura gives the image of a fish that swallows a hook hidden in tasty bait without seeing the consequence.
devanagari:
भक्ष्योत्तम प्रतिच्छन्नं मत्स्यो बडिशमायसम् ।
रूपाभिपाती ग्रसते नानुबन्धमवेक्षते ॥
iast:
bhakṣyottama praticchannaṃ matsyo baḍiśamāyasam |
rūpābhipātī grasate nānubandhamavekṣate ||
english: A fish, lured by appearance, swallows an iron hook hidden in the choicest bait; it does not see what follows.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises taking only what can be swallowed, digested and is beneficial in the end.
devanagari:
यच्छक्यं ग्रसितुं ग्रस्यं ग्रस्तं परिणमेच्च यत् ।
हितं च परिणामे यत्तदद्यं भूतिमिच्छता ॥
iast:
yacchakyaṃ grasituṃ grasyaṃ grastaṃ pariṇamecca yat |
hitaṃ ca pariṇāme yattadadyaṃ bhūtimicchatā ||
english: What can be swallowed, what once swallowed can be digested, and what is beneficial when digested: that should be eaten by one who wishes to prosper.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who picks unripe fruit gets no juice and destroys the seed.
devanagari:
वनस्पतेरपक्वानि फलानि प्रचिनोति यः ।
स नाप्नोति रसं तेभ्यो बीजं चास्य विनश्यति ॥
iast:
vanaspaterapakvāni phalāni pracinoti yaḥ |
sa nāpnoti rasaṃ tebhyo bījaṃ cāsya vinaśyati ||
english: Whoever picks the unripe fruits of a tree gets no juice from them, and their seed is destroyed.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who waits for ripe fruit gets its juice and, from its seed, fruit again.
devanagari:
यस्तु पक्वमुपादत्ते काले परिणतं फलम् ।
फलाद्रसं स लभते बीजाच्चैव फलं पुनः ॥
iast:
yastu pakvamupādatte kāle pariṇataṃ phalam |
phalādrasaṃ sa labhate bījāccaiva phalaṃ punaḥ ||
english: But whoever takes the fruit when it has ripened in its time gets juice from the fruit, and from the seed, fruit again.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises taking wealth from people as a bee takes honey, without harming the flowers.
devanagari:
यथा मधु समादत्ते रक्षन्पुष्पाणि षट्पदः ।
तद्वदर्थान्मनुष्येभ्य आदद्यादविहिंसया ॥
iast:
yathā madhu samādatte rakṣanpuṣpāṇi ṣaṭpadaḥ |
tadvadarthānmanuṣyebhya ādadyādavihiṃsayā ||
english: As a bee gathers honey while protecting the flowers, so one should take wealth from people without harming them.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues: gather like a gardener picking flower by flower, not like a charcoal-burner cutting down the roots.
devanagari:
पुष्पं पुष्पं विचिन्वीत मूलच्छेदं न कारयेत् ।
मालाकार इवारामे न यथाङ्गारकारकः ॥
iast:
puṣpaṃ puṣpaṃ vicinvīta mūlacchedaṃ na kārayet |
mālākāra ivārāme na yathāṅgārakārakaḥ ||
english: Gather flower by flower and do not cut down the roots, like a gardener in a garden, not like a charcoal-burner.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says some aims are not worth undertaking, since even effort spent on them is wasted.
devanagari:
अनारभ्या भवन्त्यर्थाः के चिन्नित्यं तथागताः ।
कृतः पुरुषकारोऽपि भवेद्येषु निरर्थकः ॥
iast:
anārabhyā bhavantyarthāḥ ke cinnityaṃ tathāgatāḥ |
kṛtaḥ puruṣakāro'pi bhavedyeṣu nirarthakaḥ ||
english: Some undertakings should not be begun, as they always end the same way; even human effort spent on them is fruitless.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise quickly start projects with small costs and great returns, and do not let obstacles stop them.
devanagari:
कांश्चिदर्थान्नरः प्राज्ञो लभु मूलान्महाफलान् ।
क्षिप्रमारभते कर्तुं न विघ्नयति तादृशान् ॥
iast:
kāṃścidarthānnaraḥ prājño labhu mūlānmahāphalān |
kṣipramārabhate kartuṃ na vighnayati tādṛśān ||
english: The wise quickly begin undertakings whose roots are light and whose fruits are great, and do not let such things be obstructed.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says people love one who looks on everything honestly, as if drinking it in with the eyes, even if he sits silent.
devanagari:
ऋजु पश्यति यः सर्वं चक्षुषानुपिबन्निव ।
आसीनमपि तूष्णीकमनुरज्यन्ति तं प्रजाः ॥
iast:
ṛju paśyati yaḥ sarvaṃ cakṣuṣānupibanniva |
āsīnamapi tūṣṇīkamanurajyanti taṃ prajāḥ ||
english: People are devoted to one who looks on everything straightforwardly, as if drinking it in with the eyes, even when he sits silent.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the world is pleased with one who pleases it in four ways: by eye, mind, speech and action.
devanagari:
चक्षुषा मनसा वाचा कर्मणा च चतुर्विधम् ।
प्रसादयति लोकं यस्तं लोकोऽनुप्रसीदति ॥
iast:
cakṣuṣā manasā vācā karmaṇā ca caturvidham |
prasādayati lokaṃ yastaṃ loko'nuprasīdati ||
english: One who pleases the world in four ways, by eye, by mind, by speech and by action, the world is pleased with in return.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one whom all beings fear, as deer fear a hunter, loses even the whole earth.
devanagari:
यस्मात्त्रस्यन्ति भूतानि मृगव्याधान्मृगा इव ।
सागरान्तामपि महीं लब्ध्वा स परिहीयते ॥
iast:
yasmāttrasyanti bhūtāni mṛgavyādhānmṛgā iva |
sāgarāntāmapi mahīṃ labdhvā sa parihīyate ||
english: One whom beings fear, as deer fear the hunter, falls from power even after gaining the earth to its ocean shores.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a ruler who follows wrong policy loses even an inherited kingdom, as wind scatters a cloud.
devanagari:
पितृपैतामहं राज्यं प्राप्तवान्स्वेन तेजसा ।
वायुरभ्रमिवासाद्य भ्रंशयत्यनये स्थितः ॥
iast:
pitṛpaitāmahaṃ rājyaṃ prāptavānsvena tejasā |
vāyurabhramivāsādya bhraṃśayatyanaye sthitaḥ ||
english: Even one who has gained his ancestral kingdom by his own power loses it, if he follows wrong policy, as the wind scatters a cloud.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the earth grows rich for a king who follows dharma as the good have always done.
devanagari:
धर्ममाचरतो राज्ञः सद्भिश्चरितमादितः ।
वसुधा वसुसम्पूर्णा वर्धते भूतिवर्धनी ॥
iast:
dharmamācarato rājñaḥ sadbhiścaritamāditaḥ |
vasudhā vasusampūrṇā vardhate bhūtivardhanī ||
english: For a king who practises dharma as the good have done from the beginning, the earth, full of wealth and increasing prosperity, flourishes.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the earth shrinks from a king who abandons dharma, like leather in a fire.
devanagari:
अथ सन्त्यजतो धर्ममधर्मं चानुतिष्ठतः ।
प्रतिसंवेष्टते भूमिरग्नौ चर्माहितं यथा ॥
iast:
atha santyajato dharmamadharmaṃ cānutiṣṭhataḥ |
pratisaṃveṣṭate bhūmiragnau carmāhitaṃ yathā ||
english: But for one who abandons dharma and practises adharma, the earth shrinks up like leather placed in fire.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the effort spent on crushing an enemy's kingdom should be spent on protecting one's own.
devanagari:
य एव यत्नः क्रियते प्रर राष्ट्रावमर्दने ।
स एव यत्नः कर्तव्यः स्वराष्ट्र परिपालने ॥
iast:
ya eva yatnaḥ kriyate prara rāṣṭrāvamardane |
sa eva yatnaḥ kartavyaḥ svarāṣṭra paripālane ||
english: The same effort that is made to crush another's kingdom should be made to protect one's own.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says power gained and kept by dharma lasts, and its holder does not lose it.
devanagari:
धर्मेण राज्यं विन्देत धर्मेण परिपालयेत् ।
धर्ममूलां श्रियं प्राप्य न जहाति न हीयते ॥
iast:
dharmeṇa rājyaṃ vindeta dharmeṇa paripālayet |
dharmamūlāṃ śriyaṃ prāpya na jahāti na hīyate ||
english: One should gain a kingdom by dharma and protect it by dharma. Having gained prosperity rooted in dharma, one neither abandons it nor loses it.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises taking the essence of wisdom from anyone, even a babbling madman or a crawling child, as gold from stones.
devanagari:
अप्युन्मत्तात्प्रलपतो बालाच्च परिसर्पतः ।
सर्वतः सारमादद्यादश्मभ्य इव काञ्चनम् ॥
iast:
apyunmattātpralapato bālācca parisarpataḥ |
sarvataḥ sāramādadyādaśmabhya iva kāñcanam ||
english: One should take what is valuable from everywhere, even from the ravings of a madman or the prattle of a child, as gold from stones.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the steady person gathers wise sayings and good deeds from everywhere, like a gleaner gathering grains.
devanagari:
सुव्याहृतानि सुधियां सुकृतानि ततस्ततः ।
सञ्चिन्वन्धीर आसीत शिला हारी शिलं यथा ॥
iast:
suvyāhṛtāni sudhiyāṃ sukṛtāni tatastataḥ |
sañcinvandhīra āsīta śilā hārī śilaṃ yathā ||
english: Gathering here and there the good sayings and good deeds of the wise, the steady person should live like a gleaner gathering grains.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says cows see by smell, brahmins by the Veda, kings by spies and ordinary people by their eyes.
devanagari:
गन्धेन गावः पश्यन्ति वेदैः पश्यन्ति ब्राह्मणाः ।
चारैः पश्यन्ति राजानश्चक्षुर्भ्यामितरे जनाः ॥
iast:
gandhena gāvaḥ paśyanti vedaiḥ paśyanti brāhmaṇāḥ |
cāraiḥ paśyanti rājānaścakṣurbhyāmitare janāḥ ||
english: Cows see by smell, brahmins see by the Vedas, kings see through spies, and other people see with their eyes.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a cow that is hard to milk suffers more, while one that gives milk easily is not troubled.
devanagari:
भूयांसं लभते क्लेशं या गौर्भवति दुर्दुहा ।
अथ या सुदुहा राजन्नैव तां विनयन्त्यपि ॥
iast:
bhūyāṃsaṃ labhate kleśaṃ yā gaurbhavati durduhā |
atha yā suduhā rājannaiva tāṃ vinayantyapi ||
english: A cow that is hard to milk suffers much trouble; but one that is easy to milk, king, they do not even restrain.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says what bends without heating is not heated, and wood that bends by itself is not forced.
devanagari:
यदतप्तं प्रणमति न तत्सन्तापयन्त्यपि ।
यच्च स्वयं नतं दारु न तत्संनामयन्त्यपि ॥
iast:
yadataptaṃ praṇamati na tatsantāpayantyapi |
yacca svayaṃ nataṃ dāru na tatsaṃnāmayantyapi ||
english: What bends without being heated, they do not heat; and wood that is already bent, they do not bend.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura draws the lesson: the wise bow to those stronger than them; bowing to the stronger is bowing to Indra.
devanagari:
एतयोपमया धीरः संनमेत बलीयसे ।
इन्द्राय स प्रणमते नमते यो बलीयसे ॥
iast:
etayopamayā dhīraḥ saṃnameta balīyase |
indrāya sa praṇamate namate yo balīyase ||
english: With this comparison, the wise should bow to the stronger; one who bows to the stronger bows to Indra.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists who protects whom, including traditional gender and caste roles.
devanagari:
पर्जन्यनाथाः पशवो राजानो मित्र बान्धवाः ।
पतयो बान्धवाः स्त्रीणां ब्राह्मणा वेद बान्धवाः ॥
iast:
parjanyanāthāḥ paśavo rājāno mitra bāndhavāḥ |
patayo bāndhavāḥ strīṇāṃ brāhmaṇā veda bāndhavāḥ ||
english: Animals have the rain cloud as protector, kings have their ministers as kin, women have their husbands as kin, and brahmins have the Vedas as kin.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says dharma is guarded by truth, learning by practice, beauty by cleansing, and family by conduct.
devanagari:
सत्येन रक्ष्यते धर्मो विद्या योगेन रक्ष्यते ।
मृजया रक्ष्यते रूपं कुलं वृत्तेन रक्ष्यते ॥
iast:
satyena rakṣyate dharmo vidyā yogena rakṣyate |
mṛjayā rakṣyate rūpaṃ kulaṃ vṛttena rakṣyate ||
english: Dharma is protected by truth, learning by practice, beauty by cleanliness, and family by good conduct.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues what protects what, including a rule about women's clothing that reflects his time.
devanagari:
मानेन रक्ष्यते धान्यमश्वान्रक्ष्यत्यनुक्रमः ।
अभीक्ष्णदर्शनाद्गावः स्त्रियो रक्ष्याः कुचेलतः ॥
iast:
mānena rakṣyate dhānyamaśvānrakṣyatyanukramaḥ |
abhīkṣṇadarśanādgāvaḥ striyo rakṣyāḥ kucelataḥ ||
english: Grain is protected by measuring, horses by training, cows by frequent watching, and women are to be protected by plain clothes.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says family is no measure for one without good conduct; even among the lowest-born, conduct is what distinguishes.
devanagari:
न कुलं वृत्ति हीनस्य प्रमाणमिति मे मतिः ।
अन्त्येष्वपि हि जातानां वृत्तमेव विशिष्यते ॥
iast:
na kulaṃ vṛtti hīnasya pramāṇamiti me matiḥ |
antyeṣvapi hi jātānāṃ vṛttameva viśiṣyate ||
english: Family is no measure of one who lacks good conduct; that is my view. Even among those born lowest, conduct alone is what excels.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who envies others' wealth, looks, strength, family, happiness or honour suffers an endless disease.
devanagari:
य ईर्ष्युः परवित्तेषु रूपे वीर्ये कुलान्वये ।
सुखे सौभाग्यसत्कारे तस्य व्याधिरनन्तकः ॥
iast:
ya īrṣyuḥ paravitteṣu rūpe vīrye kulānvaye |
sukhe saubhāgyasatkāre tasya vyādhiranantakaḥ ||
english: One who envies others for their wealth, beauty, strength, family, happiness, good fortune and honour has a disease without end.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises: fearing to do wrong, to neglect duty, or to reveal plans at the wrong time, do not drink what intoxicates.
devanagari:
अकार्य करणाद्भीतः कार्याणां च विवर्जनात् ।
अकाले मन्त्रभेदाच्च येन माद्येन्न तत्पिबेत् ॥
iast:
akārya karaṇādbhītaḥ kāryāṇāṃ ca vivarjanāt |
akāle mantrabhedācca yena mādyenna tatpibet ||
english: Fearing wrong action, neglect of what should be done, and revealing counsel at the wrong time, one should not drink anything that intoxicates.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names three intoxications, of learning, wealth and family: they inflate the proud but discipline the good.
devanagari:
विद्यामदो धनमदस्तृतीयोऽभिजनो मदः ।
एते मदावलिप्तानामेत एव सतां दमाः ॥
iast:
vidyāmado dhanamadastṛtīyo'bhijano madaḥ |
ete madāvaliptānāmeta eva satāṃ damāḥ ||
english: Pride of learning, pride of wealth and, third, pride of family: these are intoxications for the arrogant, and these same things are restraints for the good.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says when the good ask the wicked for help, the wicked start thinking themselves good.
devanagari:
असन्तोऽभ्यर्थिताः सद्भिः किं चित्कार्यं कदा चन ।
मन्यन्ते सन्तमात्मानमसन्तमपि विश्रुतम् ॥
iast:
asanto'bhyarthitāḥ sadbhiḥ kiṃ citkāryaṃ kadā cana |
manyante santamātmānamasantamapi viśrutam ||
english: When the wicked are ever asked by the good for some service, they think themselves good, though known to be wicked.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the good are the refuge of the self-controlled, of the good and even of the wicked, but the wicked are no refuge for the good.
devanagari:
गतिरात्मवतां सन्तः सन्त एव सतां गतिः ।
असतां च गतिः सन्तो न त्वसन्तः सतां गतिः ॥
iast:
gatirātmavatāṃ santaḥ santa eva satāṃ gatiḥ |
asatāṃ ca gatiḥ santo na tvasantaḥ satāṃ gatiḥ ||
english: The good are the refuge of the self-possessed; the good are the refuge of the good; the good are the refuge even of the wicked; but the wicked are not the refuge of the good.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the well-dressed win the assembly, the cattle owner his wishes, the vehicle owner the road, but the person of character wins everything.
devanagari:
जिता सभा वस्त्रवता समाशा गोमता जिता ।
अध्वा जितो यानवता सर्वं शीलवता जितम् ॥
iast:
jitā sabhā vastravatā samāśā gomatā jitā |
adhvā jito yānavatā sarvaṃ śīlavatā jitam ||
english: The well-dressed win the assembly, the owner of cattle wins his desires, the owner of a vehicle wins the road; the person of good character wins everything.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says character is foremost; for one who loses it, there is no point in life, wealth or relatives.
devanagari:
शीलं प्रधानं पुरुषे तद्यस्येह प्रणश्यति ।
न तस्य जीवितेनार्थो न धनेन न बन्धुभिः ॥
iast:
śīlaṃ pradhānaṃ puruṣe tadyasyeha praṇaśyati |
na tasya jīvitenārtho na dhanena na bandhubhiḥ ||
english: Character is foremost in a person; for one who loses it here, there is no use in life, nor wealth, nor kin.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura notes that the rich eat mostly meat, the middling dairy and the poor salt.
devanagari:
आढ्यानां मांसपरमं मध्यानां गोरसोत्तरम् ।
लवणोत्तरं दरिद्राणां भोजनं भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
āḍhyānāṃ māṃsaparamaṃ madhyānāṃ gorasottaram |
lavaṇottaraṃ daridrāṇāṃ bhojanaṃ bharatarṣabha ||
english: The food of the rich is mainly meat, of the middling mainly milk products, and of the poor mainly salt, best of the Bharatas.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the poor always eat the tastiest food, for hunger gives taste, and that is rare among the rich.
devanagari:
सम्पन्नतरमेवान्नं दरिद्रा भुञ्जते सदा ।
क्षुत्स्वादुतां जनयति सा चाढ्येषु सुदुर्लभा ॥
iast:
sampannataramevānnaṃ daridrā bhuñjate sadā |
kṣutsvādutāṃ janayati sā cāḍhyeṣu sudurlabhā ||
english: The poor always eat the most delicious food, for hunger gives taste, and that is very rare among the rich.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the rich often cannot even eat, while the poor can digest wood.
devanagari:
प्रायेण श्रीमतां लोके भोक्तुं शक्तिर्न विद्यते ।
दरिद्राणां तु राजेन्द्र अपि काष्ठं हि जीर्यते ॥
iast:
prāyeṇa śrīmatāṃ loke bhoktuṃ śaktirna vidyate |
daridrāṇāṃ tu rājendra api kāṣṭhaṃ hi jīryate ||
english: Usually the wealthy in this world have no power to eat, but the poor, lord of kings, can digest even wood.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the lowest fear losing their livelihood, the middling fear death, and the best fear dishonour most.
devanagari:
अवृत्तिर्भयमन्त्यानां मध्यानां मरणाद्भयम् ।
उत्तमानां तु मर्त्यानामवमानात्परं भयम् ॥
iast:
avṛttirbhayamantyānāṃ madhyānāṃ maraṇādbhayam |
uttamānāṃ tu martyānāmavamānātparaṃ bhayam ||
english: The lowest fear having no livelihood, the middling fear death, but the best of mortals fear dishonour most of all.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the worst intoxication is pride of power, since one drunk on it does not wake until he falls.
devanagari:
ऐश्वर्यमदपापिष्ठा मदाः पानमदादयः ।
ऐश्वर्यमदमत्तो हि नापतित्वा विबुध्यते ॥
iast:
aiśvaryamadapāpiṣṭhā madāḥ pānamadādayaḥ |
aiśvaryamadamatto hi nāpatitvā vibudhyate ||
english: Of intoxications such as drink, the intoxication of power is the worst; one intoxicated by power does not come to his senses until he falls.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says people are tormented by senses running unchecked among their objects, as stars by planets.
devanagari:
इन्द्रियौरिन्द्रियार्थेषु वर्तमानैरनिग्रहैः ।
तैरयं ताप्यते लोको नक्षत्राणि ग्रहैरिव ॥
iast:
indriyaurindriyārtheṣu vartamānairanigrahaiḥ |
tairayaṃ tāpyate loko nakṣatrāṇi grahairiva ||
english: By the senses, unrestrained and running among their objects, this world is tormented, as the stars by the planets.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says misfortunes grow like the waxing moon for one conquered by the five inborn senses that wear down the self.
devanagari:
यो जितः पञ्चवर्गेण सहजेनात्म कर्शिना ।
आपदस्तस्य वर्धन्ते शुक्लपक्ष इवोडुराड् ॥
iast:
yo jitaḥ pañcavargeṇa sahajenātma karśinā |
āpadastasya vardhante śuklapakṣa ivoḍurāḍ ||
english: For one who is conquered by the five senses, inborn and wearing down the self, misfortunes grow like the moon in the bright fortnight.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who tries to master his ministers and enemies without first mastering himself falls helpless.
devanagari:
अविजित्य य आत्मानममात्यान्विजिगीषते ।
अमित्रान्वाजितामात्यः सोऽवशः परिहीयते ॥
iast:
avijitya ya ātmānamamātyānvijigīṣate |
amitrānvājitāmātyaḥ so'vaśaḥ parihīyate ||
english: One who, without conquering himself, seeks to conquer his ministers and enemies, is overcome and helpless, and falls.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who first conquers himself, as if he were a territory, then wins over ministers and enemies, does not strive in vain.
devanagari:
आत्मानमेव प्रथमं देशरूपेण यो जयेत् ।
ततोऽमात्यानमित्रांश्च न मोघं विजिगीषते ॥
iast:
ātmānameva prathamaṃ deśarūpeṇa yo jayet |
tato'mātyānamitrāṃśca na moghaṃ vijigīṣate ||
english: One who first conquers himself, as one conquers a country, and then his ministers and enemies, does not seek victory in vain.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says fortune stays with one who controls his senses and ministers, punishes wrongdoers, acts after examination and is steady.
devanagari:
वश्येन्द्रियं जितामात्यं धृतदण्डं विकारिषु ।
परीक्ष्य कारिणं धीरमत्यन्तं श्रीर्निषेवते ॥
iast:
vaśyendriyaṃ jitāmātyaṃ dhṛtadaṇḍaṃ vikāriṣu |
parīkṣya kāriṇaṃ dhīramatyantaṃ śrīrniṣevate ||
english: Fortune serves to the utmost one who has controlled his senses and his ministers, holds the rod over wrongdoers, acts after examination, and is steady.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura gives the image of the body as a chariot, the self as charioteer and the senses as horses (compare Katha 1.3.3).
devanagari:
रथः शरीरं पुरुषस्य राजन्
नात्मा नियन्तेन्द्रियाण्यस्य चाश्वाः ।
तैरप्रमत्तः कुशलः सदश्वैर्
दान्तैः सुखं याति रथीव धीरः ॥
iast:
rathaḥ śarīraṃ puruṣasya rājan
nātmā niyantendriyāṇyasya cāśvāḥ |
tairapramattaḥ kuśalaḥ sadaśvair
dāntaiḥ sukhaṃ yāti rathīva dhīraḥ ||
english: The body is a person's chariot, king, the self is the driver, and the senses are its horses. The skilled and watchful steady person travels happily with them, like a charioteer with good, trained horses.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says uncontrolled senses can even destroy a person, as untamed horses wreck a bad driver on the road.
devanagari:
एतान्यनिगृहीतानि व्यापादयितुमप्यलम् ।
अविधेया इवादान्ता हयाः पथि कुसारथिम् ॥
iast:
etānyanigṛhītāni vyāpādayitumapyalam |
avidheyā ivādāntā hayāḥ pathi kusārathim ||
english: If not held in check, these can even destroy a person, as unruly, untamed horses destroy a poor charioteer on the road.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a fool led by the senses sees harm as good and good as harm, and takes great pain for pleasure.
devanagari:
अनर्थमर्थतः पश्यन्नर्तं चैवाप्यनर्थतः ।
इन्द्रियैः प्रसृतो बालः सुदुःखं मन्यते सुखम् ॥
iast:
anarthamarthataḥ paśyannartaṃ caivāpyanarthataḥ |
indriyaiḥ prasṛto bālaḥ suduḥkhaṃ manyate sukham ||
english: Seeing harm as good and good as harm, the immature person, carried away by the senses, thinks great pain is pleasure.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who abandons dharma and real benefit to follow the senses quickly loses fortune, life, wealth and family.
devanagari:
धर्मार्थौ यः परित्यज्य स्यादिन्द्रियवशानुगः ।
श्रीप्राणधनदारेभ्य क्षिप्रं स परिहीयते ॥
iast:
dharmārthau yaḥ parityajya syādindriyavaśānugaḥ |
śrīprāṇadhanadārebhya kṣipraṃ sa parihīyate ||
english: One who abandons dharma and true benefit and follows the lead of the senses quickly loses fortune, life, wealth and spouse.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who masters wealth but not his senses falls from power because of that lack.
devanagari:
अर्थानामीश्वरो यः स्यादिन्द्रियाणामनीश्वरः ।
इन्द्रियाणामनैश्वर्यादैश्वर्याद्भ्रश्यते हि सः ॥
iast:
arthānāmīśvaro yaḥ syādindriyāṇāmanīśvaraḥ |
indriyāṇāmanaiśvaryādaiśvaryādbhraśyate hi saḥ ||
english: One who is master of wealth but not master of the senses falls from mastery because of not mastering the senses.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one should seek oneself through oneself, with mind, intellect and senses restrained; the self is one's own friend and enemy (compare Gita 6.5).
devanagari:
आत्मनात्मानमन्विच्छेन्मनो बुद्धीन्द्रियैर्यतैः ।
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
iast:
ātmanātmānamanvicchenmano buddhīndriyairyataiḥ |
ātmaiva hyātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
english: One should seek the self by the self, with mind, intellect and senses restrained; for the self alone is the self's friend, and the self alone is the self's enemy.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says desire and anger catch a person's wisdom like a fine-meshed net catches two fish.
devanagari:
क्षुद्राक्षेणेव जालेन झषावपिहितावुभौ ।
कामश्च राजन्क्रोधश्च तौ प्राज्ञानं विलुम्पतः ॥
iast:
kṣudrākṣeṇeva jālena jhaṣāvapihitāvubhau |
kāmaśca rājankrodhaśca tau prājñānaṃ vilumpataḥ ||
english: Like two large fish caught in a fine-meshed net, desire and anger, king, rob a person of wisdom.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who gathers resources with dharma and true benefit in view grows in happiness.
devanagari:
समवेक्ष्येह धर्मार्थौ सम्भारान्योऽधिगच्छति ।
स वै सम्भृत सम्भारः सततं सुखमेधते ॥
iast:
samavekṣyeha dharmārthau sambhārānyo'dhigacchati |
sa vai sambhṛta sambhāraḥ satataṃ sukhamedhate ||
english: One who gathers what is needed while keeping dharma and true benefit in view, having gathered well, always grows in happiness.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who tries to defeat outer enemies without conquering the five inner enemies that destroy judgement is overcome by them.
devanagari:
यः पञ्चाभ्यन्तराञ्शत्रूनविजित्य मतिक्षयान् ।
जिगीषति रिपूनन्यान्रिपवोऽभिभवन्ति तम् ॥
iast:
yaḥ pañcābhyantarāñśatrūnavijitya matikṣayān |
jigīṣati ripūnanyānripavo'bhibhavanti tam ||
english: One who, without conquering the five inner enemies that destroy judgement, seeks to conquer other enemies, is overcome by those enemies.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wicked are seen to be destroyed by their own deeds, and kings by losing their kingdoms through lack of self-control.
devanagari:
दृश्यन्ते हि दुरात्मानो वध्यमानाः स्वकर्म भिः ।
इन्द्रियाणामनीशत्वाद्राजानो राज्यविभ्रमैः ॥
iast:
dṛśyante hi durātmāno vadhyamānāḥ svakarma bhiḥ |
indriyāṇāmanīśatvādrājāno rājyavibhramaiḥ ||
english: The wicked are seen being destroyed by their own deeds, and kings by the loss of their kingdoms, through not being masters of their senses.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns that through association, punishment falls on the innocent too, so one should not ally with wrongdoers.
devanagari:
असन्त्यागात्पापकृतामपापांस्
तुल्यो दण्डः स्पृशते मिश्रभावात् ।
शुष्केणार्द्रं दह्यते मिश्रभावात्
तस्मात्पापैः सह सन्धिं न कुर्यात् ॥
iast:
asantyāgātpāpakṛtāmapāpāṃs
tulyo daṇḍaḥ spṛśate miśrabhāvāt |
śuṣkeṇārdraṃ dahyate miśrabhāvāt
tasmātpāpaiḥ saha sandhiṃ na kuryāt ||
english: By not separating from wrongdoers, the innocent receive the same punishment through association; dry wood burns the green when they are mixed. So one should not make alliance with the wicked.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says misfortune swallows one who, deluded, does not restrain the five inner enemies with their five aims.
devanagari:
निजानुत्पततः शत्रून्पञ्च पञ्च प्रयोजनान् ।
यो मोहान्न निघृह्णाति तमापद्ग्रसते नरम् ॥
iast:
nijānutpatataḥ śatrūnpañca pañca prayojanān |
yo mohānna nighṛhṇāti tamāpadgrasate naram ||
english: One who, through delusion, does not restrain the five enemies rising within, each with its five aims, is swallowed by misfortune.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists virtues not found in the wicked: freedom from envy, straightforwardness, purity, contentment, kind speech, self-control, truth and calm.
devanagari:
अनसूयार्जवं शौचं सन्तोषः प्रियवादिता ।
दमः सत्यमनायासो न भवन्ति दुरात्मनाम् ॥
iast:
anasūyārjavaṃ śaucaṃ santoṣaḥ priyavāditā |
damaḥ satyamanāyāso na bhavanti durātmanām ||
english: Freedom from envy, straightforwardness, purity, contentment, kind speech, self-control, truthfulness and freedom from strain are not found in the wicked.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists virtues he says are absent among the lowest-born, reflecting caste prejudice of his time.
devanagari:
आत्मज्ञानमनायासस्तितिक्षा धर्मनित्यता ।
वाक्चैव गुप्ता दानं च नैतान्यन्त्येषु भारत ॥
iast:
ātmajñānamanāyāsastitikṣā dharmanityatā |
vākcaiva guptā dānaṃ ca naitānyantyeṣu bhārata ||
english: Self-knowledge, calm, endurance, constancy in dharma, guarded speech and generosity: these are not found among the lowest, Bharata.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the foolish hurt the wise with abuse and slander, but the slanderer takes on the sin while the one who forgives is freed.
devanagari:
आक्रोश परिवादाभ्यां विहिंसन्त्यबुधा बुधान् ।
वक्ता पापमुपादत्ते क्षममाणो विमुच्यते ॥
iast:
ākrośa parivādābhyāṃ vihiṃsantyabudhā budhān |
vaktā pāpamupādatte kṣamamāṇo vimucyate ||
english: The foolish hurt the wise with abuse and slander; the speaker takes on the sin, and the one who forgives is released.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names each group's strength, including a gendered claim about women.
devanagari:
हिंसा बलमसाधूनां राज्ञां दण्डविधिर्बलम् ।
शुश्रूषा तु बलं स्त्रीणां क्षमागुणवतां बलम् ॥
iast:
hiṃsā balamasādhūnāṃ rājñāṃ daṇḍavidhirbalam |
śuśrūṣā tu balaṃ strīṇāṃ kṣamāguṇavatāṃ balam ||
english: Violence is the strength of the wicked; punishment is the strength of kings; service is the strength of women; forgiveness is the strength of the virtuous.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says restraint of speech is the hardest of all, and one cannot speak much that is both meaningful and fresh.
devanagari:
वाक्संयमो हि नृपते सुदुष्करतमो मतः ।
अर्थवच्च विचित्रं च न शक्यं बहुभाषितुम् ॥
iast:
vāksaṃyamo hi nṛpate suduṣkaratamo mataḥ |
arthavacca vicitraṃ ca na śakyaṃ bahubhāṣitum ||
english: Restraint of speech, king, is held to be the hardest of all; and one cannot speak much that is both meaningful and striking.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says well-spoken words bring many blessings, while the same words badly spoken bring harm.
devanagari:
अभ्यावहति कल्याणं विविधा वाक्सुभाषिता ।
सैव दुर्भाषिता राजन्ननर्थायोपपद्यते ॥
iast:
abhyāvahati kalyāṇaṃ vividhā vāksubhāṣitā |
saiva durbhāṣitā rājannanarthāyopapadyate ||
english: Speech well spoken in its many forms brings good fortune; the same speech, badly spoken, king, leads to harm.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a forest cut by an axe or pierced by arrows grows back, but a wound from cruel words never heals.
devanagari:
संरोहति शरैर्विद्धं वनं परशुना हतम् ।
वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम् ॥
iast:
saṃrohati śarairviddhaṃ vanaṃ paraśunā hatam |
vācā duruktaṃ bībhatsaṃ na saṃrohati vākkṣatam ||
english: A forest pierced by arrows or cut down by an axe grows again; but a wound from ugly, harsh words does not heal.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says arrows can be pulled out of the body, but the barb of a word cannot, for it lodges in the heart.
devanagari:
कर्णिनालीकनाराचा निर्हरन्ति शरीरतः ।
वाक्षल्यस्तु न निर्हर्तुं शक्यो हृदि शयो हि सः ॥
iast:
karṇinālīkanārācā nirharanti śarīrataḥ |
vākṣalyastu na nirhartuṃ śakyo hṛdi śayo hi saḥ ||
english: Barbed arrows, darts and spears can be drawn out of the body; but the dart of a word cannot be drawn out, for it lies in the heart.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says arrow-like words fly from the mouth and leave their target grieving day and night, so the wise do not shoot them at others.
devanagari:
वाक्सायका वदनान्निष्पतन्ति
यैराहतः शोचति रत्र्यहानि ।
परस्य नामर्मसु ते पतन्ति
तान्पण्डितो नावसृजेत्परेषु ॥
iast:
vāksāyakā vadanānniṣpatanti
yairāhataḥ śocati ratryahāni |
parasya nāmarmasu te patanti
tānpaṇḍito nāvasṛjetpareṣu ||
english: Arrows of words fly from the mouth; struck by them, a person grieves night and day. They strike nowhere but in another's vital spots, so the wise should not loose them at others.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says when the gods intend someone's downfall, they first take away his judgement, so he sees things wrongly.
devanagari:
यस्मै देवाः प्रयच्छन्ति पुरुषाय पराभवम् ।
बुद्धिं तस्यापकर्षन्ति सोऽपाचीनानि पश्यति ॥
iast:
yasmai devāḥ prayacchanti puruṣāya parābhavam |
buddhiṃ tasyāpakarṣanti so'pācīnāni paśyati ||
english: When the gods intend defeat for a person, they first take away his understanding, and he sees things the wrong way round.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says when understanding is clouded and ruin is near, bad policy that looks like good policy stays fixed in the heart.
devanagari:
बुद्धौ कलुष भूतायां विनाशे प्रत्युपस्थिते ।
अनयो नयसङ्काशो हृदयान्नापसर्पति ॥
iast:
buddhau kaluṣa bhūtāyāṃ vināśe pratyupasthite |
anayo nayasaṅkāśo hṛdayānnāpasarpati ||
english: When understanding is clouded and destruction is at hand, wrong policy that looks like right policy does not leave the heart.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura tells Dhritarashtra that his judgement, and his sons', is clouded by hostility to the Pandavas, and he does not see it.
devanagari:
सेयं बुद्धिः परीता ते पुत्राणां तव भारत ।
पाण्डवानां विरोधेन न चैनाम् अवबुध्यसे ॥
iast:
seyaṃ buddhiḥ parītā te putrāṇāṃ tava bhārata |
pāṇḍavānāṃ virodhena na cainām avabudhyase ||
english: This clouded understanding has gripped your sons, Bharata, through their hostility to the Pandavas, and you do not recognise it.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura urges that Yudhishthira, fit to rule the three worlds, be the one to govern.
devanagari:
राजा लक्षणसम्पन्नस्त्रैलोक्यस्यापि यो भवेत् ।
शिष्यस्ते शासिता सोऽस्तु धृतराष्ट्र युधिष्ठिरः ॥
iast:
rājā lakṣaṇasampannastrailokyasyāpi yo bhavet |
śiṣyaste śāsitā so'stu dhṛtarāṣṭra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ||
english: Yudhishthira, who has every mark of a king and could rule even the three worlds, is your disciple, Dhritarashtra: let him be the ruler.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura praises Yudhishthira as surpassing all of Dhritarashtra's sons in fortune, energy, wisdom and knowledge of dharma.
devanagari:
अतीव सर्वान्पुत्रांस्ते भागधेय पुरस्कृतः ।
तेजसा प्रज्ञया चैव युक्तो धर्मार्थतत्त्ववित् ॥
iast:
atīva sarvānputrāṃste bhāgadheya puraskṛtaḥ |
tejasā prajñayā caiva yukto dharmārthatattvavit ||
english: Favoured by fortune, he far surpasses all your sons, endowed with energy and wisdom, knowing the truth of dharma and of true benefit.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says Yudhishthira bears many hardships out of gentleness, compassion and respect for the king.
devanagari:
आनृशंस्यादनुक्रोशाद्योऽसौ धर्मभृतां वरः ।
गौरवात्तव राजेन्द्र बहून्क्लेशांस्तितिक्षति ॥
iast:
ānṛśaṃsyādanukrośādyo'sau dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ |
gauravāttava rājendra bahūnkleśāṃstitikṣati ||
english: Out of gentleness and compassion, that best of upholders of dharma bears many hardships, lord of kings, out of respect for you.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura to say more that joins dharma and true benefit, since he never tires of hearing it.
devanagari:
ब्रूहि भूयो महाबुद्धे धर्मार्थसहितं वचः ।
शृण्वतो नास्ति मे तृप्तिर्विचित्राणीह भाषसे ॥
iast:
brūhi bhūyo mahābuddhe dharmārthasahitaṃ vacaḥ |
śṛṇvato nāsti me tṛptirvicitrāṇīha bhāṣase ||
english: Speak again, very wise one, words joined with dharma and true benefit. I am never satisfied hearing you; you say wonderful things.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says straightforwardness towards all beings is equal to, or better than, bathing at every holy place.
devanagari:
सर्वतीर्थेषु वा स्नानं सर्वभूतेषु चार्जवम् ।
उभे एते समे स्यातामार्जवं वा विशिष्यते ॥
iast:
sarvatīrtheṣu vā snānaṃ sarvabhūteṣu cārjavam |
ubhe ete same syātāmārjavaṃ vā viśiṣyate ||
english: Bathing at all the holy places, and straightforwardness towards all beings: these two may be equal, or straightforwardness may be greater.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura urges the king to be straightforward with his sons always, for fame here and heaven hereafter.
devanagari:
आर्जवं प्रतिपद्यस्व पुत्रेषु सततं विभो ।
इह कीर्तिं परां प्राप्य प्रेत्य स्वर्गमवाप्स्यसि ॥
iast:
ārjavaṃ pratipadyasva putreṣu satataṃ vibho |
iha kīrtiṃ parāṃ prāpya pretya svargamavāpsyasi ||
english: Practise straightforwardness towards your sons always, lord. Gaining the highest fame here, you will reach heaven after death.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a person is honoured in heaven as long as their good name is sung in the worlds.
devanagari:
यावत्कीर्तिर्मनुष्यस्य पुण्या लोकेषु गीयते ।
तावत्स पुरुषव्याघ्र स्वर्गलोके महीयते ॥
iast:
yāvatkīrtirmanuṣyasya puṇyā lokeṣu gīyate |
tāvatsa puruṣavyāghra svargaloke mahīyate ||
english: As long as a person's holy fame is sung in the worlds, so long, tiger among men, is that person honoured in heaven.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura introduces an old story: the dispute between Virochana and Sudhanva over Keshini (3.5-3.31).
devanagari:
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
विरोचनस्य संवादं केशिन्यर्थे सुधन्वना ॥
iast:
atrāpyudāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam |
virocanasya saṃvādaṃ keśinyarthe sudhanvanā ||
english: Here too they cite this ancient story, the dialogue of Virochana with Sudhanva for the sake of Keshini.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Keshini
context: In the story, the maiden Keshini asks Virochana whether brahmins or the sons of Diti are better.
devanagari:
किं ब्राह्मणाः स्विच्छ्रेयांसो दितिजाः स्विद्विरोचन ।
अथ केन स्म पर्यङ्कं सुधन्वा नाधिरोहति ॥
iast:
kiṃ brāhmaṇāḥ svicchreyāṃso ditijāḥ svidvirocana |
atha kena sma paryaṅkaṃ sudhanvā nādhirohati ||
english: Are brahmins better, Virochana, or the sons of Diti? And why does Sudhanva not sit on the couch?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Virochana
context: In the story, Virochana boasts that his people, descendants of Prajapati, are the best and own the worlds.
devanagari:
प्राजापत्या हि वै श्रेष्ठा वयं केशिनि सत्तमाः ।
अस्माकं खल्विमे लोकाः के देवाः के द्विजातयः ॥
iast:
prājāpatyā hi vai śreṣṭhā vayaṃ keśini sattamāḥ |
asmākaṃ khalvime lokāḥ ke devāḥ ke dvijātayaḥ ||
english: We, descendants of Prajapati, are the best, Keshini, the finest of all. These worlds are ours: who are the gods, who are the twice-born?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Keshini
context: In the story, Keshini proposes they wait for Sudhanva, who will come in the morning, to see the two meet.
devanagari:
इहैवास्स्व प्रतीक्षाव उपस्थाने विरोचन ।
सुधन्वा प्रातरागन्ता पश्येयं वां समागतौ ॥
iast:
ihaivāssva pratīkṣāva upasthāne virocana |
sudhanvā prātarāgantā paśyeyaṃ vāṃ samāgatau ||
english: Stay right here, Virochana; let us wait in this hall. Sudhanva will come in the morning, and I shall see you both together.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Virochana
context: In the story, Virochana agrees to Keshini's proposal.
devanagari:
तथा भद्रे करिष्यामि यथा त्वं भीरु भाषसे ।
सुधन्वानं च मां चैव प्रातर्द्रष्टासि सङ्गतौ ॥
iast:
tathā bhadre kariṣyāmi yathā tvaṃ bhīru bhāṣase |
sudhanvānaṃ ca māṃ caiva prātardraṣṭāsi saṅgatau ||
english: I will do as you say, gentle and timid one. In the morning you will see Sudhanva and me together.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva refuses to share a golden seat with Virochana, claiming higher rank.
devanagari:
अन्वालभे हिरण्मयं प्राह्रादेऽहं तवासनम् ।
एकत्वमुपसम्पन्नो न त्वासेयं त्वया सह ॥
iast:
anvālabhe hiraṇmayaṃ prāhrāde'haṃ tavāsanam |
ekatvamupasampanno na tvāseyaṃ tvayā saha ||
english: I touch your golden seat, son of Prahlada, but I have not come to equality with you; I will not sit with you.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Virochana
context: In the story, Virochana offers Sudhanva only a plank or a mat, saying he is not fit to sit as an equal.
devanagari:
अन्वाहरन्तु फलकं कूर्चं वाप्यथ वा बृसीम् ।
सुधन्वन्न त्वमर्होऽसि मया सह समासनम् ॥
iast:
anvāharantu phalakaṃ kūrcaṃ vāpyatha vā bṛsīm |
sudhanvanna tvamarho'si mayā saha samāsanam ||
english: Let them bring a plank, a grass seat or a mat. Sudhanva, you are not fit to share a seat with me.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva retorts that even Virochana's father would sit below him, calling Virochana a pampered child.
devanagari:
पितापि ते समासीनमुपासीतैव मामधः ।
बालः सुखैधितो गेहे न त्वं किं चन बुध्यसे ॥
iast:
pitāpi te samāsīnamupāsītaiva māmadhaḥ |
bālaḥ sukhaidhito gehe na tvaṃ kiṃ cana budhyase ||
english: Even your father would sit below me when I sit as an equal. You are a child, raised in comfort at home; you understand nothing.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Virochana
context: In the story, Virochana proposes wagering all the demons' gold and cattle on the question, to be put to those who know.
devanagari:
हिरण्यं च गवाश्वं च यद्वित्तमसुरेषु नः ।
सुधन्वन्विपणे तेन प्रश्नं पृच्छाव ये विदुः ॥
iast:
hiraṇyaṃ ca gavāśvaṃ ca yadvittamasureṣu naḥ |
sudhanvanvipaṇe tena praśnaṃ pṛcchāva ye viduḥ ||
english: The gold, cows and horses, all the wealth we demons have: with that as the wager, Sudhanva, let us put the question to those who know.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva instead proposes wagering their lives.
devanagari:
हिरण्यं च गवाश्वं च तवैवास्तु विरोचन ।
प्राणयोस्तु पणं कृत्वा प्रश्नं पृच्छाव ये विदुः ॥
iast:
hiraṇyaṃ ca gavāśvaṃ ca tavaivāstu virocana |
prāṇayostu paṇaṃ kṛtvā praśnaṃ pṛcchāva ye viduḥ ||
english: Keep your gold, cows and horses, Virochana. Let us stake our lives instead, and put the question to those who know.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Virochana
context: In the story, Virochana asks whom they will go to with their lives at stake, since he will not stand before gods or men.
devanagari:
आवां कुत्र गमिष्यावः प्राणयोर्विपणे कृते ।
न हि देवेष्वहं स्थाता न मनुष्येषु कर्हि चित् ॥
iast:
āvāṃ kutra gamiṣyāvaḥ prāṇayorvipaṇe kṛte |
na hi deveṣvahaṃ sthātā na manuṣyeṣu karhi cit ||
english: With our lives wagered, where shall we go? I will never stand before the gods, nor ever before men.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva proposes going to Virochana's own father, Prahlada, who would not lie even for his son.
devanagari:
पितरं ते गमिष्यावः प्राणयोर्विपणे कृते ।
पुत्रस्यापि स हेतोर्हि प्रह्रादो नानृतं वदेत् ॥
iast:
pitaraṃ te gamiṣyāvaḥ prāṇayorvipaṇe kṛte |
putrasyāpi sa hetorhi prahrādo nānṛtaṃ vadet ||
english: With our lives wagered, we shall go to your father; for Prahlada would not speak an untruth even for his son's sake.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Prahlada
context: In the story, Prahlada sees the two coming together like angry snakes.
devanagari:
इमौ तौ सम्प्रदृश्येते याभ्यां न चरितं सह ।
आशीविषाविव क्रुद्धावेकमार्गमिहागतौ ॥
iast:
imau tau sampradṛśyete yābhyāṃ na caritaṃ saha |
āśīviṣāviva kruddhāvekamārgamihāgatau ||
english: Here are these two, who have never gone about together, coming along one road like two angry poisonous snakes.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Prahlada
context: In the story, Prahlada asks Virochana whether he is now friends with Sudhanva.
devanagari:
किं वै सहैव चरतो न पुरा चरतः सह ।
विरोचनैतत्पृच्छामि किं ते सख्यं सुधन्वना ॥
iast:
kiṃ vai sahaiva carato na purā carataḥ saha |
virocanaitatpṛcchāmi kiṃ te sakhyaṃ sudhanvanā ||
english: Why do you now go about together, who never went together before? I ask you this, Virochana: is there friendship between you and Sudhanva?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Virochana
context: In the story, Virochana says they have staked their lives, and asks his father not to answer falsely.
devanagari:
न मे सुधन्वना सख्यं प्राणयोर्विपणावहे ।
प्रह्राद तत्त्वामृप्च्छामि मा प्रश्नमनृतं वदीः ॥
iast:
na me sudhanvanā sakhyaṃ prāṇayorvipaṇāvahe |
prahrāda tattvāmṛpcchāmi mā praśnamanṛtaṃ vadīḥ ||
english: There is no friendship between Sudhanva and me; we have staked our lives. I ask you the question, Prahlada: do not answer untruly.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Prahlada
context: In the story, Prahlada orders the customary welcome for the brahmin Sudhanva.
devanagari:
उदकं मधुपर्कं चाप्यानयन्तु सुधन्वने ।
ब्रह्मन्नभ्यर्चनीयोऽसि श्वेता गौः पीवरी कृता ॥
iast:
udakaṃ madhuparkaṃ cāpyānayantu sudhanvane |
brahmannabhyarcanīyo'si śvetā gauḥ pīvarī kṛtā ||
english: Let water and honey-drink be brought for Sudhanva. You are worthy of honour, brahmin; a fat white cow has been readied.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva says he has already been welcomed and asks Prahlada to answer truly.
devanagari:
उदकं मधुपर्कं च पथ एवार्पितं मम ।
प्रह्राद त्वं तु नौ प्रश्नं तथ्यं प्रब्रूहि पृच्छतोः ॥
iast:
udakaṃ madhuparkaṃ ca patha evārpitaṃ mama |
prahrāda tvaṃ tu nau praśnaṃ tathyaṃ prabrūhi pṛcchatoḥ ||
english: Water and honey-drink were offered to me on the way. But you, Prahlada, tell us truly the answer to our question.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Prahlada
context: In the story, Prahlada asks how a judge should decide between his own son and another who dispute.
devanagari:
पुर्तो वान्यो भवान्ब्रह्मन्साक्ष्ये चैव भवेत्स्थितः ।
तयोर्विवदतोः प्रश्नं कथमस्मद्विभो वदेत् ॥
iast:
purto vānyo bhavānbrahmansākṣye caiva bhavetsthitaḥ |
tayorvivadatoḥ praśnaṃ kathamasmadvibho vadet ||
english: Between a son and another, brahmin, if one stands as witness, how should one like me give the answer when the two dispute?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Prahlada
context: In the story, Prahlada asks what becomes of one who gives a false answer, or none at all.
devanagari:
अथ यो नैव प्रब्रूयात्सत्यं वा यदि वानृतम् ।
एतत्सुधन्वन्पृच्छामि दुर्विवक्ता स्म किं वसेत् ॥
iast:
atha yo naiva prabrūyātsatyaṃ vā yadi vānṛtam |
etatsudhanvanpṛcchāmi durvivaktā sma kiṃ vaset ||
english: And one who answers neither truly nor falsely: I ask you this, Sudhanva, how does such a bad judge fare?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva says a false judge spends nights like those of a supplanted wife, a ruined gambler or an overloaded porter.
devanagari:
यां रात्रिमधिविन्ना स्त्री यां चैवाक्ष पराजितः ।
यां च भाराभितप्ताङ्गो दुर्विवक्ता स्म तां वसेत् ॥
iast:
yāṃ rātrimadhivinnā strī yāṃ caivākṣa parājitaḥ |
yāṃ ca bhārābhitaptāṅgo durvivaktā sma tāṃ vaset ||
english: The night a wife spends when another wife has been taken, the night a man spends defeated at dice, the night of one whose body aches under a load: such a night the false judge spends,
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva continues: or like one shut out of the city, hungry at the gate, surrounded by enemies.
devanagari:
नगरे प्रतिरुद्धः सन्बहिर्द्वारे बुभुक्षितः ।
अमित्रान्भूयसः पश्यन्दुर्विवक्ता स्म तां वसेत् ॥
iast:
nagare pratiruddhaḥ sanbahirdvāre bubhukṣitaḥ |
amitrānbhūyasaḥ paśyandurvivaktā sma tāṃ vaset ||
english: shut out of the city, hungry at the outer gate, seeing many enemies around: such a night the false judge spends.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva says lying about animals or people destroys many generations (an old idiom of grave harm).
devanagari:
पञ्च पश्वनृते हन्ति दश हन्ति गवानृते ।
शतमश्वानृते हन्ति सहस्रं पुरुषानृते ॥
iast:
pañca paśvanṛte hanti daśa hanti gavānṛte |
śatamaśvānṛte hanti sahasraṃ puruṣānṛte ||
english: A lie about cattle destroys five; a lie about cows destroys ten; a lie about horses destroys a hundred; a lie about people destroys a thousand.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva says lying for gold destroys those born and unborn, and lying about land destroys everything.
devanagari:
हन्ति जातानजातांश्च हिरण्यार्थोऽनृतं वदन् ।
सर्वं भूम्यनृते हन्ति मा स्म भूम्यनृतं वदीः ॥
iast:
hanti jātānajātāṃśca hiraṇyārtho'nṛtaṃ vadan |
sarvaṃ bhūmyanṛte hanti mā sma bhūmyanṛtaṃ vadīḥ ||
english: One who lies for gold destroys those born and unborn; one who lies about land destroys everything. Never tell a lie about land.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Prahlada
context: In the story, Prahlada judges against his own son, ranking Sudhanva's lineage and mother above his.
devanagari:
मत्तः श्रेयानङ्गिरा वै सुधन्वा त्वद्विरोचन ।
मातास्य श्रेयसी मातुस्तस्मात्त्वं तेन वै जितः ॥
iast:
mattaḥ śreyānaṅgirā vai sudhanvā tvadvirocana |
mātāsya śreyasī mātustasmāttvaṃ tena vai jitaḥ ||
english: Angiras is better than I am, and Sudhanva is better than you, Virochana. His mother is better than your mother; so you have been defeated by him.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Prahlada
context: In the story, Prahlada tells Virochana that Sudhanva now owns his life, and asks Sudhanva to return his son.
devanagari:
विरोचन सुधन्वायं प्राणानामीश्वरस्तव ।
सुधन्वन्पुनरिच्छामि त्वया दत्तं विरोचनम् ॥
iast:
virocana sudhanvāyaṃ prāṇānāmīśvarastava |
sudhanvanpunaricchāmi tvayā dattaṃ virocanam ||
english: Virochana, this Sudhanva is now master of your life. Sudhanva, I would have Virochana given back to me by you.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva returns Prahlada's son because Prahlada chose dharma and would not lie out of love.
devanagari:
यद्धर्ममवृणीथास्त्वं न कामादनृतं वदीः ।
पुनर्ददामि ते तस्मात्पुत्रं प्रह्राद दुर्लभम् ॥
iast:
yaddharmamavṛṇīthāstvaṃ na kāmādanṛtaṃ vadīḥ |
punardadāmi te tasmātputraṃ prahrāda durlabham ||
english: Because you chose dharma and did not speak falsely out of desire, I give you back your son, Prahlada, so hard to find again.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Sudhanva
context: In the story, Sudhanva returns Virochana on condition he wash Sudhanva's feet before the maiden.
devanagari:
एष प्रह्राद पुत्रस्ते मया दत्तो विरोचनः ।
पादप्रक्षालनं कुर्यात्कुमार्याः संनिधौ मम ॥
iast:
eṣa prahrāda putraste mayā datto virocanaḥ |
pādaprakṣālanaṃ kuryātkumāryāḥ saṃnidhau mama ||
english: Here is your son Virochana, Prahlada, given back by me. But let him wash my feet in the presence of the maiden.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura draws the lesson for Dhritarashtra: do not lie for the sake of land, or he and his sons will come to ruin.
devanagari:
तस्माद्राजेन्द्र भूम्यर्थे नानृतं वक्तुमर्हसि ।
मा गमः स सुतामात्योऽत्ययं पुत्राननुभ्रमन् ॥
iast:
tasmādrājendra bhūmyarthe nānṛtaṃ vaktumarhasi |
mā gamaḥ sa sutāmātyo'tyayaṃ putrānanubhraman ||
english: So, lord of kings, you should not speak untruth for the sake of land. Do not, following your sons, go to ruin with your sons and ministers.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the gods do not guard people with a stick like herdsmen; they protect someone by giving them good judgement.
devanagari:
न देवा यष्टिमादाय रक्षन्ति पशुपालवत् ।
यं तु रक्षितुमिच्छन्ति बुद्ध्या संविभजन्ति तम् ॥
iast:
na devā yaṣṭimādāya rakṣanti paśupālavat |
yaṃ tu rakṣitumicchanti buddhyā saṃvibhajanti tam ||
english: The gods do not take up a stick and guard people like a herdsman. Whomever they wish to protect, they endow with understanding.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the more a person sets the mind on the good, the more all their aims succeed.
devanagari:
यथा यथा हि पुरुषः कल्याणे कुरुते मनः ।
तथा तथास्य सर्वार्थाः सिध्यन्ते नात्र संशयः ॥
iast:
yathā yathā hi puruṣaḥ kalyāṇe kurute manaḥ |
tathā tathāsya sarvārthāḥ sidhyante nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
english: The more a person sets their mind on what is good, the more all their aims succeed; there is no doubt of this.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says sacred verses do not save a deceiver from wrongdoing; they leave him at the end like fledged birds leave the nest.
devanagari:
न छन्दांसि वृजिनात्तारयन्ति
आयाविनं मायया वर्तमानम् ।
नीडं शकुन्ता इव जातपक्षाश्
छन्दांस्येनं प्रजहत्यन्तकाले ॥
iast:
na chandāṃsi vṛjināttārayanti
āyāvinaṃ māyayā vartamānam |
nīḍaṃ śakuntā iva jātapakṣāś
chandāṃsyenaṃ prajahatyantakāle ||
english: The Vedic verses do not carry across sin a deceitful person who lives by deceit; at the end they leave him, as fledged birds leave the nest.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists things to avoid: drunken drinking, quarrels, feuds with groups, coming between spouses, family splits and corrupt paths.
devanagari:
मत्तापानं कलहं पूगवैरं
भार्यापत्योरन्तरं ज्ञातिभेदम् ।
राजद्विष्टं स्त्रीपुमांसोर्विवादं
वर्ज्यान्याहुर्यश्च पन्थाः प्रदुष्ठः ॥
iast:
mattāpānaṃ kalahaṃ pūgavairaṃ
bhāryāpatyorantaraṃ jñātibhedam |
rājadviṣṭaṃ strīpumāṃsorvivādaṃ
varjyānyāhuryaśca panthāḥ praduṣṭhaḥ ||
english: Drinking to intoxication, quarrels, feuds with groups, coming between husband and wife, dividing relatives, what the king hates, disputes between men and women, and any path that is corrupt: these, they say, are to be avoided.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists seven kinds of people not to appoint as witnesses, reflecting his time's suspicion of certain trades.
devanagari:
सामुद्रिकं वणिजं चोरपूर्वं
शलाक धूर्तं च चिकित्सकं च ।
अरिं च मित्रं च कुशीलवं च
नैतान्साख्येष्वधिकुर्वीत सप्त ॥
iast:
sāmudrikaṃ vaṇijaṃ corapūrvaṃ
śalāka dhūrtaṃ ca cikitsakaṃ ca |
ariṃ ca mitraṃ ca kuśīlavaṃ ca
naitānsākhyeṣvadhikurvīta sapta ||
english: A palm-reader, a merchant who was once a thief, a gambler, a physician, an enemy, a friend and a performer: these seven should not be made witnesses.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura repeats that rites which remove fear bring fear when done out of pride.
devanagari:
मानाग्निहोत्रमुत मानमौनं
मानेनाधीतमुत मानयज्ञः ।
एतानि चत्वार्यभयङ्कराणि
भयं प्रयच्छन्त्ययथा कृतानि ॥
iast:
mānāgnihotramuta mānamaunaṃ
mānenādhītamuta mānayajñaḥ |
etāni catvāryabhayaṅkarāṇi
bhayaṃ prayacchantyayathā kṛtāni ||
english: The fire offering for pride, silence for pride, study for pride and sacrifice for pride: these four, which remove fear, bring fear when done improperly.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura begins a list of those equal to a brahmin-killer, from arsonists to traitors to friends (3.39-3.41).
devanagari:
अगार दाही गरदः कुण्डाशी सोमविक्रयी ।
पर्व कारश्च सूची च मित्र ध्रुक्पारदारिकः ॥
iast:
agāra dāhī garadaḥ kuṇḍāśī somavikrayī |
parva kāraśca sūcī ca mitra dhrukpāradārikaḥ ||
english: One who sets houses on fire, a poisoner, one who lives off an adulteress's son, a seller of soma, a maker of arrows, an astrologer, one who betrays a friend, an adulterer,
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues the list of grave wrongdoers in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
भ्रूणहा गुरु तल्पी च यश्च स्यात्पानपो द्विजः ।
अतितीक्ष्णश्च काकश्च नास्तिको वेद निन्दकः ॥
iast:
bhrūṇahā guru talpī ca yaśca syātpānapo dvijaḥ |
atitīkṣṇaśca kākaśca nāstiko veda nindakaḥ ||
english: one who kills an embryo, one who violates his teacher's bed, a twice-born who drinks, one who is excessively harsh, a crow-like person, an unbeliever, a reviler of the Veda,
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura completes the list, ending with one who harms someone who asked for protection.
devanagari:
स्रुव प्रग्रहणो व्रात्यः कीनाशश्चार्थवानपि ।
रक्षेत्युक्तश्च यो हिंस्यात्सर्वे ब्रह्मण्हणैः समाः ॥
iast:
sruva pragrahaṇo vrātyaḥ kīnāśaścārthavānapi |
rakṣetyuktaśca yo hiṃsyātsarve brahmaṇhaṇaiḥ samāḥ ||
english: one who takes up the ladle though outcaste, a peasant even when wealthy, and one who harms someone who asked for protection: all these are equal to killers of brahmins.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says each thing is tested its own way: gold by fire, a good person by conduct, the brave by danger, and friends by hardship.
devanagari:
तृणोक्लया ज्ञायते जातरूपं
युगे भद्रो व्यवहारेण साधुः ।
शूरो भयेष्वर्थकृच्छ्रेषु धीरः
कृच्छ्रास्वापत्सु सुहृदश्चारयश् च ॥
iast:
tṛṇoklayā jñāyate jātarūpaṃ
yuge bhadro vyavahāreṇa sādhuḥ |
śūro bhayeṣvarthakṛcchreṣu dhīraḥ
kṛcchrāsvāpatsu suhṛdaścārayaś ca ||
english: Gold is known by a flame of grass, the good by their dealings, the virtuous by their conduct, the brave in times of fear, the steady in money troubles, and friends and enemies in hard times and calamities.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists what robs what: age robs beauty, hope robs patience, envy robs dharma, anger robs fortune, and pride robs everything.
devanagari:
जरा रूपं हरति हि धैर्यमाशा
मृत्युः प्राणान्धर्मचर्यामसूया ।
क्रोधः श्रियं शीलमनार्य सेवा
ह्रियं कामः सर्वमेवाभिमानः ॥
iast:
jarā rūpaṃ harati hi dhairyamāśā
mṛtyuḥ prāṇāndharmacaryāmasūyā |
krodhaḥ śriyaṃ śīlamanārya sevā
hriyaṃ kāmaḥ sarvamevābhimānaḥ ||
english: Old age robs beauty, hope robs patience, death robs life, envy robs the practice of dharma, anger robs good fortune, serving the ignoble robs good character, lust robs modesty, and pride robs everything.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says fortune is born of good deeds, grows with confidence, takes root through skill and stands firm through self-control.
devanagari:
श्रीर्मङ्गलात्प्रभवति प्रागल्भ्यात्सम्प्रवर्धते ।
दाक्ष्यात्तु कुरुते मूलं संयमात्प्रतितिष्ठति ॥
iast:
śrīrmaṅgalātprabhavati prāgalbhyātsampravardhate |
dākṣyāttu kurute mūlaṃ saṃyamātpratitiṣṭhati ||
english: Fortune arises from auspicious conduct, grows through boldness, takes root through skill, and stands firm through self-control.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura repeats the eight qualities that make a person shine (as at 1.108).
devanagari:
अष्टौ गुणाः पुरुषं दीपयन्ति
प्रज्ञा च कौल्यं च दमः श्रुतं च ।
पराक्रमश्चाबहु भाषिता च
दानं यथाशक्ति कृतज्ञता च ॥
iast:
aṣṭau guṇāḥ puruṣaṃ dīpayanti
prajñā ca kaulyaṃ ca damaḥ śrutaṃ ca |
parākramaścābahu bhāṣitā ca
dānaṃ yathāśakti kṛtajñatā ca ||
english: Eight qualities make a person shine: wisdom, good family, self-control, learning, courage, not talking too much, giving according to one's means, and gratitude.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura adds that one quality, being honoured by the king, outshines all the others.
devanagari:
एतान्गुणांस्तात महानुभावान्
एको गुणः संश्रयते प्रसह्य ।
राजा यदा सत्कुरुते मनुष्यं
सर्वान्गुणानेष गुणोऽतिभाति ॥
iast:
etānguṇāṃstāta mahānubhāvān
eko guṇaḥ saṃśrayate prasahya |
rājā yadā satkurute manuṣyaṃ
sarvānguṇāneṣa guṇo'tibhāti ||
english: These great qualities, dear one, one quality takes over by force: when the king honours a person, that one quality outshines all the others.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names eight signs of heaven in the human world: four followed by the good and four the good keep to.
devanagari:
अष्टौ नृपेमानि मनुष्यलोके
स्वर्गस्य लोकस्य निदर्शनानि ।
चत्वार्येषामन्ववेतानि सद्भिश्
चत्वार्येषामन्ववयन्ति सन्तः ॥
iast:
aṣṭau nṛpemāni manuṣyaloke
svargasya lokasya nidarśanāni |
catvāryeṣāmanvavetāni sadbhiś
catvāryeṣāmanvavayanti santaḥ ||
english: These eight, king, are signs of the heavenly world in the world of humans: four of them are followed by the good, and four the good always keep to.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names them: sacrifice, giving, study and austerity; and self-control, truth, straightforwardness and gentleness.
devanagari:
यज्ञो दानमध्ययनं तपश् च
चत्वार्येतान्यन्ववेतानि सद्भिः ।
दमः सत्यमार्जवमानृशंस्यं
चत्वार्येतान्यन्ववयन्ति सन्तः ॥
iast:
yajño dānamadhyayanaṃ tapaś ca
catvāryetānyanvavetāni sadbhiḥ |
damaḥ satyamārjavamānṛśaṃsyaṃ
catvāryetānyanvavayanti santaḥ ||
english: Sacrifice, giving, study and austerity: these four are followed by the good. Self-control, truth, straightforwardness and gentleness: these four the good always keep to.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says it is no assembly without elders, they are no elders if they do not speak dharma, and it is no truth if mixed with deceit.
devanagari:
न सा सभा यत्र न सन्ति वृद्धा
न ते वृद्धा ये न वदन्ति धर्मम् ।
नासौ हर्मो यतन सत्यमस्ति
न तत्सत्यं यच्छलेनानुविद्धम् ॥
iast:
na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā
na te vṛddhā ye na vadanti dharmam |
nāsau harmo yatana satyamasti
na tatsatyaṃ yacchalenānuviddham ||
english: That is no assembly where there are no elders; they are no elders who do not speak dharma; that is no dharma where there is no truth; that is no truth which is pierced with deceit.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names ten grounds of association: truth, looks, learning, knowledge, family, character, strength, wealth, courage and fine speech.
devanagari:
सत्यं रूपं श्रुतं विद्या कौल्यं शीलं बलं धनम् ।
शौर्यं च चिरभाष्यं च दशः संसर्गयोनयः ॥
iast:
satyaṃ rūpaṃ śrutaṃ vidyā kaulyaṃ śīlaṃ balaṃ dhanam |
śauryaṃ ca cirabhāṣyaṃ ca daśaḥ saṃsargayonayaḥ ||
english: Truth, beauty, learning, knowledge, family, character, strength, wealth, courage and varied speech: these ten are the sources of association.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says doing wrong earns a bad name and bad fruit; doing good earns a good name and good fruit.
devanagari:
पापं कुर्वन्पापकीर्तिः पापमेवाश्नुते फलम् ।
पुण्यं कुर्वन्पुण्यकीर्तिः पुण्यमेवाश्नुते फलम् ॥
iast:
pāpaṃ kurvanpāpakīrtiḥ pāpamevāśnute phalam |
puṇyaṃ kurvanpuṇyakīrtiḥ puṇyamevāśnute phalam ||
english: Doing wrong, one gains a bad name and reaps only wrong's fruit; doing good, one gains a good name and reaps only good's fruit.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says wrongdoing repeated destroys judgement, and one who has lost judgement keeps doing wrong.
devanagari:
पापं प्रज्ञां नाशयति क्रियमाणं पुनः पुनः ।
नष्टप्रज्ञः पापमेव नित्यमारभते नरः ॥
iast:
pāpaṃ prajñāṃ nāśayati kriyamāṇaṃ punaḥ punaḥ |
naṣṭaprajñaḥ pāpameva nityamārabhate naraḥ ||
english: Wrongdoing, done again and again, destroys wisdom; a person whose wisdom is destroyed always takes up wrongdoing again.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says doing good repeatedly increases wisdom, and one grown wise keeps doing good.
devanagari:
पुण्यं प्रज्ञां वर्धयति क्रियमाणं पुनः पुनः ।
वृद्धप्रज्ञः पुण्यमेव नित्यमारभते नरः ॥
iast:
puṇyaṃ prajñāṃ vardhayati kriyamāṇaṃ punaḥ punaḥ |
vṛddhaprajñaḥ puṇyameva nityamārabhate naraḥ ||
english: Good deeds, done again and again, increase wisdom; a person whose wisdom has grown always takes up good deeds.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the envious, biting, harsh and quarrelsome person, doing wrong, soon meets great trouble.
devanagari:
असूयको दन्द शूको निष्ठुरो वैरकृन्नरः ।
स कृच्छ्रं महदाप्नोतो नचिरात्पापमाचरन् ॥
iast:
asūyako danda śūko niṣṭhuro vairakṛnnaraḥ |
sa kṛcchraṃ mahadāpnoto nacirātpāpamācaran ||
english: The envious, the biting, the harsh and the one who makes enemies, doing wrong, soon meets great trouble.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one free of envy, wise and always doing good, finds happiness easily and shines everywhere.
devanagari:
अनसूयः कृतप्रज्ञ्टः शोभनान्याचरन्सदा ।
अकृच्छ्रात्सुखमाप्नोति सर्वत्र च विराजते ॥
iast:
anasūyaḥ kṛtaprajñṭaḥ śobhanānyācaransadā |
akṛcchrātsukhamāpnoti sarvatra ca virājate ||
english: One free of envy, of mature wisdom, always doing what is good, gains happiness without hardship and shines everywhere.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise person is one who learns wisdom from the wise, and so can grow in happiness.
devanagari:
प्रज्ञामेवागमयति यः प्राज्ञेभ्यः स पण्डितः ।
प्राज्ञो ह्यवाप्य धर्मार्थौ शक्नोति सुखमेधितुम् ॥
iast:
prajñāmevāgamayati yaḥ prājñebhyaḥ sa paṇḍitaḥ |
prājño hyavāpya dharmārthau śaknoti sukhamedhitum ||
english: One who gains wisdom from the wise is truly wise; for the wise, having gained dharma and true benefit, can grow in happiness.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says do by day what lets you sleep in peace at night, and in eight months what lets you live well in the rains.
devanagari:
दिवसेनैव तत्कुर्याद्येन रातौ सुखं वसेत् ।
अष्ट मासेन तत्कुर्याद्येन वर्षाः सुखं वसेत् ॥
iast:
divasenaiva tatkuryādyena rātau sukhaṃ vaset |
aṣṭa māsena tatkuryādyena varṣāḥ sukhaṃ vaset ||
english: One should do in the day what lets one live happily at night, and in eight months what lets one live happily through the rainy season.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues: in youth do what lets you live happily in old age, and through life what lets you be happy after death.
devanagari:
पूर्वे वयसि तत्कुर्याद्येन वृद्धसुखं वसेत् ।
यावज्जीवेन तत्कुर्याद्येन प्रेत्य सुखं वसेत् ॥
iast:
pūrve vayasi tatkuryādyena vṛddhasukhaṃ vaset |
yāvajjīvena tatkuryādyena pretya sukhaṃ vaset ||
english: In youth one should do what lets one live happily in old age, and throughout life what lets one live happily after death.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists things praised only once their test is past, including a wife past her youth, in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
जीर्णमन्नं प्रशंसन्ति भार्यं च गतयौवनाम् ।
शूरं विगतसङ्ग्रामं गतपारं तपस्विनम् ॥
iast:
jīrṇamannaṃ praśaṃsanti bhāryaṃ ca gatayauvanām |
śūraṃ vigatasaṅgrāmaṃ gatapāraṃ tapasvinam ||
english: They praise food once digested, a wife whose youth has passed, a hero whose battles are over, and an ascetic who has reached the far shore.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a gap patched with wrongly gained wealth stays open, and another one breaks open elsewhere.
devanagari:
धनेनाधर्मलब्धेन यच्छिद्रमपिधीयते ।
असंवृतं तद्भवति ततोऽन्यदवदीर्यते ॥
iast:
dhanenādharmalabdhena yacchidramapidhīyate |
asaṃvṛtaṃ tadbhavati tato'nyadavadīryate ||
english: The gap that is covered with wealth gained by adharma stays uncovered, and another breaks open from it.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the teacher governs the self-controlled, the king the wicked, and Yama, god of death, governs secret wrongdoers.
devanagari:
गुरुरात्मवतां शास्ता शासा राजा दुरात्मनाम् ।
अथ प्रच्छन्नपापानां शास्ता वैवस्वतो यमः ॥
iast:
gururātmavatāṃ śāstā śāsā rājā durātmanām |
atha pracchannapāpānāṃ śāstā vaivasvato yamaḥ ||
english: The teacher is the instructor of the self-controlled; the king is the ruler of the wicked; and of those who sin in secret, the ruler is Yama, son of Vivasvat.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the origins of sages, rivers and great families should not be probed, with a gendered remark about women.
devanagari:
ऋषीणां च नदीनां च कुलानां च महामनाम् ।
प्रभवो नाधिगन्तव्यः स्त्रीणां दुश्चरितस्य च ॥
iast:
ṛṣīṇāṃ ca nadīnāṃ ca kulānāṃ ca mahāmanām |
prabhavo nādhigantavyaḥ strīṇāṃ duścaritasya ca ||
english: The origin of sages, of rivers, of great-souled families, and of women's misconduct should not be investigated.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a kshatriya who honours the twice-born, gives and is straightforward with kin rules long and reaches heaven.
devanagari:
द्विजातिपूजाभिरतो दाता ज्ञातिषु चार्जवी ।
क्षत्रियः स्वर्गभाग्राजंश्चिरं पालयते महीम् ॥
iast:
dvijātipūjābhirato dātā jñātiṣu cārjavī |
kṣatriyaḥ svargabhāgrājaṃściraṃ pālayate mahīm ||
english: A kshatriya devoted to honouring the twice-born, generous and straightforward with his kin, rules the earth long, king, and gains heaven.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says three gather the earth's golden flowers: the brave, the learned and one who knows how to serve.
devanagari:
सुवर्णपुष्पां पृथिवीं चिन्वन्ति पुरुषास्त्रयः ।
शूरश्च कृतविद्यश्च यश्च जानाति सेवितुम् ॥
iast:
suvarṇapuṣpāṃ pṛthivīṃ cinvanti puruṣāstrayaḥ |
śūraśca kṛtavidyaśca yaśca jānāti sevitum ||
english: Three kinds of people gather the earth's golden flowers: the brave, the learned, and one who knows how to serve.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura ranks work by whether it uses intellect, arms, legs or carrying loads, reflecting his time's hierarchy of labour.
devanagari:
बुद्धिश्रेष्ठानि कर्माणि बाहुमध्यानि भारत ।
तानि जङ्घा जघन्यानि भारप्रत्यवराणि च ॥
iast:
buddhiśreṣṭhāni karmāṇi bāhumadhyāni bhārata |
tāni jaṅghā jaghanyāni bhārapratyavarāṇi ca ||
english: Deeds of the intellect are best, Bharata; deeds of the arms are middling; deeds of the legs are lowest, and carrying loads lower still.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura again asks how the king hopes to prosper with power placed in Duryodhana, Shakuni, Duhshasana and Karna.
devanagari:
दुर्योधने च शकुनौ मूढे दुःशासने तथा ।
कर्णे चैश्वर्यमाधाय कथं त्वं भूतिमिच्छसि ॥
iast:
duryodhane ca śakunau mūḍhe duḥśāsane tathā |
karṇe caiśvaryamādhāya kathaṃ tvaṃ bhūtimicchasi ||
english: Having placed sovereignty in Duryodhana, in Shakuni, in the foolish Duhshasana, and in Karna, how can you hope for prosperity?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura reminds Dhritarashtra that the Pandavas treat him as a father and asks him to treat them as sons.
devanagari:
सर्वैर्गुणैरुपेताश्च पाण्डवा भरतर्षभ ।
पितृवत्त्वयि वर्तन्ते तेषु वर्तस्व पुत्रवत् ॥
iast:
sarvairguṇairupetāśca pāṇḍavā bharatarṣabha |
pitṛvattvayi vartante teṣu vartasva putravat ||
english: The Pandavas, endowed with every virtue, best of the Bharatas, behave towards you as towards a father; behave towards them as towards sons.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura introduces an old story: the dialogue of the sage Atreya with the Sadhya gods.
devanagari:
अत्रैवोदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम् ।
आत्रेयस्य च संवादं साध्यानां चेति नः श्रुतम् ॥
iast:
atraivodāharantīmamitihāsaṃ purātanam |
