ātreyasya ca saṃvādaṃ sādhyānāṃ ceti naḥ śrutam ||
english: On this they cite an ancient story, the dialogue of Atreya and the Sadhyas, as we have heard.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: The story begins: the Sadhya gods question a great sage of strict vows who wanders in the form of a swan.
devanagari:
चरन्तं हंसरूपेण महर्षिं संशितव्रतम् ।
साध्या देवा महाप्राज्ञं पर्यपृच्छन्त वै पुरा ॥
iast:
carantaṃ haṃsarūpeṇa maharṣiṃ saṃśitavratam |
sādhyā devā mahāprājñaṃ paryapṛcchanta vai purā ||
english: Long ago the Sadhya gods questioned the very wise great sage of strict vows as he wandered in the form of a swan.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the Sadhyas
context: In the story, the Sadhyas tell the swan-sage they cannot fathom him and ask for his wise words.
devanagari:
साध्या देवा वय्मस्मो महर्षे
दृष्ट्वा भवन्तं न शक्नुमोऽनुमातुम् ।
श्रुतेन धीरो बुद्धिमांस्त्वं मतो नः
काव्यां वाचं वक्तुमर्हस्युदाराम् ॥
iast:
sādhyā devā vaymasmo maharṣe
dṛṣṭvā bhavantaṃ na śaknumo'numātum |
śrutena dhīro buddhimāṃstvaṃ mato naḥ
kāvyāṃ vācaṃ vaktumarhasyudārām ||
english: We are the Sadhya gods, great sage. Seeing you, we cannot fathom you. You are known to us as steady and wise through learning; please speak noble, wise words.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says the task is steadiness, calm and following true dharma, untying the heart's knots and mastering likes and dislikes.
devanagari:
एतत्कार्यममराः संश्रुतं मे
धृतिः शमः सत्यधर्मानुवृत्तिः ।
ग्रन्थिं विनीय हृदयस्य सर्वं
प्रियाप्रिये चात्मवशं नयीत ॥
iast:
etatkāryamamarāḥ saṃśrutaṃ me
dhṛtiḥ śamaḥ satyadharmānuvṛttiḥ |
granthiṃ vinīya hṛdayasya sarvaṃ
priyāpriye cātmavaśaṃ nayīta ||
english: This, immortals, I have heard is what must be done: steadiness, calm and following the dharma of truth. Untying every knot of the heart, one should bring the pleasant and unpleasant under one's control.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says not to answer abuse with abuse: anger endured burns up the abuser and wins merit for the one who endures.
devanagari:
आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षितः ।
आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति ॥
iast:
ākruśyamāno nākrośenmanyureva titikṣitaḥ |
ākroṣṭāraṃ nirdahati sukṛtaṃ cāsya vindati ||
english: When abused, one should not abuse in return. Anger that is endured burns up the abuser, and the one who endures gains his merit.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage advises against abusing, insulting, betraying friends, serving the base, arrogance and harsh, wounding speech.
devanagari:
नाक्रोशी स्यान्नावमानी परस्य
मित्रद्रोही नोत नीचोपसेवी ।
न चातिमानी न च हीनवृत्तो
रूक्षां वाचं रुशतीं वर्जयीत ॥
iast:
nākrośī syānnāvamānī parasya
mitradrohī nota nīcopasevī |
na cātimānī na ca hīnavṛtto
rūkṣāṃ vācaṃ ruśatīṃ varjayīta ||
english: One should not be abusive, nor insult another, nor betray a friend, nor serve the base; not be too proud, nor of low conduct; and should avoid harsh, wounding speech.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says cruel words burn a person's vital spots, bones, heart and life, so the lover of dharma avoids them.
devanagari:
मर्माण्यस्थीनि हृदयं तथासून्
घोरा वाचो निर्दहन्तीह पुंसाम् ।
तस्माद्वाचं रुशतीं रूक्षरूपां
धर्मारामो नित्यशो वर्जयीत ॥
iast:
marmāṇyasthīni hṛdayaṃ tathāsūn
ghorā vāco nirdahantīha puṃsām |
tasmādvācaṃ ruśatīṃ rūkṣarūpāṃ
dharmārāmo nityaśo varjayīta ||
english: Cruel words burn up a person's vital spots, bones, heart and life. So one who delights in dharma should always avoid wounding, harsh speech.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says the harsh-tongued person who stings others with thorny words carries misfortune in his own mouth.
devanagari:
अरुं तुरं परुषं रूक्षवाचं
वाक्कण्टकैर्वितुदन्तं मनुष्यान् ।
विद्यादलक्ष्मीकतमं जनानां
मुखे निबद्धां निरृतिं वहन्तम् ॥
iast:
aruṃ turaṃ paruṣaṃ rūkṣavācaṃ
vākkaṇṭakairvitudantaṃ manuṣyān |
vidyādalakṣmīkatamaṃ janānāṃ
mukhe nibaddhāṃ nirṛtiṃ vahantam ||
english: Know that the cutting, harsh, rough-tongued person who pricks others with thorns of words is the most unfortunate of people, carrying ruin bound in his mouth.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says if someone pierces the wise with sharp, burning arrows of words, the wise know that this adds to their merit.
devanagari:
परश्चेदेनमधिविध्येत बाणैर्
भृशं सुतीक्ष्णैरनलार्क दीप्तैः ।
विरिच्यमानोऽप्यतिरिच्यमानो
विद्यात्कविः सुकृतं मे दधाति ॥
iast:
paraścedenamadhividhyeta bāṇair
bhṛśaṃ sutīkṣṇairanalārka dīptaiḥ |
viricyamāno'pyatiricyamāno
vidyātkaviḥ sukṛtaṃ me dadhāti ||
english: If another pierces him deeply with very sharp arrows of words, burning like fire or sun, the wise one, though hurt and wounded, should know: 'He is adding to my merit.'
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says a person takes on the colour of whoever he serves, good or bad, like cloth in dye.
devanagari:
यदि सन्तं सेवते यद्यसन्तं
तपस्विनं यदि वा स्तेनमेव ।
वासो यथा रङ्ग वशं प्रयाति
तथा स तेषां वशमभ्युपैति ॥
iast:
yadi santaṃ sevate yadyasantaṃ
tapasvinaṃ yadi vā stenameva |
vāso yathā raṅga vaśaṃ prayāti
tathā sa teṣāṃ vaśamabhyupaiti ||
english: Whether one keeps company with the good or the bad, with an ascetic or a thief, one comes under their influence, as cloth takes the colour of the dye.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says the gods long for one who does not start or provoke quarrels, does not strike back or harm, and wishes no evil even to an attacker.
devanagari:
वादं तु यो न प्रवदेन्न वादयेद्
यो नाहतः प्रतिहन्यान्न घातयेत् ।
यो हन्तुकामस्य न पापमिच्छेत्
तस्मै देवाः स्पृहयन्त्यागताय ॥
iast:
vādaṃ tu yo na pravadenna vādayed
yo nāhataḥ pratihanyānna ghātayet |
yo hantukāmasya na pāpamicchet
tasmai devāḥ spṛhayantyāgatāya ||
english: One who does not start a quarrel nor provoke one, who, when struck, does not strike back nor cause another to strike, and who wishes no harm even to one who wants to kill him: the gods long for his coming.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage ranks speech: silence is better than speaking; then truthful speech, then kind speech, then righteous speech.
devanagari:
अव्याहृतं व्याहृताच्छ्रेय आहुः
सत्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तद्द्वितीयम् ।
प्रियंवदेद्व्याहृतं तत्तृतीयं
धर्म्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तच्चतुर्थम् ॥
iast:
avyāhṛtaṃ vyāhṛtācchreya āhuḥ
satyaṃ vadedvyāhṛtaṃ taddvitīyam |
priyaṃvadedvyāhṛtaṃ tattṛtīyaṃ
dharmyaṃ vadedvyāhṛtaṃ taccaturtham ||
english: They say not speaking is better than speaking; speaking the truth is the second-best speech; speaking kindly is the third; speaking what is righteous is the fourth.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says a person becomes like those he argues with, those he serves, and what he wishes to become.
devanagari:
यादृशैः संविवदते यादृशांश् चोपसेवते ।
यादृगिच्छेच्च भवितुं तादृग्भवति पूरुषः ॥
iast:
yādṛśaiḥ saṃvivadate yādṛśāṃś copasevate |
yādṛgicchecca bhavituṃ tādṛgbhavati pūruṣaḥ ||
english: Such as those he quarrels with, such as those he serves, and such as he wishes to be: such a person becomes.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says from whatever one withdraws, one is freed; by withdrawing from all, one knows not the least pain.
devanagari:
यतो यतो निवर्तते ततस्ततो विमुच्यते ।
निवर्तनाद्धि सर्वतो न वेत्ति दुःखमण्वपि ॥
iast:
yato yato nivartate tatastato vimucyate |
nivartanāddhi sarvato na vetti duḥkhamaṇvapi ||
english: From whatever one turns away, from that one is freed. By turning away from everything, one does not know even the slightest pain.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage describes the best person: neither conquered nor seeking to conquer, makes no enemies, even in blame and praise, neither grieving nor exulting.
devanagari:
न जीयते नोत जिगीषतेऽन्यान्
न वैरक्कृच्चाप्रतिघातकश् च ।
निन्दा प्रशंसासु समस्वभावो
न शोचते हृष्यति नैव चायम् ॥
iast:
na jīyate nota jigīṣate'nyān
na vairakkṛccāpratighātakaś ca |
nindā praśaṃsāsu samasvabhāvo
na śocate hṛṣyati naiva cāyam ||
english: He is not conquered and does not seek to conquer others; he makes no enmity and does not strike back; he is the same in blame and praise; he neither grieves nor exults.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says the best person wishes everyone well, never plots another's ruin, and is truthful, gentle and self-controlled.
devanagari:
भावमिच्छति सर्वस्य नाभावे कुरुते मतिम् ।
सत्यवादी मृदुर्दान्तो यः स उत्तमपूरुषः ॥
iast:
bhāvamicchati sarvasya nābhāve kurute matim |
satyavādī mṛdurdānto yaḥ sa uttamapūruṣaḥ ||
english: One who wishes well to all, does not set his mind on anyone's ruin, and is truthful, gentle and self-controlled is the best of people.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says the middling person does not give empty comfort, gives what he promises, and knows success from failure.
devanagari:
नानर्थकं सान्त्वयति प्रतिज्ञाय ददाति च ।
राद्धापराद्धे जानाति यः स मध्यमपूरुषः ॥
iast:
nānarthakaṃ sāntvayati pratijñāya dadāti ca |
rāddhāparāddhe jānāti yaḥ sa madhyamapūruṣaḥ ||
english: One who does not console without reason, who gives once he has promised, and who knows success from failure is a middling person.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage describes the lowest person: harsh in rule, destructive, ungrateful, ruled by anger and friend to no one.
devanagari:
दुःशासनस्तूपहन्ता न शास्ता
नावर्तते मन्युवशात्कृतघ्नः ।
न कस्य चिन्मित्रमथो दुरात्मा
कलाश्चैता अधमस्येह पुंसः ॥
iast:
duḥśāsanastūpahantā na śāstā
nāvartate manyuvaśātkṛtaghnaḥ |
na kasya cinmitramatho durātmā
kalāścaitā adhamasyeha puṃsaḥ ||
english: Harsh in command, a destroyer rather than a guide, not turning back from anger, ungrateful, friend to no one, evil-minded: these are the marks of the lowest person here.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says the lowest person, distrusting himself, believes no good of others and drives away friends.
devanagari:
न श्रद्दधाति कल्याणं परेभ्योऽप्यात्मशङ्कितः ।
निराकरोति मित्राणि यो वै सोऽधम पूरुषः ॥
iast:
na śraddadhāti kalyāṇaṃ parebhyo'pyātmaśaṅkitaḥ |
nirākaroti mitrāṇi yo vai so'dhama pūruṣaḥ ||
english: One who, doubting himself, does not believe any good of others, and drives away his friends, is the lowest person.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage advises serving the best people, the middling when the time demands, and never the lowest.
devanagari:
उत्तमानेव सेवेत प्राप्ते काले तु मध्यमान् ।
अधमांस्तु न सेवेत य इच्छेच्छ्रेय आत्मनः ॥
iast:
uttamāneva seveta prāpte kāle tu madhyamān |
adhamāṃstu na seveta ya icchecchreya ātmanaḥ ||
english: One who wishes his own good should serve the best; when the time comes, the middling; but should not serve the lowest.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: the swan
context: The swan-sage says one can get wealth by wicked force, constant effort, intelligence or valour, but not real praise or the conduct of great families.
devanagari:
प्राप्नोति वै वित्तमसद्बलेन
नित्योत्थानात्प्रज्ञया पौरुषेण ।
न त्वेव सम्यग्लभते प्रशंसां
न वृत्तमाप्नोति महाकुलानाम् ॥
iast:
prāpnoti vai vittamasadbalena
nityotthānātprajñayā pauruṣeṇa |
na tveva samyaglabhate praśaṃsāṃ
na vṛttamāpnoti mahākulānām ||
english: One may gain wealth by wicked force, by constant effort, by intelligence and by valour; but one does not truly gain praise, nor the conduct of great families.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra asks Vidura which families are truly great, the kind gods and the learned admire.
devanagari:
महाकुलानां स्पृहयन्ति देवा
धर्मार्थवृद्धाश्च बहुश्रुताश् च ।
पृच्छामि त्वां विदुर प्रश्नमेतं
भवन्ति वै कानि महाकुलानि ॥
iast:
mahākulānāṃ spṛhayanti devā
dharmārthavṛddhāśca bahuśrutāś ca |
pṛcchāmi tvāṃ vidura praśnametaṃ
bhavanti vai kāni mahākulāni ||
english: The gods, those grown in dharma and true benefit, and the deeply learned admire great families. I ask you this question, Vidura: which families are truly great?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says families with austerity, self-control, knowledge of Brahman, sacrifices, good marriages and constant giving of food are great.
devanagari:
तमो दमो ब्रह्मवित्त्वं वितानाः
पुण्या विवाहाः सततान्न दानम् ।
येष्वेवैते सप्तगुणा भवन्ति
सम्यग्वृत्तास्तानि महाकुलानि ॥
iast:
tamo damo brahmavittvaṃ vitānāḥ
puṇyā vivāhāḥ satatānna dānam |
yeṣvevaite saptaguṇā bhavanti
samyagvṛttāstāni mahākulāni ||
english: Austerity, self-control, knowledge of the Veda, sacrifices, pure marriages and constant giving of food: families in which these seven qualities are found and practised rightly are great families.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says great families are those whose conduct does not falter, who practise dharma gladly, seek honour for their family and give up falsehood.
devanagari:
येषां न वृत्तं व्यथते न योनिर्
वृत्तप्रसादेन चरन्ति धर्मम् ।
ये कीर्तिमिच्छन्ति कुले विशिष्टां
त्यक्तानृतास्तानि महाकुलानि ॥
iast:
yeṣāṃ na vṛttaṃ vyathate na yonir
vṛttaprasādena caranti dharmam |
ye kīrtimicchanti kule viśiṣṭāṃ
tyaktānṛtāstāni mahākulāni ||
english: Those whose conduct does not falter, who do not shame their ancestry, who practise dharma with a glad heart, who wish for distinguished fame for their family and have given up falsehood: those are great families.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says families fall low through neglecting worship and proper marriage, abandoning the Veda and transgressing dharma.
devanagari:
अनिज्ययाविवाहैर्श्च वेदस्योत्सादनेन च ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति धर्मस्यातिक्रमेण च ॥
iast:
anijyayāvivāhairśca vedasyotsādanena ca |
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti dharmasyātikrameṇa ca ||
english: Through neglecting sacrifice, through improper marriages, through abandoning the Veda, and through transgressing dharma, families fall to low standing.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says families fall by destroying temple property, stealing from brahmins and disrespecting brahmins.
devanagari:
देव द्रव्यविनाशेन ब्रह्म स्वहरणेन च ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति ब्राह्मणातिक्रमेण च ॥
iast:
deva dravyavināśena brahma svaharaṇena ca |
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti brāhmaṇātikrameṇa ca ||
english: Through destroying what belongs to the gods, stealing brahmins' property, and slighting brahmins, families fall to low standing.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says families fall by insulting brahmins and by stealing what was entrusted to them.
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणानां परिभवात्परिवादाच्च भारत ।
कुलान्यकुलतां यान्ति न्यासापहरणेन च ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇānāṃ paribhavātparivādācca bhārata |
kulānyakulatāṃ yānti nyāsāpaharaṇena ca ||
english: Through contempt for brahmins and slander of them, Bharata, and through stealing deposits held in trust, families fall to low standing.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says families rich in cattle, people and horses do not count as families if they lack good conduct.
devanagari:
कुलानि समुपेतानि गोभिः पुरुषतोऽश्वतः ।
कुलसङ्ख्यां न गच्छन्ति यानि हीनानि वृत्ततः ॥
iast:
kulāni samupetāni gobhiḥ puruṣato'śvataḥ |
kulasaṅkhyāṃ na gacchanti yāni hīnāni vṛttataḥ ||
english: Families rich in cattle, people and horses do not count as families if they are lacking in conduct.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says families of little wealth but good conduct count as families and win great fame.
devanagari:
वृत्ततस्त्वविहीनानि कुलान्यल्पधनान्यपि ।
कुलसङ्ख्यां तु गच्छन्ति कर्षन्ति च मयद्यशः ॥
iast:
vṛttatastvavihīnāni kulānyalpadhanānyapi |
kulasaṅkhyāṃ tu gacchanti karṣanti ca mayadyaśaḥ ||
english: But families not lacking in conduct, even if poor in wealth, count as families and win great fame.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura voices a family's wish: may no one among us make enmities, steal, betray friends, deceive, lie, or eat before honouring others.
devanagari:
मा नः कुले वैरकृत्कश् चिदस्तु
राजामात्यो मा परस्वापहारी ।
मित्रद्रोही नैकृतिकोऽनृती वा
पूर्वाशी वा पितृदेवातिथिभ्यः ॥
iast:
mā naḥ kule vairakṛtkaś cidastu
rājāmātyo mā parasvāpahārī |
mitradrohī naikṛtiko'nṛtī vā
pūrvāśī vā pitṛdevātithibhyaḥ ||
english: May there be none in our family who makes enmity, no king's minister who steals others' property, no betrayer of friends, no deceiver or liar, and none who eats before the ancestors, gods and guests.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues the family's wish in terms of his time, concerning brahmins and farming.
devanagari:
यश्च नो ब्राह्मणं हन्याद्यश्च नो ब्राह्मणान्द्विषेत् ।
न नः स समितिं गच्छेद्यश्च नो निर्वपेत्कृषिम् ॥
iast:
yaśca no brāhmaṇaṃ hanyādyaśca no brāhmaṇāndviṣet |
na naḥ sa samitiṃ gacchedyaśca no nirvapetkṛṣim ||
english: Whoever among us kills a brahmin or hates brahmins, and whoever among us takes up farming, let him not come to our assembly.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says four things are never lacking in a good home: grass for a seat, ground, water and kind words.
devanagari:
तृणानि भूमिरुदकं वाक्चतुर्थी च सूनृता ।
सतामेतानि गेहेषु नोच्छिद्यन्ते कदा चन ॥
iast:
tṛṇāni bhūmirudakaṃ vākcaturthī ca sūnṛtā |
satāmetāni geheṣu nocchidyante kadā cana ||
english: A grass mat, ground, water, and fourth, kind words: these are never lacking in the homes of the good.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says these are offered with great faith as hospitality by righteous people of good deeds.
devanagari:
श्रद्धया परया राजन्नुपनीतानि सत्कृतिम् ।
प्रवृत्तानि महाप्राज्ञ धर्मिणां पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥
iast:
śraddhayā parayā rājannupanītāni satkṛtim |
pravṛttāni mahāprājña dharmiṇāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām ||
english: These, king, offered with supreme faith as hospitality, are the practice of righteous people who do good deeds, very wise one.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a small chariot can carry a load other trees cannot, and so people of good families bear burdens others cannot.
devanagari:
सूक्ष्मोऽपि भारं नृपते स्यन्दनो वै
शक्तो वोढुं न तथान्ये महीजाः ।
एवं युक्ता भारसहा भवन्ति
महाकुलीना न तथान्ये मनुष्याः ॥
iast:
sūkṣmo'pi bhāraṃ nṛpate syandano vai
śakto voḍhuṃ na tathānye mahījāḥ |
evaṃ yuktā bhārasahā bhavanti
mahākulīnā na tathānye manuṣyāḥ ||
english: Even a small chariot, king, can bear a load that other things from the earth cannot. So people of great families, when joined to a task, bear the burden, and other people do not.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a friend whose anger you fear, or whom you must approach warily, is not a friend; a true friend is one you trust like a father.
devanagari:
न तन्मित्रं यस्य कोपाद्बिभेति
यद्वा मित्रं शङ्कितेनोपचर्यम् ।
यस्मिन्मित्रे पितरीवाश्वसीत
तद्वै मित्रं सङ्गतानीतराणि ॥
iast:
na tanmitraṃ yasya kopādbibheti
yadvā mitraṃ śaṅkitenopacaryam |
yasminmitre pitarīvāśvasīta
tadvai mitraṃ saṅgatānītarāṇi ||
english: That is no friend whose anger one fears, or a friend who must be approached with suspicion. The friend in whom one can trust as in a father: that is a friend; the rest are mere acquaintances.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says even one who is no relation, if he acts as a friend, is kin, friend, refuge and support.
devanagari:
यदि चेदप्यसम्बन्धो मित्रभावेन वर्तते ।
स एव बन्धुस्तन्मित्रं सा गतिस्तत्परायणम् ॥
iast:
yadi cedapyasambandho mitrabhāvena vartate |
sa eva bandhustanmitraṃ sā gatistatparāyaṇam ||
english: Even if unrelated, one who acts in friendship is the true kinsman, the true friend, the refuge and the final support.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says friendships do not last for one whose mind is fickle, who does not serve elders, and whose thinking keeps shifting.
devanagari:
चलचित्तस्य वै पुंसो वृद्धाननुपसेवतः ।
पारिप्लवमतेर्नित्यमध्रुवो मित्र सङ्ग्रहः ॥
iast:
calacittasya vai puṃso vṛddhānanupasevataḥ |
pāriplavamaternityamadhruvo mitra saṅgrahaḥ ||
english: For a person of fickle mind who does not serve the elders, whose thinking always wavers, the gathering of friends is never lasting.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says wealth passes by the fickle, undisciplined person ruled by the senses, as swans leave a dry lake.
devanagari:
चलचित्तमनात्मानमिन्द्रियाणां वशानुगम् ।
अर्थाः समतिवर्तन्ते हंसाः शुष्कं सरो यथा ॥
iast:
calacittamanātmānamindriyāṇāṃ vaśānugam |
arthāḥ samativartante haṃsāḥ śuṣkaṃ saro yathā ||
english: Wealth passes by the fickle-minded, undisciplined person who follows the senses, as swans leave a dry lake.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wicked grow angry suddenly and are pleased without reason, like a shifting cloud.
devanagari:
अकस्मादेव कुप्यन्ति प्रसीदन्त्यनिमित्ततः ।
शीलमेतदसाधूनामभ्रं पारिप्लवं यथा ॥
iast:
akasmādeva kupyanti prasīdantyanimittataḥ |
śīlametadasādhūnāmabhraṃ pāriplavaṃ yathā ||
english: They grow angry for no reason and are pleased without cause: this is the character of the wicked, like a drifting cloud.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says those who, honoured and helped, do not stand by their friends are so ungrateful even carrion-eaters refuse them when dead.
devanagari:
सत्कृताश्च कृतार्थाश्च मित्राणां न भवन्ति ये ।
तान्मृतानपि क्रव्यादाः कृतघ्नान्नोपभुञ्जते ॥
iast:
satkṛtāśca kṛtārthāśca mitrāṇāṃ na bhavanti ye |
tānmṛtānapi kravyādāḥ kṛtaghnānnopabhuñjate ||
english: Those who, honoured and helped by friends, do not stand by them: even flesh-eating creatures will not eat such ungrateful people when dead.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one should honour friends whether one has wealth or not; only by asking can one learn which friends are true.
devanagari:
अर्थयेदेव मित्राणि सति वासति वा धने ।
नानर्थयन्विजानाति मित्राणां सारफल्गुताम् ॥
iast:
arthayedeva mitrāṇi sati vāsati vā dhane |
nānarthayanvijānāti mitrāṇāṃ sāraphalgutām ||
english: One should seek out friends whether one has wealth or not; without asking of them, one does not learn which friends are solid and which hollow.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says grief destroys beauty, strength and knowledge, and brings disease.
devanagari:
सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते रूपं सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते बलम् ।
सन्तापाद्भ्रश्यते ज्ञानं सन्तापाद्व्याधिमृच्छति ॥
iast:
santāpādbhraśyate rūpaṃ santāpādbhraśyate balam |
santāpādbhraśyate jñānaṃ santāpādvyādhimṛcchati ||
english: Through grief beauty is lost; through grief strength is lost; through grief knowledge is lost; through grief one falls ill.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises not to set the mind on grief: what is lost is not regained by it, the body suffers, and enemies rejoice.
devanagari:
अनवाप्यं च शोकेन शरीरं चोपतप्यते ।
अमित्राश्च प्रहृष्यन्ति मा स्म शोके मनः कृथाः ॥
iast:
anavāpyaṃ ca śokena śarīraṃ copatapyate |
amitrāśca prahṛṣyanti mā sma śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
english: What is beyond reach is not gained by grieving; the body only suffers, and enemies rejoice. Do not set your mind on grief.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a person dies and is born, declines and grows, asks and is asked, grieves and is grieved for, again and again.
devanagari:
पुनर्नरो म्रियते जायते च
पुनर्नरो हीयते वर्धते पुनः ।
पुनर्नरो याचति याच्यते च
पुनर्नरः शोचति शोच्यते पुनः ॥
iast:
punarnaro mriyate jāyate ca
punarnaro hīyate vardhate punaḥ |
punarnaro yācati yācyate ca
punarnaraḥ śocati śocyate punaḥ ||
english: Again and again a person dies and is born; again and again a person declines and grows; again and again a person begs and is begged from; again and again a person grieves and is grieved for.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says pleasure and pain, gain and loss, death and life all touch everyone in turn, so the steady neither exult nor grieve.
devanagari:
सुखं च दुःखं च भवाभवौ च
लाभालाभौ मरणं जीवितं च ।
पर्यायशः सर्वमिह स्पृशन्ति
तस्माद्धीरो नैव हृष्येन्न शोचेत् ॥
iast:
sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca bhavābhavau ca
lābhālābhau maraṇaṃ jīvitaṃ ca |
paryāyaśaḥ sarvamiha spṛśanti
tasmāddhīro naiva hṛṣyenna śocet ||
english: Pleasure and pain, rise and fall, gain and loss, death and life: all these touch everyone in turn. So the steady person neither exults nor grieves.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says wherever the restless six senses go, judgement leaks out like water from a cracked pot.
devanagari:
चलानि हीमानि षडिन्द्रियाणि
तेषां यद्यद्वर्तते यत्र यत्र ।
ततस्ततः स्रवते बुद्धिरस्य
छिद्रोद कुम्भादिव नित्यमम्भः ॥
iast:
calāni hīmāni ṣaḍindriyāṇi
teṣāṃ yadyadvartate yatra yatra |
tatastataḥ sravate buddhirasya
chidroda kumbhādiva nityamambhaḥ ||
english: These six senses are restless. Wherever any of them goes, there a person's understanding flows out, like water from a cracked pot, constantly.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra fears that Yudhishthira, whom he wronged, will destroy his foolish sons in war.
devanagari:
तनुरुच्छः शिखी राजा मिथ्योपचरितो मया ।
मन्दानां मम पुत्राणां युद्धेनान्तं करिष्यति ॥
iast:
tanurucchaḥ śikhī rājā mithyopacarito mayā |
mandānāṃ mama putrāṇāṃ yuddhenāntaṃ kariṣyati ||
english: King Yudhishthira, like a slender flame, whom I treated falsely, will put an end to my foolish sons in war.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra says everything, and his mind, is always anxious, and asks Vidura for the state that is free of anxiety.
devanagari:
नित्योद्विग्नमिदं सर्वं नित्योद्विग्नमिदं मनः ।
यत्तत्पदमनुद्विग्नं तन्मे वद महामते ॥
iast:
nityodvignamidaṃ sarvaṃ nityodvignamidaṃ manaḥ |
yattatpadamanudvignaṃ tanme vada mahāmate ||
english: All this is always anxious; this mind is always anxious. Tell me, very wise one, that state which is free of anxiety.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says he sees no peace apart from learning and austerity, restraint of the senses and giving up greed.
devanagari:
नान्यत्र विद्या तपसोर्नान्यत्रेन्द्रिय निग्रहात् ।
नान्यत्र लोभसन्त्यागाच्छान्तिं पश्याम तेऽनघ ॥
iast:
nānyatra vidyā tapasornānyatrendriya nigrahāt |
nānyatra lobhasantyāgācchāntiṃ paśyāma te'nagha ||
english: I see no peace for you, sinless one, other than through learning and austerity, other than through restraint of the senses, other than through giving up greed.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says understanding removes fear, austerity gains greatness, service to the teacher gives knowledge, and letting go brings peace.
devanagari:
बुद्ध्या भयं प्रणुदति तपसा विन्दते महत् ।
गुरुशुश्रूषया ज्ञानं शान्तिं त्यागेन विन्दति ॥
iast:
buddhyā bhayaṃ praṇudati tapasā vindate mahat |
guruśuśrūṣayā jñānaṃ śāntiṃ tyāgena vindati ||
english: By understanding one drives away fear; by austerity one gains greatness; by serving the teacher one gains knowledge; by letting go one finds peace.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says those seeking liberation move freely here, not relying on the merit of gifts or of the Veda, free of attraction and aversion.
devanagari:
अनाश्रिता दानपुण्यं वेद पुण्यमनाश्रिताः ।
रागद्वेषविनिर्मुक्ता विचरन्तीह मोक्षिणः ॥
iast:
anāśritā dānapuṇyaṃ veda puṇyamanāśritāḥ |
rāgadveṣavinirmuktā vicarantīha mokṣiṇaḥ ||
english: Not depending on the merit of giving, not depending on the merit of the Veda, free of attraction and aversion, those who seek liberation move about here.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says at the end of good study, a well-fought struggle, a good deed and well-practised austerity, happiness grows.
devanagari:
स्वधीतस्य सुयुद्धस्य सुकृतस्य च कर्मणः ।
तपसश्च सुतप्तस्य तस्यान्ते सुखमेधते ॥
iast:
svadhītasya suyuddhasya sukṛtasya ca karmaṇaḥ |
tapasaśca sutaptasya tasyānte sukhamedhate ||
english: At the end of well-done study, a well-fought battle, a good deed and well-practised austerity, happiness grows.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says those divided from their kin never sleep well, even on fine beds, and take no joy in pleasures or praise.
devanagari:
स्वास्तीर्णानि शयनानि प्रपन्ना
न वै भिन्ना जातु निद्रां लभन्ते ।
न स्त्रीषु राजन्रतिमाप्नुवन्ति
न मागधैः स्तूयमाना न सूतैः ॥
iast:
svāstīrṇāni śayanāni prapannā
na vai bhinnā jātu nidrāṃ labhante |
na strīṣu rājanratimāpnuvanti
na māgadhaiḥ stūyamānā na sūtaiḥ ||
english: Those who are divided never find sleep, even lying on well-spread beds; they find no joy in women, king, nor in being praised by bards and heralds.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the divided never practise dharma, never find happiness, do not honour the worthy and do not like peace.
devanagari:
न वै भिन्ना जातु चरन्ति धर्मं
न वै सुखं प्राप्नुवन्तीह भिन्नाः ।
न वै भिन्ना गौरवं मानयन्ति
न वै भिन्नाः प्रशमं रोचयन्ति ॥
iast:
na vai bhinnā jātu caranti dharmaṃ
na vai sukhaṃ prāpnuvantīha bhinnāḥ |
na vai bhinnā gauravaṃ mānayanti
na vai bhinnāḥ praśamaṃ rocayanti ||
english: The divided never practise dharma; the divided never find happiness here; the divided do not honour the worthy; the divided do not like peace.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says good advice tastes bad to the divided, they cannot secure their welfare, and only ruin awaits them.
devanagari:
न वै तेषां स्वदते पथ्यमुक्तं
योगक्षेमं कल्पते नोत तेषाम् ।
भिन्नानां वै मनुजेन्द्र परायणं
न विद्यते किं चिदन्यद्विनाशात् ॥
iast:
na vai teṣāṃ svadate pathyamuktaṃ
yogakṣemaṃ kalpate nota teṣām |
bhinnānāṃ vai manujendra parāyaṇaṃ
na vidyate kiṃ cidanyadvināśāt ||
english: Good advice does not please them, and their getting and keeping does not prosper. For the divided, lord of men, there is no end other than destruction.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists what can be expected of each, including stereotypes about brahmins and women.
devanagari:
सम्भाव्यं गोषु सम्पन्नं सम्भाव्यं ब्राह्मणे तपः ।
सम्भाव्यं स्त्रीषु चापल्यं सम्भाव्यं ज्ञातितो भयम् ॥
iast:
sambhāvyaṃ goṣu sampannaṃ sambhāvyaṃ brāhmaṇe tapaḥ |
sambhāvyaṃ strīṣu cāpalyaṃ sambhāvyaṃ jñātito bhayam ||
english: Wealth is to be expected in cows, austerity in a brahmin, fickleness in women, and danger from kin.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says threads, many and equal when joined, bear much strain: an image of good people united.
devanagari:
तन्तवोऽप्यायता नित्यं तन्तवो बहुलाः समाः ।
बहून्बहुत्वादायासान्सहन्तीत्युपमा सताम् ॥
iast:
tantavo'pyāyatā nityaṃ tantavo bahulāḥ samāḥ |
bahūnbahutvādāyāsānsahantītyupamā satām ||
english: Threads, though thin, when always stretched together and many and equal, bear many strains because they are many: this is the image of the good.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says kinsmen are like firebrands: apart they smoke, together they blaze.
devanagari:
धूमायन्ते व्यपेतानि ज्वलन्ति सहितानि च ।
धृतराष्ट्रोल्मुकानीव ज्ञातयो भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
dhūmāyante vyapetāni jvalanti sahitāni ca |
dhṛtarāṣṭrolmukānīva jñātayo bharatarṣabha ||
english: Apart they smoke, together they blaze: kinsmen are like firebrands, Dhritarashtra, best of the Bharatas.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says those who show 'courage' against brahmins, women, kin and cows fall like ripe fruit from the stalk.
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणेषु च ये शूराः स्त्रीषु ज्ञातिषु गोषु च ।
वृन्तादिव फलं पक्वं धृतराष्ट्र पतन्ति ते ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇeṣu ca ye śūrāḥ strīṣu jñātiṣu goṣu ca |
vṛntādiva phalaṃ pakvaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭra patanti te ||
english: Those who show their courage against brahmins, women, kin and cows fall, Dhritarashtra, like ripe fruit from the stalk.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says even a great, strong, well-rooted tree standing alone can be broken by the wind.
devanagari:
महानप्येकजो वृक्षो बलवान्सुप्रतिष्ठितः ।
प्रसह्य एव वातेन शाखा स्कन्धं विमर्दितुम् ॥
iast:
mahānapyekajo vṛkṣo balavānsupratiṣṭhitaḥ |
prasahya eva vātena śākhā skandhaṃ vimarditum ||
english: Even a great tree standing alone, strong and well rooted, can be broken, branches and trunk, by the wind's force.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says trees standing together, well rooted, withstand the fiercest winds by supporting each other.
devanagari:
अथ ये सहिता वृक्षाः सङ्घशः सुप्रतिष्ठिताः ।
ते हि शीघ्रतमान्वातान्सहन्तेऽन्योन्यसंश्रयात् ॥
iast:
atha ye sahitā vṛkṣāḥ saṅghaśaḥ supratiṣṭhitāḥ |
te hi śīghratamānvātānsahante'nyonyasaṃśrayāt ||
english: But trees that stand together in groups, well rooted, withstand even the fiercest winds by supporting one another.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says enemies think a person alone, even with virtues, can be overcome, as wind overcomes a lone tree.
devanagari:
एवं मनुष्यमप्येकं गुणैरपि समन्वितम् ।
शक्यं द्विषन्तो मन्यन्ते वायुर्द्रुममिवौकजम् ॥
iast:
evaṃ manuṣyamapyekaṃ guṇairapi samanvitam |
śakyaṃ dviṣanto manyante vāyurdrumamivaukajam ||
english: So too, enemies think that a person standing alone, even endowed with virtues, can be overcome, as the wind thinks of a lone tree.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says kin flourish by supporting and relying on one another, like lotuses in a lake.
devanagari:
अन्योन्यसमुपष्टम्भादन्योन्यापाश्रयेण च ।
ज्ञातयः सम्प्रवर्धन्ते सरसीवोत्पलान्युत ॥
iast:
anyonyasamupaṣṭambhādanyonyāpāśrayeṇa ca |
jñātayaḥ sampravardhante sarasīvotpalānyuta ||
english: By supporting one another and relying on one another, kinsmen flourish together, like lotuses in a lake.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists those who must never be killed, including brahmins, cows, women, children and those who seek refuge.
devanagari:
अवध्या ब्राह्मणा गावो स्त्रियो बालाश्च ज्ञातयः ।
येषां चान्नानि भुञ्जीत ये च स्युः शरणागताः ॥
iast:
avadhyā brāhmaṇā gāvo striyo bālāśca jñātayaḥ |
yeṣāṃ cānnāni bhuñjīta ye ca syuḥ śaraṇāgatāḥ ||
english: Not to be killed are brahmins, cows, women, children, kinsmen, those whose food one has eaten, and those who come for refuge.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says that even for the wealthy, no quality matters more than good health; the sick are like the dead.
devanagari:
न मनुष्ये गुणः कश्चिदन्यो धनवताम् अपि ।
अनातुरत्वाद्भद्रं ते मृतकल्पा हि रोगिणः ॥
iast:
na manuṣye guṇaḥ kaścidanyo dhanavatām api |
anāturatvādbhadraṃ te mṛtakalpā hi rogiṇaḥ ||
english: No other quality in a person, even the wealthy, matters like freedom from illness, bless you; the sick are as good as dead.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura urges the king to swallow his anger, a bitter, headache-causing drink that the good drink and the wicked do not.
devanagari:
अव्याधिजं कटुकं शीर्ष रोगं
पापानुबन्धं परुषं तीक्ष्णमुग्रम् ।
सतां पेयं यन्न पिबन्त्यसन्तो
मन्युं महाराज पिब प्रशाम्य ॥
iast:
avyādhijaṃ kaṭukaṃ śīrṣa rogaṃ
pāpānubandhaṃ paruṣaṃ tīkṣṇamugram |
satāṃ peyaṃ yanna pibantyasanto
manyuṃ mahārāja piba praśāmya ||
english: Anger is not born of disease, yet it is bitter, a headache, bound to wrongdoing, harsh, sharp and fierce. The good drink it down; the wicked do not. Drink it down, great king, and be calm.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the sick do not value fruits or enjoy things; always in pain, they know neither wealth nor pleasure.
devanagari:
रोगार्दिता न फलान्याद्रियन्ते
न वै लभन्ते विषयेषु तत्त्वम् ।
दुःखोपेता रोगिणो नित्यमेव
न बुध्यन्ते धनभोगान्न सौख्यम् ॥
iast:
rogārditā na phalānyādriyante
na vai labhante viṣayeṣu tattvam |
duḥkhopetā rogiṇo nityameva
na budhyante dhanabhogānna saukhyam ||
english: Those afflicted by disease do not care for fruits, nor find the true taste of things; always in pain, the sick know neither the enjoyment of wealth nor happiness.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura reminds the king that he ignored his warning at the dice game where Draupadi was won, and that the wise avoid gambling.
devanagari:
पुरा ह्युक्तो नाकरोस्त्वं वचो मे
द्यूते जितां द्रौपदीं प्रेक्ष्य राजन् ।
दुर्योधनं वारयेत्यक्षवत्यां
कितवत्वं पण्डिता वर्जयन्ति ॥
iast:
purā hyukto nākarostvaṃ vaco me
dyūte jitāṃ draupadīṃ prekṣya rājan |
duryodhanaṃ vārayetyakṣavatyāṃ
kitavatvaṃ paṇḍitā varjayanti ||
english: Earlier, seeing Draupadi won at the dice game, I told you, king, 'Stop Duryodhana'; you did not follow my words. The wise avoid gambling.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says strength that clashes with gentleness is no strength; fortune built by cruelty perishes, but fortune grown gently passes to grandchildren.
devanagari:
न तद्बलं यन्मृदुना विरुध्यते
मिश्रो धर्मस्तरसा सेवितव्यः ।
प्रध्वंसिनी क्रूरसमाहिता श्रीर्
मृदुप्रौढा गच्छति पुत्रपौत्रान् ॥
iast:
na tadbalaṃ yanmṛdunā virudhyate
miśro dharmastarasā sevitavyaḥ |
pradhvaṃsinī krūrasamāhitā śrīr
mṛduprauḍhā gacchati putrapautrān ||
english: That is not strength which opposes gentleness; dharma mixed with force should be followed. Fortune gathered by cruelty is ruinous; fortune grown through gentleness passes on to sons and grandsons.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura urges that Dhritarashtra's sons and the Pandavas protect each other and live united and prosperous.
devanagari:
धार्तराष्ट्राः पाण्डवान्पालयन्तु
पाण्डोः सुतास्तव पुत्रांश्च पान्तु ।
एकारिमित्राः कुरवो ह्येकमन्त्रा
जीवन्तु राजन्सुखिनः समृद्धाः ॥
iast:
dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ pāṇḍavānpālayantu
pāṇḍoḥ sutāstava putrāṃśca pāntu |
ekārimitrāḥ kuravo hyekamantrā
jīvantu rājansukhinaḥ samṛddhāḥ ||
english: Let Dhritarashtra's sons protect the Pandavas, and let Pandu's sons protect your sons. Let the Kurus, with one enemy and one friend and one counsel, live happy and prosperous, king.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura tells the king he is the pillar of the Kurus and urges him to protect the young Pandavas, worn by exile.
devanagari:
मेढीभूतः कौरवाणां त्वमद्य
त्वय्याधीनं कुरु कुलमाजमीढ ।
पार्थान्बालान्वनवास प्रतप्तान्
गोपायस्व स्वं यशस्तात रक्षन् ॥
iast:
meḍhībhūtaḥ kauravāṇāṃ tvamadya
tvayyādhīnaṃ kuru kulamājamīḍha |
pārthānbālānvanavāsa prataptān
gopāyasva svaṃ yaśastāta rakṣan ||
english: You are today the central post of the Kauravas; the Kuru family depends on you, descendant of Ajamidha. Protect the sons of Pritha, young and scorched by forest exile, and guard your own good name, dear one.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura urges the king to make peace between the Kauravas and the Pandavas, so enemies find no gap, and to restrain Duryodhana.
devanagari:
सन्धत्स्व त्वं कौरवान्पाण्डुपुत्रैर्
मा तेऽन्तरं रिपवः प्रार्थयन्तु ।
सत्ये स्थितास्ते नरदेव सर्वे
दुर्योधनं स्थापय त्वं नरेन्द्र ॥
iast:
sandhatsva tvaṃ kauravānpāṇḍuputrair
mā te'ntaraṃ ripavaḥ prārthayantu |
satye sthitāste naradeva sarve
duryodhanaṃ sthāpaya tvaṃ narendra ||
english: Make peace between the Kauravas and the sons of Pandu; do not let enemies look for a gap between you. They all stand in truth, god among men; restrain Duryodhana, lord of men.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura cites Manu's list of seventeen people who strike the sky with their fists, that is, act in vain (5.1-5.6).
devanagari:
सप्तदशेमान्राजेन्द्र मनुः स्वायम्भुवोऽब्रवीत् ।
वैचित्रवीर्य पुरुषानाकाशं मुष्टिभिर्घ्नतः ॥
iast:
saptadaśemānrājendra manuḥ svāyambhuvo'bravīt |
vaicitravīrya puruṣānākāśaṃ muṣṭibhirghnataḥ ||
english: Svayambhuva Manu, lord of kings, spoke of these seventeen people, son of Vichitravirya, who strike the sky with their fists,
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues: those who try to bend Indra's unbendable bow, or grasp the unbendable rays of light.
devanagari:
तानेविन्द्रस्य हि धनुरनाम्यं नमतोऽब्रवीत् ।
अथो मरीचिनः पादाननाम्यान्नमतस्तथा ॥
iast:
tānevindrasya hi dhanuranāmyaṃ namato'bravīt |
atho marīcinaḥ pādānanāmyānnamatastathā ||
english: who try to bend Indra's bow that cannot be bent, and to bend the rays of light that cannot be bent:
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists futile people: one who teaches the unteachable, the angry, one who courts an enemy, one who does not protect women, the beggar of the unbeggable and the boaster.
devanagari:
यश्चाशिष्यं शासति यश् च कुप्यते
यश्चातिवेलं भजते द्विषन्तम् ।
स्त्रियश्च योऽरक्षति भद्रमस्तु ते
यश्चायाच्यं याचति यश् च कत्थते ॥
iast:
yaścāśiṣyaṃ śāsati yaś ca kupyate
yaścātivelaṃ bhajate dviṣantam |
striyaśca yo'rakṣati bhadramastu te
yaścāyācyaṃ yācati yaś ca katthate ||
english: one who instructs the unteachable, one who gets angry, one who serves an enemy beyond measure, one who does not protect women, bless you, one who begs what should not be begged, and one who boasts;
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues: the well-born who does wrong, the weak always at war with the strong, one who speaks to the faithless, and one who wants the undesirable.
devanagari:
यश्चाभिजातः प्रकरोत्यकार्यं
यश्चाबलो बलिना नित्यवैरी ।
अश्रद्दधानाय च यो ब्रवीति
यश्चाकाम्यं कामयते नरेन्द्र ॥
iast:
yaścābhijātaḥ prakarotyakāryaṃ
yaścābalo balinā nityavairī |
aśraddadhānāya ca yo bravīti
yaścākāmyaṃ kāmayate narendra ||
english: one of good birth who does what should not be done, a weak man always at enmity with the strong, one who speaks to the faithless, and one who desires what should not be desired, lord of men;
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues the list with improper behaviour within families, in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
वध्वा हासं श्वशुरो यश् च मन्यते
वध्वा वसन्नुत यो मानकामः ।
परक्षेत्रे निर्वपति यश्च बीजं
स्त्रियं च यः परिवदतेऽतिवेलम् ॥
iast:
vadhvā hāsaṃ śvaśuro yaś ca manyate
vadhvā vasannuta yo mānakāmaḥ |
parakṣetre nirvapati yaśca bījaṃ
striyaṃ ca yaḥ parivadate'tivelam ||
english: a father-in-law who jokes with his daughter-in-law, one who lives with his daughter-in-law and wants honour, one who sows seed in another's field, and one who speaks ill of women beyond measure;
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura ends the list: one who denies receiving, one who boasts of giving when asked, one who flatters the wicked; these follow the wind, noose in hand.
devanagari:
यश्चैव लब्ध्वा न स्मरामीत्युवाच
दत्त्वा च यः कत्थति याच्यमानः ।
यश्चासतः सान्त्वमुपासतीह
एतेऽनुयान्त्यनिलं पाशहस्ताः ॥
iast:
yaścaiva labdhvā na smarāmītyuvāca
dattvā ca yaḥ katthati yācyamānaḥ |
yaścāsataḥ sāntvamupāsatīha
ete'nuyāntyanilaṃ pāśahastāḥ ||
english: one who, having received, says 'I do not remember'; one who, having given, boasts when asked; and one who courts the wicked with flattery: these follow the wind with nooses in their hands.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura states a rule of reciprocity: treat each person as they treat you; meet deceit with deceit and goodness with goodness.
devanagari:
यस्मिन्यथा वर्तते यो मनुष्यस्
तस्मिंस्तथा वर्तितव्यं स धर्मः ।
मायाचारो मायया वर्तितव्यः
साध्वाचारः साधुना प्रत्युदेयः ॥
iast:
yasminyathā vartate yo manuṣyas
tasmiṃstathā vartitavyaṃ sa dharmaḥ |
māyācāro māyayā vartitavyaḥ
sādhvācāraḥ sādhunā pratyudeyaḥ ||
english: As a person behaves towards someone, so should one behave towards them: that is dharma. A deceiver should be met with deceit; good conduct should be returned with goodness.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra asks why, if the Vedas say a person lives a hundred years, people do not reach that span.
devanagari:
शतायुरुक्तः पुरुषः सर्ववेदेषु वै यदा ।
नाप्नोत्यथ च तत्सर्वमायुः केनेह हेतुना ॥
iast:
śatāyuruktaḥ puruṣaḥ sarvavedeṣu vai yadā |
nāpnotyatha ca tatsarvamāyuḥ keneha hetunā ||
english: When a person is said in all the Vedas to live a hundred years, why does he not reach that whole life here?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names six things that cut life short: excessive talk, excessive pride, stinginess, anger, selfishness and betraying friends.
devanagari:
अतिवादोऽतिमानश्च तथात्यागो नराधिपः ।
क्रोधश्चातिविवित्सा च मित्रद्रोहश्च तानि षट् ॥
iast:
ativādo'timānaśca tathātyāgo narādhipaḥ |
krodhaścātivivitsā ca mitradrohaśca tāni ṣaṭ ||
english: Excessive speech, excessive pride, lack of generosity, anger, excessive self-seeking and betraying friends: these are the six, lord of men.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says these six, not death, are the sharp swords that cut short people's lives.
devanagari:
एत एवासयस्तीक्ष्णाः कृन्तन्त्यायूंषि देहिनाम् ।
एतानि मानवान्घ्नन्ति न मृत्युर्भद्रमस्तु ते ॥
iast:
eta evāsayastīkṣṇāḥ kṛntantyāyūṃṣi dehinām |
etāni mānavānghnanti na mṛtyurbhadramastu te ||
english: These are the sharp swords that cut short the lives of embodied beings. These kill people, not death; bless you.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names grave wrongdoers in the terms of his time, including adultery with a trusting friend's wife.
devanagari:
विश्वस्तस्यैति यो दारान्यश्चापि गुरु तक्पगः ।
वृषली पतिर्द्विजो यश्च पानपश्चैव भारत ॥
iast:
viśvastasyaiti yo dārānyaścāpi guru takpagaḥ |
vṛṣalī patirdvijo yaśca pānapaścaiva bhārata ||
english: One who goes to the wife of a man who trusts him, one who violates his teacher's bed, a twice-born man who marries a shudra woman, and a drinker, Bharata,
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says these, and one who kills a refugee, equal a brahmin-killer and need atonement.
devanagari:
शरणागतहा चैव सर्वे ब्रह्महणैः समाः ।
एतैः समेत्य कर्तव्यं प्रायश्चित्तमिति श्रुतिः ॥
iast:
śaraṇāgatahā caiva sarve brahmahaṇaiḥ samāḥ |
etaiḥ sametya kartavyaṃ prāyaścittamiti śrutiḥ ||
english: and one who kills a refugee: all are equal to killers of brahmins. Scripture says that having fallen in with these, one must do atonement.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise householder who is generous, honest in speech, non-violent, grateful, truthful and gentle reaches heaven.
devanagari:
गृही वदान्योऽनपविद्ध वाक्यः
शेषान्न भोकाप्यविहिंसकश् च ।
नानर्थकृत्त्यक्तकलिः कृतज्ञः
सत्यो मृदुः स्वर्गमुपैति विद्वान् ॥
iast:
gṛhī vadānyo'napaviddha vākyaḥ
śeṣānna bhokāpyavihiṃsakaś ca |
nānarthakṛttyaktakaliḥ kṛtajñaḥ
satyo mṛduḥ svargamupaiti vidvān ||
english: The wise householder who is generous, whose word is not set aside, who eats what is left after others and does no harm, who does no mischief, has given up quarrels, is grateful, truthful and gentle, reaches heaven.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says people who speak pleasantly are easy to find, but rare are those who speak, or hear, unpleasant truths that do good.
devanagari:
सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन्सततं प्रियवादिनः ।
अप्रियस्य तु पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः ॥
iast:
sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājansatataṃ priyavādinaḥ |
apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ ||
english: People who always speak pleasantly are easy to find, king; but rare are both the speaker and the hearer of what is unpleasant yet beneficial.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a ruler has a true ally in one who, relying on dharma, says what is unpleasant but beneficial regardless of the master's likes.
devanagari:
यो हि धर्मं व्यपाश्रित्य हित्वा भर्तुः प्रियाप्रिये ।
अप्रियाण्याह पथ्यानि तेन राजा सहायवान् ॥
iast:
yo hi dharmaṃ vyapāśritya hitvā bhartuḥ priyāpriye |
apriyāṇyāha pathyāni tena rājā sahāyavān ||
english: One who, relying on dharma and setting aside his master's likes and dislikes, speaks unpleasant but beneficial words: through him a king has a true ally.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura states an order of priorities: give up one person for the family, the family for the village, the village for the country, the world for the self.
devanagari:
त्यजेत्कुलार्थे पुरुषं ग्रामस्यार्थे कुलं त्यजेत् ।
ग्रामं जनपदस्यार्थे आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत् ॥
iast:
tyajetkulārthe puruṣaṃ grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet |
grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet ||
english: One should give up a person for the sake of the family, a family for the sake of the village, a village for the sake of the country, and the earth for the sake of the self.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises keeping wealth for emergencies and protecting oneself above all, in the terms of his time regarding wives.
devanagari:
आपदर्थं धनं रक्षेद्दारान्रक्षेद्धनैरपि ।
आत्मानं सततं रक्षेद्दारैरपि धनैरपि ॥
iast:
āpadarthaṃ dhanaṃ rakṣeddārānrakṣeddhanairapi |
ātmānaṃ satataṃ rakṣeddārairapi dhanairapi ||
english: One should guard wealth against misfortune; guard one's wife even with wealth; and always guard oneself, even with wife and wealth.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura reminds the king that his warning at the dice game was unwelcome to him, like medicine to a sick man.
devanagari:
उक्तं मया द्यूतकालेऽपि राजन्
नैवं युक्तं वचनं प्रातिपीय ।
तदौषधं पथ्यमिवातुरस्य
न रोचते तव वैचित्र वीर्य ॥
iast:
uktaṃ mayā dyūtakāle'pi rājan
naivaṃ yuktaṃ vacanaṃ prātipīya |
tadauṣadhaṃ pathyamivāturasya
na rocate tava vaicitra vīrya ||
english: I said at the time of the dice game, king, that this was not right. But like medicine to a sick man, that beneficial advice did not please you, son of Vichitravirya.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the king has defeated the peacock-like Pandavas with crow-like sons, abandoning lions for jackals, and will grieve.
devanagari:
काकैरिमांश्चित्रबर्हान्मयूरान्
पराजैष्ठाः पाण्डवान्धार्तराष्ट्रैः ।
हित्वा सिंहान्क्रोष्टु कान्गूहमानः
प्राप्ते काले शोचिता त्वं नरेन्द्र ॥
iast:
kākairimāṃścitrabarhānmayūrān
parājaiṣṭhāḥ pāṇḍavāndhārtarāṣṭraiḥ |
hitvā siṃhānkroṣṭu kāngūhamānaḥ
prāpte kāle śocitā tvaṃ narendra ||
english: You have defeated these bright-plumed peacocks, the Pandavas, with crows, Dhritarashtra's sons. Abandoning lions and hiding jackals, you will grieve when the time comes, lord of men.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says servants trust and stand by a master who never grows angry with a devoted servant working for his good.
devanagari:
यस्तात न क्रुध्यति सर्वकालं
भृत्यस्य भक्तस्य हिते रतस्य ।
तस्मिन्भृत्या भर्तरि विश्वसन्ति
न चैनमापत्सु परित्यजन्ति ॥
iast:
yastāta na krudhyati sarvakālaṃ
bhṛtyasya bhaktasya hite ratasya |
tasminbhṛtyā bhartari viśvasanti
na cainamāpatsu parityajanti ||
english: Dear one, servants trust a master who is never angry with a servant who is devoted and intent on his good, and they do not abandon him in hard times.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns against cutting loyal staff's livelihood to take on new outsiders; deprived, even loyal people leave.
devanagari:
न भृत्यानां वृत्ति संरोधनेन
बाह्यं जनं सञ्जिघृक्षेदपूर्वम् ।
त्यजन्ति ह्येनमुचितावरुद्धाः
स्निग्धा ह्यमात्याः परिहीनभोगाः ॥
iast:
na bhṛtyānāṃ vṛtti saṃrodhanena
bāhyaṃ janaṃ sañjighṛkṣedapūrvam |
tyajanti hyenamucitāvaruddhāḥ
snigdhā hyamātyāḥ parihīnabhogāḥ ||
english: One should not try to win over new outsiders by cutting off the livelihood of one's servants; deprived of what is due, even affectionate ministers abandon him.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises first reckoning all tasks, income, expenses and fair pay, then gathering suitable helpers, since hard tasks need help.
devanagari:
कृत्यानि पूर्वं परिसङ्ख्याय सर्वाण्य्
आयव्ययावनुरूपां च वृत्तिम् ।
सङ्गृह्णीयादनुरूपान्सहायान्
सहायसाध्यानि हि दुष्कराणि ॥
iast:
kṛtyāni pūrvaṃ parisaṅkhyāya sarvāṇy
āyavyayāvanurūpāṃ ca vṛttim |
saṅgṛhṇīyādanurūpānsahāyān
sahāyasādhyāni hi duṣkarāṇi ||
english: Having first reckoned up all the tasks, income and expenditure, and a fitting livelihood, one should gather suitable helpers; for difficult things are achieved with helpers.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a devoted helper who knows his master's mind, works tirelessly and speaks for his good deserves to be cherished like oneself.
devanagari:
अभिप्रायं यो विदित्वा तु भर्तुः
सर्वाणि कार्याणि करोत्यतन्द्रीः ।
वक्ता हितानामनुरक्त आर्यः
शक्तिज्ञ आत्मेव हि सोऽनुकम्प्यः ॥
iast:
abhiprāyaṃ yo viditvā tu bhartuḥ
sarvāṇi kāryāṇi karotyatandrīḥ |
vaktā hitānāmanurakta āryaḥ
śaktijña ātmeva hi so'nukampyaḥ ||
english: One who, knowing his master's intention, does all tasks without weariness, speaks what is good for him, is devoted, noble and knows his own strength, deserves compassion as one's own self.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a servant who ignores instruction, argues when assigned, and is proud of his own cleverness should be let go quickly.
devanagari:
वाक्यं तु यो नाद्रियतेऽनुशिष्टः
प्रत्याह यश्चापि नियुज्यमानः ।
प्रज्ञाभिमानी प्रतिकूलवादी
त्याज्यः स तादृक्त्वरयैव भृत्यः ॥
iast:
vākyaṃ tu yo nādriyate'nuśiṣṭaḥ
pratyāha yaścāpi niyujyamānaḥ |
prajñābhimānī pratikūlavādī
tyājyaḥ sa tādṛktvarayaiva bhṛtyaḥ ||
english: A servant who does not heed words when instructed, who answers back when assigned, who is proud of his intellect and contrary in speech, should be let go quickly.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists the eight qualities of a good envoy: not arrogant, not timid, not slow, compassionate, gentle, incorruptible, healthy and eloquent.
devanagari:
अस्तब्धमक्लीबमदीर्घसूत्रं
सानुक्रोशं श्लक्ष्णमहार्यमन्यैः ।
अरोग जातीयमुदारवाक्यं
दूतं वदन्त्यष्ट गुणोपपन्नम् ॥
iast:
astabdhamaklībamadīrghasūtraṃ
sānukrośaṃ ślakṣṇamahāryamanyaiḥ |
aroga jātīyamudāravākyaṃ
dūtaṃ vadantyaṣṭa guṇopapannam ||
english: Not stubborn, not timid, not slow, compassionate, gentle, not to be won over by others, of healthy stock and eloquent: they call such an envoy endowed with eight qualities.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura gives practical cautions: do not enter another's house at odd hours out of trust, linger at crossroads at night, or court a royal woman.
devanagari:
न विश्वासाज्जातु परस्य गेहं
गच्छेन्नरश्चेतयानो विकाले ।
न चत्वरे निशि तिष्ठेन्निगूढो
न राजन्यां योषितं प्रार्थयीत ॥
iast:
na viśvāsājjātu parasya gehaṃ
gacchennaraścetayāno vikāle |
na catvare niśi tiṣṭhennigūḍho
na rājanyāṃ yoṣitaṃ prārthayīta ||
english: A careful person should never go to another's house at an odd hour out of trust, nor stand hidden at a crossroads at night, nor court a woman of the royal household.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises not contradicting a powerful man surrounded by bad company, nor saying 'I do not trust you', but giving a reason or excuse instead.
devanagari:
न निह्नवं सत्र गतस्य गच्छेत्
संसृष्ट मन्त्रस्य कुसङ्गतस्य ।
न च ब्रूयान्नाश्वसामि त्वयीति
स कारणं व्यपदेशं तु कुर्यात् ॥
iast:
na nihnavaṃ satra gatasya gacchet
saṃsṛṣṭa mantrasya kusaṅgatasya |
na ca brūyānnāśvasāmi tvayīti
sa kāraṇaṃ vyapadeśaṃ tu kuryāt ||
english: One should not contradict a man sitting in an assembly whose counsel is mixed with bad company; nor should one say 'I do not trust you', but should give a reason or excuse.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists people to avoid in business dealings, including stereotypes about certain women.
devanagari:
घृणी राजा पुंश्चली राजभृत्यः
पुत्रो भ्राता विधवा बाल पुत्रा ।
सेना जीवी चोद्धृत भक्त एव
व्यवहारे वै वर्जनीयाः स्युरेते ॥
iast:
ghṛṇī rājā puṃścalī rājabhṛtyaḥ
putro bhrātā vidhavā bāla putrā |
senā jīvī coddhṛta bhakta eva
vyavahāre vai varjanīyāḥ syurete ||
english: A compassionate king, a loose woman, a king's servant, a son, a brother, a widow with a young son, one who lives by soldiering, and one who has lost his position: these should be avoided in transactions.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists the benefits of regular bathing, ending with a remark about women in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
गुणा दश स्नानशीलं भजन्ते
बलं रूपं स्वरवर्णप्रशुद्धिः ।
स्पर्शश्च गन्धश्च विशुद्धता च
श्रीः सौकुमार्यं प्रवराश्च नार्यः ॥
iast:
guṇā daśa snānaśīlaṃ bhajante
balaṃ rūpaṃ svaravarṇapraśuddhiḥ |
sparśaśca gandhaśca viśuddhatā ca
śrīḥ saukumāryaṃ pravarāśca nāryaḥ ||
english: Ten benefits come to one who bathes regularly: strength, beauty, a clear voice and complexion, softness of touch, fragrance, purity, fortune, delicacy, and the finest women.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who eats moderately gains health, long life, happiness, strength and healthy children, and no one calls him a glutton.
devanagari:
गुणाश्च षण्मितभुक्तं भजन्ते
आरोग्यमायुश्च सुखं बलं च ।
अनाविलं चास्य भवेदपत्यं
न चैनमाद्यून इति क्षिपन्ति ॥
iast:
guṇāśca ṣaṇmitabhuktaṃ bhajante
ārogyamāyuśca sukhaṃ balaṃ ca |
anāvilaṃ cāsya bhavedapatyaṃ
na cainamādyūna iti kṣipanti ||
english: Six benefits come to one who eats moderately: health, long life, happiness and strength; his children are healthy, and no one mocks him as a glutton.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises not to house the idle, the gluttonous, the hated, the deceitful, the cruel, those without tact, and the indecently dressed.
devanagari:
अकर्म शीलं च महाशनं च
लोकद्विष्टं बहु मायं नृशंसम् ।
अदेशकालज्ञमनिष्ट वेषम्
एतान्गृहे न प्रतिवासयीत ॥
iast:
akarma śīlaṃ ca mahāśanaṃ ca
lokadviṣṭaṃ bahu māyaṃ nṛśaṃsam |
adeśakālajñamaniṣṭa veṣam
etāngṛhe na prativāsayīta ||
english: One who is idle, a glutton, hated by people, very deceitful, cruel, ignorant of place and time, and improperly dressed: one should not let these live in one's house.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises never begging, even in distress, from the miserly, the abusive, the ignorant, the base, the vain, the cruel, the vengeful or the ungrateful.
devanagari:
कदर्यमाक्रोशकमश्रुतं च
वराक सम्भूतममान्य मानिनम् ।
निष्ठूरिणं कृतवैरं कृतघ्नम्
एतान्भृतार्तोऽपि न जातु याचेत् ॥
iast:
kadaryamākrośakamaśrutaṃ ca
varāka sambhūtamamānya māninam |
niṣṭhūriṇaṃ kṛtavairaṃ kṛtaghnam
etānbhṛtārto'pi na jātu yācet ||
english: A miser, an abuser, the unlearned, the base-born who honours the dishonourable, the harsh, one who has made enemies, and the ungrateful: one should never beg from these, even in distress.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names six base people not to serve: those of troubled deeds, slanderers, constant liars, the unfaithful, the passion-driven and the vain.
devanagari:
सङ्क्लिष्टकर्माणमतिप्रवादं
नित्यानृतं चादृढ भक्तिकं च ।
विकृष्टरागं बहुमानिनं चाप्य्
एतान्न सेवेत नराधमान्षट् ॥
iast:
saṅkliṣṭakarmāṇamatipravādaṃ
nityānṛtaṃ cādṛḍha bhaktikaṃ ca |
vikṛṣṭarāgaṃ bahumāninaṃ cāpy
etānna seveta narādhamānṣaṭ ||
english: One of corrupt deeds, a slanderer, one always lying, one of unsteady devotion, one without affection, and one very conceited: one should not serve these six lowest of people.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says goals depend on helpers and helpers depend on means; each needs the other to succeed.
devanagari:
सहायबन्धना ह्यर्थाः सहायाश्चार्थबन्धनाः ।
अन्योन्यबन्धनावेतौ विनान्योन्यं न सिध्यतः ॥
iast:
sahāyabandhanā hyarthāḥ sahāyāścārthabandhanāḥ |
anyonyabandhanāvetau vinānyonyaṃ na sidhyataḥ ||
english: Aims are bound to helpers, and helpers are bound to means; these two are bound to each other, and neither succeeds without the other.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises that, after raising sons, clearing debts, providing for them and settling daughters, one should seek to live as a sage in the forest.
devanagari:
उत्पाद्य पुत्राननृणांश्च कृत्वा
वृत्तिं च तेभ्योऽनुविधाय कां चित् ।
स्थाने कुमारीः प्रतिपाद्य सर्वा
अरण्यसंस्थो मुनिवद्बुभूषेत् ॥
iast:
utpādya putrānanṛṇāṃśca kṛtvā
vṛttiṃ ca tebhyo'nuvidhāya kāṃ cit |
sthāne kumārīḥ pratipādya sarvā
araṇyasaṃstho munivadbubhūṣet ||
english: Having fathered sons and freed them from debt, having arranged some livelihood for them, and having given all daughters in marriage properly, one should wish to live in the forest as a sage.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one should do what is good for all beings and brings happiness to oneself; this is the root of success in dharma and true benefit.
devanagari:
हितं यत्सर्वभूतानामात्मनश्च सुखावहम् ।
तत्कुर्यादीश्वरो ह्येतन्मूलं धर्मार्थसिद्धये ॥
iast:
hitaṃ yatsarvabhūtānāmātmanaśca sukhāvaham |
tatkuryādīśvaro hyetanmūlaṃ dharmārthasiddhaye ||
english: What is beneficial to all beings and brings happiness to oneself, the lord should do; this is the root of success in dharma and true benefit.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who has intelligence, influence, energy, strength, enterprise and resolve need not fear lacking a livelihood.
devanagari:
बुद्धिः प्रभावस्तेजश्च सत्त्वमुत्थानमेव च ।
व्यवसायश्च यस्य स्यात्तस्यावृत्ति भयं कुतः ॥
iast:
buddhiḥ prabhāvastejaśca sattvamutthānameva ca |
vyavasāyaśca yasya syāttasyāvṛtti bhayaṃ kutaḥ ||
english: One who has intelligence, influence, energy, strength, enterprise and resolve: where is his fear of having no livelihood?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura urges the king to see the evils of war with the Pandavas: enmity with sons, constant anxiety, lost fame and enemies' joy.
devanagari:
पश्य दोषान्पाण्डवैर्विग्रहे त्वं
यत्र व्यथेरन्नपि देवाः स शक्राः ।
पुत्रैर्वैरं नित्यमुद्विग्नवासो
यशः प्रणाशो द्विषतां च हर्षः ॥
iast:
paśya doṣānpāṇḍavairvigrahe tvaṃ
yatra vyatherannapi devāḥ sa śakrāḥ |
putrairvairaṃ nityamudvignavāso
yaśaḥ praṇāśo dviṣatāṃ ca harṣaḥ ||
english: See the evils in a conflict with the Pandavas, at which even the gods with Indra would tremble: enmity with your sons, living in constant anxiety, loss of fame and the joy of enemies.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns that the anger of Bhishma, the king, Drona and Yudhishthira could destroy the world like a comet.
devanagari:
भीष्मस्य कोपस्तव चेन्द्र कल्प
द्रोणस्य राज्ञश्च युधिष्ठिरस्य ।
उत्सादयेल्लोकमिमं प्रवृद्धः
श्वेतो ग्रहस्तिर्यगिवापतन्खे ॥
iast:
bhīṣmasya kopastava cendra kalpa
droṇasya rājñaśca yudhiṣṭhirasya |
utsādayellokamimaṃ pravṛddhaḥ
śveto grahastiryagivāpatankhe ||
english: The anger of Bhishma, of you who are like Indra, of Drona and of King Yudhishthira, once roused, could destroy this world, like a white comet falling across the sky.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the king's hundred sons, Karna and the five Pandavas together could rule the whole earth.
devanagari:
तव पुत्रशतं चैव कर्णः पञ्च च पाण्डवाः ।
पृथिवीमनुशासेयुरखिलां सागराम्बराम् ॥
iast:
tava putraśataṃ caiva karṇaḥ pañca ca pāṇḍavāḥ |
pṛthivīmanuśāseyurakhilāṃ sāgarāmbarām ||
english: Your hundred sons, Karna and the five Pandavas could together rule the whole earth, clothed by the ocean.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the Kauravas are the forest and the Pandavas its tigers: do not cut the forest with its tigers, nor drive the tigers out.
devanagari:
धार्तराष्ट्रा वनं राजन्व्याघ्राः पाण्डुसुता मताः ।
मा वनं छिन्धि स व्याघ्रं मा व्याघ्रान्नीनशो वनात् ॥
iast:
dhārtarāṣṭrā vanaṃ rājanvyāghrāḥ pāṇḍusutā matāḥ |
mā vanaṃ chindhi sa vyāghraṃ mā vyāghrānnīnaśo vanāt ||
english: Dhritarashtra's sons are a forest, king, and Pandu's sons are held to be the tigers. Do not cut down the forest with its tigers; do not drive the tigers out of the forest.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura explains: the forest and tigers protect each other, as the two families should.
devanagari:
न स्याद्वनमृते व्याघ्रान्व्याघ्रा न स्युरृते वनम् ।
वनं हि रक्ष्यते व्याघ्रैर्व्याघ्रान्रक्षति काननम् ॥
iast:
na syādvanamṛte vyāghrānvyāghrā na syurṛte vanam |
vanaṃ hi rakṣyate vyāghrairvyāghrānrakṣati kānanam ||
english: There is no forest without tigers, and no tigers without a forest. The forest is protected by the tigers, and the tigers are protected by the forest.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wicked are less eager to know others' virtues than to know their faults.
devanagari:
न तथेच्छन्त्यकल्याणाः परेषां वेदितुं गुणान् ।
यथैषां ज्ञातुमिच्छन्ति नैर्गुण्यं पापचेतसः ॥
iast:
na tathecchantyakalyāṇāḥ pareṣāṃ vedituṃ guṇān |
yathaiṣāṃ jñātumicchanti nairguṇyaṃ pāpacetasaḥ ||
english: The ill-natured do not wish to learn others' virtues as much as the evil-minded wish to learn their faults.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who wants the greatest success should practise dharma from the start, for wealth never departs from dharma.
devanagari:
अर्थसिद्धिं परामिच्छन्धर्ममेवादितश् चरेत् ।
न हि धर्मादपैत्यर्थः स्वर्गलोकादिवामृतम् ॥
iast:
arthasiddhiṃ parāmicchandharmamevāditaś caret |
na hi dharmādapaityarthaḥ svargalokādivāmṛtam ||
english: Wishing for the highest success in one's aims, one should practise dharma from the very beginning; for wealth does not depart from dharma, as nectar does not depart from heaven.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one whose mind has turned from wrong and is set on the good understands everything, nature and its changes.
devanagari:
यस्यात्मा विरतः पापात्कल्याणे च निवेशितः ।
तेन सर्वमिदं बुद्धं प्रकृतिर्विकृतिर्श्च या ॥
iast:
yasyātmā virataḥ pāpātkalyāṇe ca niveśitaḥ |
tena sarvamidaṃ buddhaṃ prakṛtirvikṛtirśca yā ||
english: One whose self has turned away from wrong and is set on the good has understood all this, both nature and its changes.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who pursues dharma, wealth and pleasure each at the right time finds all three together, here and hereafter.
devanagari:
यो धर्ममर्थं कामं च यथाकालं निषेवते ।
धर्मार्थकामसंयोगं योऽमुत्रेह च विन्दति ॥
iast:
yo dharmamarthaṃ kāmaṃ ca yathākālaṃ niṣevate |
dharmārthakāmasaṃyogaṃ yo'mutreha ca vindati ||
english: One who pursues dharma, wealth and pleasure each at its proper time gains the union of dharma, wealth and pleasure, both hereafter and here.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who restrains the rising force of anger and excitement, and is not confused in trouble, is fit for fortune.
devanagari:
संनियच्छति यो वेगमुत्थितं क्रोधहर्षयोः ।
स श्रियो भाजनं राजन्यश्चापत्सु न मुह्यति ॥
iast:
saṃniyacchati yo vegamutthitaṃ krodhaharṣayoḥ |
sa śriyo bhājanaṃ rājanyaścāpatsu na muhyati ||
english: One who restrains the rising force of anger and elation, and is not bewildered in misfortune, is a vessel of good fortune, king.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names five kinds of strength, of which strength of arm is the least (5.48-5.51).
devanagari:
बलं पञ्च विधं नित्यं पुरुषाणां निबोध मे ।
यत्तु बाहुबलं नाम कनिष्ठं बलमुच्यते ॥
iast:
balaṃ pañca vidhaṃ nityaṃ puruṣāṇāṃ nibodha me |
yattu bāhubalaṃ nāma kaniṣṭhaṃ balamucyate ||
english: Learn from me the five kinds of strength people always have. What is called strength of arm is said to be the lowest strength.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues: gaining good counsellors is the second strength; gaining wealth, the third.
devanagari:
अमात्यलाभो भद्रं ते द्वितीयं बलमुच्यते ।
धनलाभस्तृतीयं तु बलमाहुर्जिगीषवः ॥
iast:
amātyalābho bhadraṃ te dvitīyaṃ balamucyate |
dhanalābhastṛtīyaṃ tu balamāhurjigīṣavaḥ ||
english: Gaining ministers, bless you, is called the second strength; gaining wealth, those who seek victory call the third strength.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues: the strength of birth, inherited from ancestors, is the fourth.
devanagari:
यत्त्वस्य सहजं राजन्पितृपैतामहं बलम् ।
अभिजात बलं नाम तच्चतुर्थं बलं स्मृतम् ॥
iast:
yattvasya sahajaṃ rājanpitṛpaitāmahaṃ balam |
abhijāta balaṃ nāma taccaturthaṃ balaṃ smṛtam ||
english: The natural strength, king, that comes from father and grandfather, called strength of birth, is remembered as the fourth strength.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the strength of wisdom, which gathers all the others, is the best of all strengths.
devanagari:
येन त्वेतानि सर्वाणि सङ्गृहीतानि भारत ।
यद्बलानां बलं श्रेष्ठं तत्प्रज्ञा बलमुच्यते ॥
iast:
yena tvetāni sarvāṇi saṅgṛhītāni bhārata |
yadbalānāṃ balaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tatprajñā balamucyate ||
english: But the strength by which all these are gathered together, Bharata, the best of all strengths, is called the strength of wisdom.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns: having made an enemy of someone able to do you great harm, do not feel safe because you are far away.
devanagari:
महते योऽपकाराय नरस्य प्रभवेन्नरः ।
तेन वैरं समासज्य दूरस्थोऽस्मीति नाश्वसेत् ॥
iast:
mahate yo'pakārāya narasya prabhavennaraḥ |
tena vairaṃ samāsajya dūrastho'smīti nāśvaset ||
english: Having made an enemy of a person able to do one great harm, one should not feel secure thinking 'I am far away'.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists things a wise person would not trust, including women, kings and snakes, in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
स्त्रीषु राजसु सर्पेषु स्वाध्याये शत्रुसेविषु ।
भोगे चायुषि विश्वासं कः प्राज्ञः कर्तुमर्हति ॥
iast:
strīṣu rājasu sarpeṣu svādhyāye śatruseviṣu |
bhoge cāyuṣi viśvāsaṃ kaḥ prājñaḥ kartumarhati ||
english: In women, kings and snakes, in one's own learning, in those who serve the enemy, in enjoyment and in life itself: what wise person would place trust?
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says for one struck by the arrow of wisdom, no doctor, medicine, ritual or charm can help.
devanagari:
प्रज्ञा शरेणाभिहतस्य जन्तोश्
चिकित्सकाः सन्ति न चौषधानि ।
न होममन्त्रा न च मङ्गलानि
नाथर्वणा नाप्यगदाः सुसिद्धाः ॥
iast:
prajñā śareṇābhihatasya jantoś
cikitsakāḥ santi na cauṣadhāni |
na homamantrā na ca maṅgalāni
nātharvaṇā nāpyagadāḥ susiddhāḥ ||
english: For a creature struck by the arrow of wisdom there are no physicians and no medicines, no sacrificial chants or blessings, no Atharvan spells nor well-made antidotes.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a snake, fire, a lion and a son of good family should never be underestimated, being full of power.
devanagari:
सर्पश्चाग्निश्च सिंहश्च कुलपुत्रश्च भारत ।
नावज्ञेया मनुष्येण सर्वे ते ह्यतितेजसः ॥
iast:
sarpaścāgniśca siṃhaśca kulaputraśca bhārata |
nāvajñeyā manuṣyeṇa sarve te hyatitejasaḥ ||
english: A snake, fire, a lion and a son of noble family, Bharata: none of these should be despised by a person, for all of them are full of power.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says fire, the great energy in the world, lies hidden in wood and does not consume it until kindled by others.
devanagari:
अग्निस्तेजो महल्लोके गूढस्तिष्ठति दारुषु ।
न चोपयुङ्क्ते तद्दारु यावन्नो दीप्यते परैः ॥
iast:
agnistejo mahalloke gūḍhastiṣṭhati dāruṣu |
na copayuṅkte taddāru yāvanno dīpyate paraiḥ ||
english: Fire, a great energy in the world, lies hidden in wood, and does not consume that wood until it is kindled by others.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues: once kindled by friction, that fire burns the wood and the whole forest.
devanagari:
स एव खलु दारुभ्यो यदा निर्मथ्य दीप्यते ।
तदा तच्च वनं चान्यन्निर्दहत्याशु तेजसा ॥
iast:
sa eva khalu dārubhyo yadā nirmathya dīpyate |
tadā tacca vanaṃ cānyannirdahatyāśu tejasā ||
english: But when it is kindled from that wood by churning, it quickly burns that wood and the rest of the forest with its energy.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says people of good family with fire-like energy lie calm and forbearing, like fire in wood, until provoked.
devanagari:
एवमेव कुले जाताः पावकोपम तेजसः ।
क्षमावन्तो निराकाराः काष्ठेऽग्निरिव शेरते ॥
iast:
evameva kule jātāḥ pāvakopama tejasaḥ |
kṣamāvanto nirākārāḥ kāṣṭhe'gniriva śerate ||
english: So those born in noble families, with energy like fire, forbearing and showing no sign, lie quiet like fire in wood.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the king and his sons are a creeper and the Pandavas the great tree; a creeper never grows without a tree's support.
devanagari:
लता धर्मा त्वं सपुत्रः शालाः पाण्डुसुता मताः ।
न लता वर्धते जातु महाद्रुममनाश्रिता ॥
iast:
latā dharmā tvaṃ saputraḥ śālāḥ pāṇḍusutā matāḥ |
na latā vardhate jātu mahādrumamanāśritā ||
english: You and your sons are a creeper, and Pandu's sons are held to be great sal trees. A creeper never grows without leaning on a great tree.
