licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura repeats: the king and his sons are the forest and the Pandavas its lions; each perishes without the other.
devanagari:
वनं राजंस्त्वं सपुत्रोऽम्बिकेय
सिंहान्वने पाण्डवांस्तात विद्धि ।
सिंहैर्विहीनं हि वनं विनश्येत्
सिंहा विनश्येयुरृते वनेन ॥
iast:
vanaṃ rājaṃstvaṃ saputro'mbikeya
siṃhānvane pāṇḍavāṃstāta viddhi |
siṃhairvihīnaṃ hi vanaṃ vinaśyet
siṃhā vinaśyeyurṛte vanena ||
english: You and your sons, son of Ambika, are the forest; know the Pandavas, dear one, as the lions in it. A forest without lions perishes, and lions perish without a forest.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a young person's life-breath rises when an elder approaches and settles again when he rises and greets them.
devanagari:
ऊर्ध्वं प्राणा ह्युत्क्रामन्ति यूनः स्थविर आयति ।
प्रत्युत्थानाभिवादाभ्यां पुनस्तान्पतिपद्यते ॥
iast:
ūrdhvaṃ prāṇā hyutkrāmanti yūnaḥ sthavira āyati |
pratyutthānābhivādābhyāṃ punastānpatipadyate ||
english: The life-breaths of a young person rise up when an elder approaches; by rising and greeting him, he regains them.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura describes welcoming a good guest: give a seat, bring water, wash his feet, ask after his welfare, then offer food.
devanagari:
पीठं दत्त्वा साधवेऽभ्यागताय
आनीयापः परिनिर्णिज्य पादौ ।
सुखं पृष्ट्वा प्रतिवेद्यात्म संस्थं
ततो दद्यादन्नमवेक्ष्य धीरः ॥
iast:
pīṭhaṃ dattvā sādhave'bhyāgatāya
ānīyāpaḥ parinirṇijya pādau |
sukhaṃ pṛṣṭvā prativedyātma saṃsthaṃ
tato dadyādannamavekṣya dhīraḥ ||
english: Having given a seat to a good person who has come, bringing water and washing his feet, asking after his well-being and telling of one's own, the steady person should then give food, with care.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the noble call a life useless when a learned guest refuses a host's offerings because of the host's greed, fear or meanness.
devanagari:
यस्योदकं मधुपर्कं च गां च
न मन्त्रवित्प्रतिगृह्णाति गेहे ।
लोभाद्भयादर्थकार्पण्यतो वा
तस्यानर्थं जीवितमाहुरार्याः ॥
iast:
yasyodakaṃ madhuparkaṃ ca gāṃ ca
na mantravitpratigṛhṇāti gehe |
lobhādbhayādarthakārpaṇyato vā
tasyānarthaṃ jīvitamāhurāryāḥ ||
english: When a learned guest will not accept water, honey-drink and a cow in someone's house because of the host's greed, fear or miserliness, the noble say that person's life is useless.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists guests not to be honoured with water, reflecting his time's prejudices against certain occupations.
devanagari:
चिकित्सकः शक्य कर्तावकीर्णी
स्तेनः क्रूरो मद्यपो भ्रूणहा च ।
सेनाजीवी श्रुतिविक्रायकश् च
भृशं प्रियोऽप्यतिथिर्नोदकार्हः ॥
iast:
cikitsakaḥ śakya kartāvakīrṇī
stenaḥ krūro madyapo bhrūṇahā ca |
senājīvī śrutivikrāyakaś ca
bhṛśaṃ priyo'pyatithirnodakārhaḥ ||
english: A physician, a surgeon, one who has broken his vow of celibacy, a thief, a cruel person, a drinker, one who kills embryos, one who lives by soldiering, and one who sells the Veda: however dear, such a guest is not worthy of water.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists things not to be sold, from salt and cooked food to honey, oil and red cloth.
devanagari:
अविक्रेयं लवणं पक्वमन्नं दधि
क्षीरं मधु तैलं घृतं च ।
तिला मांसं मूलफलानि शाकं
रक्तं वासः सर्वगन्धा गुडश् च ॥
iast:
avikreyaṃ lavaṇaṃ pakvamannaṃ dadhi
kṣīraṃ madhu tailaṃ ghṛtaṃ ca |
tilā māṃsaṃ mūlaphalāni śākaṃ
raktaṃ vāsaḥ sarvagandhā guḍaś ca ||
english: Not to be sold are salt, cooked food, curd, milk, honey, oil and ghee, sesame, meat, roots and fruits, vegetables, red cloth, all perfumes and jaggery.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura describes the true mendicant: without anger, treating gold and clay alike, free of grief, beyond blame and praise.
devanagari:
अरोषणो यः समलोष्ट काञ्चनः
प्रहीण शोको गतसन्धि विग्रहः ।
निन्दा प्रशंसोपरतः प्रियाप्रिये
चरन्नुदासीनवदेष भिक्षुकः ॥
iast:
aroṣaṇo yaḥ samaloṣṭa kāñcanaḥ
prahīṇa śoko gatasandhi vigrahaḥ |
nindā praśaṃsoparataḥ priyāpriye
carannudāsīnavadeṣa bhikṣukaḥ ||
english: One who is free of anger, to whom a clod and gold are the same, who has left grief behind, is beyond alliance and conflict, has stopped caring for blame and praise, and moves among the pleasant and unpleasant as if indifferent: this is a mendicant.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura describes the forest ascetic: living on wild grains, roots and greens, self-controlled, careful with guests.
devanagari:
नीवार मूलेङ्गुद शाकवृत्तिः
सुसंयतात्माग्निकार्येष्वचोद्यः ।
वने वसन्नतिथिष्वप्रमत्तो
धुरन्धरः पुण्यकृदेष तापसः ॥
iast:
nīvāra mūleṅguda śākavṛttiḥ
susaṃyatātmāgnikāryeṣvacodyaḥ |
vane vasannatithiṣvapramatto
dhurandharaḥ puṇyakṛdeṣa tāpasaḥ ||
english: Living on wild rice, roots, ingudi nuts and greens, well self-controlled, needing no urging in the fire rites, living in the forest and attentive to guests: this foremost doer of good is an ascetic.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns that one who has wronged a wise person should not feel safe at a distance, for the wise have long arms.
devanagari:
अपकृत्वा बुद्धिमतो दूरस्थोऽस्मीति नाश्वसेत् ।
दीर्घौ बुद्धिमतो बाहू याभ्यां हिंसति हिंसितः ॥
iast:
apakṛtvā buddhimato dūrastho'smīti nāśvaset |
dīrghau buddhimato bāhū yābhyāṃ hiṃsati hiṃsitaḥ ||
english: Having wronged a wise person, one should not relax, thinking 'I am far away'. The arms of the wise are long; with them, the one who was harmed strikes back.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises not trusting the untrustworthy, nor over-trusting the trustworthy, since fear born of trust cuts even the roots.
devanagari:
न विश्वसेदविश्वस्ते विश्वस्ते नातिविश्वसेत् ।
विश्वासाद्भयमुत्पन्नं मूलान्यपि निकृन्तति ॥
iast:
na viśvasedaviśvaste viśvaste nātiviśvaset |
viśvāsādbhayamutpannaṃ mūlānyapi nikṛntati ||
english: Do not trust one who is not trustworthy, and do not trust too much one who is. Danger that arises from trust cuts away even the roots.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura gives a husband's conduct in the terms of his time: not jealous, generous, kind-spoken, but not under women's control.
devanagari:
अनीर्ष्युर्गुप्तदारः स्यात्संविभागी प्रियंवदः ।
श्लक्ष्णो मधुरवाक्स्त्रीणां न चासां वशगो भवेत् ॥
iast:
anīrṣyurguptadāraḥ syātsaṃvibhāgī priyaṃvadaḥ |
ślakṣṇo madhuravākstrīṇāṃ na cāsāṃ vaśago bhavet ||
english: One should be free of jealousy, guard one's wife, share with others, speak kindly, be gentle and sweet-spoken to women, but not come under their control.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura praises women as worthy of honour and the light and fortune of the home, to be specially protected, in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
पूजनीया महाभागाः पुण्याश्च गृहदीप्तयः ।
स्त्रियः श्रियो गृहस्योक्तास्तस्माद्रक्ष्या विशेषतः ॥
iast:
pūjanīyā mahābhāgāḥ puṇyāśca gṛhadīptayaḥ |
striyaḥ śriyo gṛhasyoktāstasmādrakṣyā viśeṣataḥ ||
english: Women are worthy of honour, greatly blessed, pure and the light of the house. They are called the fortune of the home; so they should be protected above all.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises entrusting household areas to family members and doing key work oneself, in the household terms of his time.
devanagari:
पितुरन्तःपुरं दद्यान्मातुर्दद्यान्महानसम् ।
गोषु चात्मसमं दद्यात्स्वयमेव कृषिं व्रजेत् ।
भृत्यैर्वणिज्याचारं च पुत्रैः सेवेत ब्राह्मणान् ॥
iast:
piturantaḥpuraṃ dadyānmāturdadyānmahānasam |
goṣu cātmasamaṃ dadyātsvayameva kṛṣiṃ vrajet |
bhṛtyairvaṇijyācāraṃ ca putraiḥ seveta brāhmaṇān ||
english: Give the inner apartments to your father, give the kitchen to your mother, give the cattle to one like yourself, and go to the farming yourself. Carry on trade through servants, and serve brahmins through your sons.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says fire rose from water, the warrior from the priest, iron from stone; their power, spreading everywhere, is quenched in its source.
devanagari:
अद्भ्योऽग्निर्ब्रह्मतः क्षत्रमश्मनो लोहमुत्थितम् ।
तेषां सर्वत्रगं तेजः स्वासु योनिषु शाम्यति ॥
iast:
adbhyo'gnirbrahmataḥ kṣatramaśmano lohamutthitam |
teṣāṃ sarvatragaṃ tejaḥ svāsu yoniṣu śāmyati ||
english: Fire arose from water, the kshatriya from the brahmin, iron from stone. Their power reaches everywhere, but it is quenched in its own source.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura repeats that the good of noble family, with fire-like energy, lie forbearing and without outward sign, like fire in wood.
devanagari:
नित्यं सन्तः कुले जाताः पावकोपम तेजसः ।
क्षमावन्तो निराकाराः काष्ठेऽग्निरिव शेरते ॥
iast:
nityaṃ santaḥ kule jātāḥ pāvakopama tejasaḥ |
kṣamāvanto nirākārāḥ kāṣṭhe'gniriva śerate ||
english: The good, born in noble families, with energy like fire, always forbearing and showing no outward sign, lie quiet like fire in wood.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the king whose counsel neither outsiders nor insiders know, and who sees everywhere, enjoys power long.
devanagari:
यस्य मन्त्रं न जानन्ति बाह्याश्चाभ्यन्तराश् च ये ।
स राजा सर्वतश्चक्षुश्चिरमैश्वर्यमश्नुते ॥
iast:
yasya mantraṃ na jānanti bāhyāścābhyantarāś ca ye |
sa rājā sarvataścakṣuściramaiśvaryamaśnute ||
english: The king whose counsel is not known by those outside or those inside, and who has eyes everywhere, enjoys sovereignty for a long time.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises not announcing what one plans to do, but showing only what is done, so plans are not leaked.
devanagari:
करिष्यन्न प्रभाषेत कृतान्येव च दर्शयेत् ।
धर्मकामार्थ कार्याणि तथा मन्त्रो न भिद्यते ॥
iast:
kariṣyanna prabhāṣeta kṛtānyeva ca darśayet |
dharmakāmārtha kāryāṇi tathā mantro na bhidyate ||
english: When about to act, do not announce it; show only what has been done. In tasks of dharma, desire and wealth, in this way counsel is not leaked.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says private counsel should be held on a hilltop, in a secluded palace room, or in a forest clearing with no cover.
devanagari:
गिरिपृष्ठमुपारुह्य प्रासादं वा रहोगतः ।
अरण्ये निःशलाके वा तत्र मन्त्रो विधीयते ॥
iast:
giripṛṣṭhamupāruhya prāsādaṃ vā rahogataḥ |
araṇye niḥśalāke vā tatra mantro vidhīyate ||
english: Climbing to a mountain top or a palace roof, having gone to a secluded place, or in a forest without bushes: there counsel should be held.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a non-friend, a foolish friend, or a learned but undisciplined friend should not know one's deepest counsel.
devanagari:
नासुहृत्परमं मन्त्रं भारतार्हति वेदितुम् ।
अपण्डितो वापि सुहृत्पण्डितो वाप्यनात्मवान् ।
अमात्ये ह्यर्थलिप्सा च मन्त्ररक्षणमेव च ॥
iast:
nāsuhṛtparamaṃ mantraṃ bhāratārhati veditum |
apaṇḍito vāpi suhṛtpaṇḍito vāpyanātmavān |
amātye hyarthalipsā ca mantrarakṣaṇameva ca ||
english: One who is not a friend does not deserve to know one's highest counsel, Bharata; nor does a friend who is unwise, nor a wise one who lacks self-control. Choose a minister only after testing him, for on him depend gaining wealth and keeping counsel.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a king whose plans are secret, and whose deeds his courtiers learn of only when done, succeeds without doubt.
devanagari:
कृतानि सर्वकार्याणि यस्य वा पार्षदा विदुः ।
गूढमन्त्रस्य नृपतेस्तस्य सिद्धिरसंशयम् ॥
iast:
kṛtāni sarvakāryāṇi yasya vā pārṣadā viduḥ |
gūḍhamantrasya nṛpatestasya siddhirasaṃśayam ||
english: The king whose counsel is hidden, and whose tasks his courtiers know only once they are done: his success is beyond doubt.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who, deluded, does blameworthy deeds loses even his life when those deeds go wrong.
devanagari:
अप्रशस्तानि कर्माणि यो मोहादनुतिष्ठति ।
स तेषां विपरिभ्रंशे भ्रश्यते जीवितादपि ॥
iast:
apraśastāni karmāṇi yo mohādanutiṣṭhati |
sa teṣāṃ viparibhraṃśe bhraśyate jīvitādapi ||
english: One who out of delusion carries out blameworthy actions falls even from life when they go wrong.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says doing praiseworthy deeds brings happiness, while failing to do them brings great regret later.
devanagari:
कर्मणां तु प्रशस्तानामनुष्ठानं सुखावहम् ।
तेषामेवाननुष्ठानं पश्चात्तापकरं महत् ॥
iast:
karmaṇāṃ tu praśastānāmanuṣṭhānaṃ sukhāvaham |
teṣāmevānanuṣṭhānaṃ paścāttāpakaraṃ mahat ||
english: Doing praiseworthy actions brings happiness; not doing them causes great remorse later.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the earth is in the power of a king who knows growth and decline, the six policies, and whose conduct is beyond reproach.
devanagari:
स्थानवृद्ध क्षयज्ञस्य षाड्गुण्य विदितात्मनः ।
अनवज्ञात शीलस्य स्वाधीना पृथिवी नृप ॥
iast:
sthānavṛddha kṣayajñasya ṣāḍguṇya viditātmanaḥ |
anavajñāta śīlasya svādhīnā pṛthivī nṛpa ||
english: For one who knows standing still, growth and decline, who understands the six policies, and whose conduct is not despised, the earth is in his own control, king.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the earth gives wealth to a king whose anger and favour have effect, who checks tasks himself and keeps his own treasury.
devanagari:
अमोघक्रोधहर्षस्य स्वयं कृत्यान्ववेक्षिणः ।
आत्मप्रत्यय कोशस्य वसुधेयं वसुन्धरा ॥
iast:
amoghakrodhaharṣasya svayaṃ kṛtyānvavekṣiṇaḥ |
ātmapratyaya kośasya vasudheyaṃ vasundharā ||
english: For one whose anger and joy are not fruitless, who personally oversees what must be done, and whose treasury is known to himself, this earth yields wealth.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a ruler should be content with his title and royal parasol, share wealth with his servants, and not take everything alone.
devanagari:
नाममात्रेण तुष्येत छत्रेण च महीपतिः ।
भृत्येभ्यो विसृजेदर्थान्नैकः सर्वहरो भवेत् ॥
iast:
nāmamātreṇa tuṣyeta chatreṇa ca mahīpatiḥ |
bhṛtyebhyo visṛjedarthānnaikaḥ sarvaharo bhavet ||
english: A ruler should be content with just the name and the royal parasol. He should distribute wealth to his servants and not be the one who takes everything.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says people know their own kind: brahmin knows brahmin, husband knows wife, king knows minister and king.
devanagari:
ब्राह्मणो ब्राह्मणं वेद भर्ता वेद स्त्रियं तथा ।
अमात्यं नृपतिर्वेद राजा राजानमेव च ॥
iast:
brāhmaṇo brāhmaṇaṃ veda bhartā veda striyaṃ tathā |
amātyaṃ nṛpatirveda rājā rājānameva ca ||
english: A brahmin knows a brahmin, a husband knows his wife, a king knows his minister, and a king knows a king.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises that an enemy in one's power who deserves death should not be released, since danger soon comes from him.
devanagari:
न शत्रुरङ्कमापन्नो मोक्तव्यो वध्यतां गतः ।
अहताद्धि भयं तस्माज्जायते नचिरादिव ॥
iast:
na śatruraṅkamāpanno moktavyo vadhyatāṃ gataḥ |
ahatāddhi bhayaṃ tasmājjāyate nacirādiva ||
english: An enemy who has fallen into one's lap and deserves death should not be let go; for danger soon arises from one who is not killed.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says anger must always be carefully restrained towards gods, kings, brahmins, the old, children and the sick.
devanagari:
दैवतेषु च यत्नेन राजसु ब्राह्मणेषु च ।
नियन्तव्यः सदा क्रोधो वृद्धबालातुरेषु च ॥
iast:
daivateṣu ca yatnena rājasu brāhmaṇeṣu ca |
niyantavyaḥ sadā krodho vṛddhabālātureṣu ca ||
english: Anger should always be carefully restrained towards the gods, kings and brahmins, and towards the old, children and the sick.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise avoid pointless quarrels, which fools pursue; they gain good name and avoid harm.
devanagari:
निरर्थं कलहं प्राज्ञो वर्जयेन्मूढ सेवितम् ।
कीर्तिं च लभते लोके न चानर्थेन युज्यते ॥
iast:
nirarthaṃ kalahaṃ prājño varjayenmūḍha sevitam |
kīrtiṃ ca labhate loke na cānarthena yujyate ||
english: The wise person should avoid pointless quarrels, which fools engage in. He gains a good name in the world and is not joined to misfortune.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says no one wants a master whose favour and anger both mean nothing, using a comparison from his time about women.
devanagari:
प्रसादो निष्फलो यस्य क्रोधश्चापि निरर्थकः ।
न तं भर्तारमिच्छन्ति षण्ढं पतिमिव स्त्रियः ॥
iast:
prasādo niṣphalo yasya krodhaścāpi nirarthakaḥ |
na taṃ bhartāramicchanti ṣaṇḍhaṃ patimiva striyaḥ ||
english: One whose favour bears no fruit and whose anger is also without effect: people do not want him as master, as women do not want an impotent husband.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says intelligence does not guarantee wealth, nor dullness poverty; only the wise understand how the world turns.
devanagari:
न बुद्धिर्धनलाभाय न जाड्यमसमृद्धये ।
लोकपर्याय वृत्तान्तं प्राज्ञो जानाति नेतरः ॥
iast:
na buddhirdhanalābhāya na jāḍyamasamṛddhaye |
lokaparyāya vṛttāntaṃ prājño jānāti netaraḥ ||
english: Intelligence is not for gaining wealth, nor is dullness the cause of poverty. The wise person knows how the world turns; no one else does.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the fool always looks down on those senior in learning, conduct, age, intelligence, wealth or family.
devanagari:
विद्या शीलवयोवृद्धान्बुद्धिवृद्धांश्च भारत ।
धनाभिजन वृद्धांश्च नित्यं मूढोऽवमन्यते ॥
iast:
vidyā śīlavayovṛddhānbuddhivṛddhāṃśca bhārata |
dhanābhijana vṛddhāṃśca nityaṃ mūḍho'vamanyate ||
english: The fool always despises those senior in learning, character and age, those senior in intelligence, and those senior in wealth and family, Bharata.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says misfortunes come quickly to the ill-behaved, the foolish, the envious, the unrighteous, the foul-mouthed and the angry.
devanagari:
अनार्य वृत्तमप्राज्ञमसूयकमधार्मिकम् ।
अनर्थाः क्षिप्रमायान्ति वाग्दुष्टं क्रोधनं तथा ॥
iast:
anārya vṛttamaprājñamasūyakamadhārmikam |
anarthāḥ kṣipramāyānti vāgduṣṭaṃ krodhanaṃ tathā ||
english: Troubles quickly come to one of ignoble conduct, the unwise, the envious, the unrighteous, one who speaks harshly, and one who is quick to anger.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says not deceiving, giving, keeping agreements and well-directed speech win people over.
devanagari:
अविसंवादनं दानं समयस्याव्यतिक्रमः ।
आवर्तयन्ति भूतानि सम्यक्प्रणिहिता च वाक् ॥
iast:
avisaṃvādanaṃ dānaṃ samayasyāvyatikramaḥ |
āvartayanti bhūtāni samyakpraṇihitā ca vāk ||
english: Not deceiving, giving, not breaking an agreement, and speech well directed: these win living beings over.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who is honest, capable, grateful, sensible and straightforward finds supporters even when his treasury is exhausted.
devanagari:
अविसंवादको दक्षः कृतज्ञो मतिमानृजुः ।
अपि सङ्क्षीण कोशोऽपि लभते परिवारणम् ॥
iast:
avisaṃvādako dakṣaḥ kṛtajño matimānṛjuḥ |
api saṅkṣīṇa kośo'pi labhate parivāraṇam ||
english: One who does not deceive, is capable, grateful, intelligent and straightforward finds people around him even when his treasury is exhausted.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names seven kindlings of fortune: steadiness, calm, self-control, purity, compassion, gentle speech and not betraying friends.
devanagari:
धृतिः शमो दमः शौचं कारुण्यं वागनिष्ठुरा ।
मित्राणां चानभिद्रोहः सतैताः समिधः श्रियः ॥
iast:
dhṛtiḥ śamo damaḥ śaucaṃ kāruṇyaṃ vāganiṣṭhurā |
mitrāṇāṃ cānabhidrohaḥ sataitāḥ samidhaḥ śriyaḥ ||
english: Steadiness, calm, self-control, purity, compassion, speech that is not harsh, and not betraying friends: these seven are the fuel of good fortune.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the person who does not share, is wicked, ungrateful and shameless is the lowest of people and should be avoided.
devanagari:
असंविभागी दुष्टात्मा कृतघ्नो निरपत्रपः ।
तादृङ्नराधमो लोके वर्जनीयो नराधिप ॥
iast:
asaṃvibhāgī duṣṭātmā kṛtaghno nirapatrapaḥ |
tādṛṅnarādhamo loke varjanīyo narādhipa ||
english: One who does not share, who is evil-minded, ungrateful and shameless: such a lowest of men should be avoided in the world, lord of men.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who angers innocent people close to him, though himself at fault, sleeps uneasily, as if with a snake in the house.
devanagari:
न स रात्रौ सुखं शेते स सर्प इव वेश्मनि ।
यः कोपयति निर्दोषं स दोषोऽभ्यन्तरं जनम् ॥
iast:
na sa rātrau sukhaṃ śete sa sarpa iva veśmani |
yaḥ kopayati nirdoṣaṃ sa doṣo'bhyantaraṃ janam ||
english: He does not sleep happily at night, as if with a snake in the house, who, being himself at fault, angers innocent people close to him.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises always keeping pleased, like gods, those whose ill will could threaten one's livelihood and security.
devanagari:
येषु दुष्टेषु दोषः स्याद्योगक्षेमस्य भारत ।
सदा प्रसादनं तेषां देवतानामिवाचरेत् ॥
iast:
yeṣu duṣṭeṣu doṣaḥ syādyogakṣemasya bhārata |
sadā prasādanaṃ teṣāṃ devatānāmivācaret ||
english: Those who, if offended, could harm one's welfare and security, Bharata: one should always keep them pleased, as one would the gods.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says wealth entrusted to women, to upstarts or to ignoble people is all at risk, in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
येऽर्थाः स्त्रीषु समासक्ताः प्रथमोत्पतितेषु च ।
ये चानार्य समासक्ताः सर्वे ते संशयं गताः ॥
iast:
ye'rthāḥ strīṣu samāsaktāḥ prathamotpatiteṣu ca |
ye cānārya samāsaktāḥ sarve te saṃśayaṃ gatāḥ ||
english: Wealth entrusted to women, to those newly risen, and to the ignoble: all of it falls into doubt.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says lands ruled by a woman, a gambler or a child sink helplessly like a stone raft, in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
यत्र स्त्री यत्र कितवो यत्र बालोऽनुशास्ति च ।
मज्जन्ति तेऽवशा देशा नद्यामश्मप्लवा इव ॥
iast:
yatra strī yatra kitavo yatra bālo'nuśāsti ca |
majjanti te'vaśā deśā nadyāmaśmaplavā iva ||
english: Where a woman, a gambler or a child gives the orders, those lands sink helplessly, like a raft of stone in a river.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura counts as wise those who stick to the main purposes, not to details, since details lead to entanglement.
devanagari:
प्रयोजनेषु ये सक्ता न विशेषेषु भारत ।
तानहं पण्डितान्मन्ये विशेषा हि प्रसङ्गिनः ॥
iast:
prayojaneṣu ye saktā na viśeṣeṣu bhārata |
tānahaṃ paṇḍitānmanye viśeṣā hi prasaṅginaḥ ||
english: Those who are attached to the main purposes, not to particulars, I consider wise, Bharata; for particulars lead to entanglement.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns that one praised by gamblers, flattering bards and loose women does not really live, in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
यं प्रशंसन्ति कितवा यं प्रशंसन्ति चारणाः ।
यं प्रशंसन्ति बन्धक्यो न स जीवति मानवः ॥
iast:
yaṃ praśaṃsanti kitavā yaṃ praśaṃsanti cāraṇāḥ |
yaṃ praśaṃsanti bandhakyo na sa jīvati mānavaḥ ||
english: The man whom gamblers praise, whom bards praise, whom loose women praise: that man does not truly live.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura reproaches the king for passing over the mighty Pandavas and placing great sovereignty in Duryodhana's hands.
devanagari:
हित्वा तान्परमेष्वासान्पाण्डवानमितौजसः ।
आहितं भारतैश्वर्यं त्वया दुर्योधने महत् ॥
iast:
hitvā tānparameṣvāsānpāṇḍavānamitaujasaḥ |
āhitaṃ bhārataiśvaryaṃ tvayā duryodhane mahat ||
english: Abandoning the Pandavas, great archers of boundless energy, you have placed the great sovereignty of the Bharatas in Duryodhana, Bharata.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura predicts the king will soon see Duryodhana, blinded by pride of power, fall from it, as Bali fell from the three worlds.
devanagari:
तं द्रक्ष्यसि परिभ्रष्टं तस्मात्त्वं नचिरादिव ।
ऐश्वर्यमदसंमूढं बलिं लोकत्रयादिव ॥
iast:
taṃ drakṣyasi paribhraṣṭaṃ tasmāttvaṃ nacirādiva |
aiśvaryamadasaṃmūḍhaṃ baliṃ lokatrayādiva ||
english: You will soon see him fallen from it, bewildered by the intoxication of power, like Bali fallen from the three worlds.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra says a person has no control over gain or loss, like a puppet on strings ruled by fate, and asks Vidura to continue.
devanagari:
अनीश्वरोऽयं पुरुषो भवाभवे
सूत्रप्रोता दारुमयीव योषा ।
धात्रा हि दिष्टस्य वशे किलायं
तस्माद्वद त्वं श्रवणे घृतोऽहम् ॥
iast:
anīśvaro'yaṃ puruṣo bhavābhave
sūtraprotā dārumayīva yoṣā |
dhātrā hi diṣṭasya vaśe kilāyaṃ
tasmādvada tvaṃ śravaṇe ghṛto'ham ||
english: This person is not master of his rising or falling; he is like a wooden doll moved by strings. He is under the control of what the Creator has ordained. So speak on; I am intent on listening.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says even Brihaspati, speaking out of season, would meet contempt for his intelligence and dishonour.
devanagari:
अप्राप्तकालं वचनं बृहस्पतिरपि ब्रुवन् ।
लभते बुद्ध्यवज्ञानमवमानं च भारत ॥
iast:
aprāptakālaṃ vacanaṃ bṛhaspatirapi bruvan |
labhate buddhyavajñānamavamānaṃ ca bhārata ||
english: Even Brihaspati, speaking words at the wrong time, would meet with contempt for his intellect and with dishonour, Bharata.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says some are liked for giving, others for pleasant speech, others for strength of counsel; but one who is truly dear is dear anyway.
devanagari:
प्रियो भवति दानेन प्रियवादेन चापरः ।
मन्त्रं मूलबलेनान्यो यः प्रियः प्रिय एव सः ॥
iast:
priyo bhavati dānena priyavādena cāparaḥ |
mantraṃ mūlabalenānyo yaḥ priyaḥ priya eva saḥ ||
english: One becomes dear through gifts, another through pleasant words, another through the strength of counsel and charms; but one who is dear is dear simply.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says someone disliked is not seen as good, wise or learned; good deeds are seen in the liked and bad in the disliked.
devanagari:
द्वेष्यो न साधुर्भवति न मेधावी न पण्डितः ।
प्रिये शुभानि कर्माणि द्वेष्ये पापानि भारत ॥
iast:
dveṣyo na sādhurbhavati na medhāvī na paṇḍitaḥ |
priye śubhāni karmāṇi dveṣye pāpāni bhārata ||
english: One who is disliked is not thought good, nor intelligent, nor learned. In the one we like we see good deeds; in the one we dislike, bad ones, Bharata.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a loss that brings growth is not a loss; the real loss is a gain that leads to losing much.
devanagari:
न स क्षयो महाराज यः क्षयो वृद्धिमावहेत् ।
क्षयः स त्विह मन्तव्यो यं लब्ध्वा बहु नाशयेत् ॥
iast:
na sa kṣayo mahārāja yaḥ kṣayo vṛddhimāvahet |
kṣayaḥ sa tviha mantavyo yaṃ labdhvā bahu nāśayet ||
english: That is not a loss, great king, which brings growth. Loss here should be understood as that which, once obtained, destroys much.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says some are rich in virtues, others in wealth; avoid those rich in wealth but poor in virtue.
devanagari:
समृद्धा गुणतः के चिद्भवन्ति धनतोऽपरे ।
धनवृद्धान्गुणैर्हीनान्धृतराष्ट्र विवर्जयेत् ॥
iast:
samṛddhā guṇataḥ ke cidbhavanti dhanato'pare |
dhanavṛddhānguṇairhīnāndhṛtarāṣṭra vivarjayet ||
english: Some are prosperous in virtues, others in wealth. Avoid, Dhritarashtra, those grown rich in wealth who lack virtues.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra admits Vidura's advice is wise and far-sighted, but says he cannot give up his son, while granting that victory lies with dharma.
devanagari:
सर्वं त्वमायती युक्तं भाषसे प्राज्ञसंमतम् ।
न चोत्सहे सुतं त्यक्तुं यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः ॥
iast:
sarvaṃ tvamāyatī yuktaṃ bhāṣase prājñasaṃmatam |
na cotsahe sutaṃ tyaktuṃ yato dharmastato jayaḥ ||
english: All that you say is sound for the future and approved by the wise. Yet I cannot bring myself to abandon my son. Where dharma is, there is victory.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one endowed with natural virtue and humility will never cause even the slightest harm to living beings.
devanagari:
स्वभावगुणसम्पन्नो न जातु विनयान्वितः ।
सुसूक्ष्ममपि भूतानामुपमर्दं प्रयोक्ष्यते ॥
iast:
svabhāvaguṇasampanno na jātu vinayānvitaḥ |
susūkṣmamapi bhūtānāmupamardaṃ prayokṣyate ||
english: One endowed with good qualities by nature and with humility will never cause even the slightest harm to living beings.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura describes the wicked: always busy speaking ill of others, causing them pain, and stirring up quarrels among them.
devanagari:
परापवाद निरताः परदुःखोदयेषु च ।
परस्परविरोधे च यतन्ते सततोथिताः ॥
iast:
parāpavāda niratāḥ paraduḥkhodayeṣu ca |
parasparavirodhe ca yatante satatothitāḥ ||
english: Devoted to speaking ill of others and to causing others pain, they are always up and striving to set people against one another.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues: even seeing such people is a fault; living with them is a great danger; taking from or giving to them both bring harm.
devanagari:
स दोषं दर्शनं येषां संवासे सुमहद्भयम् ।
अर्थादाने महान्दोषः प्रदाने च महद्भयम् ॥
iast:
sa doṣaṃ darśanaṃ yeṣāṃ saṃvāse sumahadbhayam |
arthādāne mahāndoṣaḥ pradāne ca mahadbhayam ||
english: Even to see them is a fault; living with them is a very great danger. To take wealth from them is a great fault, and to give to them is a great danger.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says to avoid people known to be sinful, condemned by those who live with them, and tied to other great faults.
devanagari:
ये पापा इति विख्याताः संवासे परिगर्हिताः ।
युक्ताश्चान्यैर्महादोषैर्ये नरास्तान्विवर्जयेत् ॥
iast:
ye pāpā iti vikhyātāḥ saṃvāse parigarhitāḥ |
yuktāścānyairmahādoṣairye narāstānvivarjayet ||
english: Those known to be wicked, censured by those who live with them, and joined to other great faults: one should avoid such people.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says when friendship with a base person ends, the affection, its benefits and the happiness of friendship all vanish.
devanagari:
निवर्तमाने सौहार्दे प्रीतिर्नीचे प्रणश्यति ।
या चैव फलनिर्वृत्तिः सौहृदे चैव यत्सुखम् ॥
iast:
nivartamāne sauhārde prītirnīce praṇaśyati |
yā caiva phalanirvṛttiḥ sauhṛde caiva yatsukham ||
english: When friendship with a base person comes to an end, the affection is destroyed, along with whatever fruit and happiness the friendship brought.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues: such a person then works to defame you and to ruin you, and over a small wrong finds no peace.
devanagari:
यतते चापवादाय यत्नमारभते क्षये ।
अल्पेऽप्यपकृते मोहान्न शान्तिमुपगच्छति ॥
iast:
yatate cāpavādāya yatnamārabhate kṣaye |
alpe'pyapakṛte mohānna śāntimupagacchati ||
english: He strives to slander you and sets about your ruin; even for a small wrong, out of delusion, he finds no peace.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the learned person, after careful thought, should keep far away from friendship with such base, cruel and undisciplined people.
devanagari:
तादृशैः सङ्गतं नीचैर्नृशंसैरकृतात्मभिः ।
निशाम्य निपुणं बुद्ध्या विद्वान्दूराद्विवर्जयेत् ॥
iast:
tādṛśaiḥ saṅgataṃ nīcairnṛśaṃsairakṛtātmabhiḥ |
niśāmya nipuṇaṃ buddhyā vidvāndūrādvivarjayet ||
english: Having carefully considered it with his intellect, a learned person should keep far from association with such base, cruel and undisciplined people.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who helps poor, wretched or sick relatives gains growth in children and cattle and lasting fame.
devanagari:
यो ज्ञातिमनुगृह्णाति दरिद्रं दीनमातुरम् ।
सपुत्रपशुभिर्वृद्धिं यशश्चाव्ययमश्नुते ॥
iast:
yo jñātimanugṛhṇāti daridraṃ dīnamāturam |
saputrapaśubhirvṛddhiṃ yaśaścāvyayamaśnute ||
english: One who supports a relative who is poor, miserable or sick gains increase in sons and cattle, and undying fame.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says those who want their own good and their family's growth must help their relatives prosper, and urges the king to act well.
devanagari:
ज्ञातयो वर्धनीयास्तैर्य इच्छन्त्यात्मनः शुभम् ।
कुलवृद्धिं च राजेन्द्र तस्मात्साधु समाचर ॥
iast:
jñātayo vardhanīyāstairya icchantyātmanaḥ śubham |
kulavṛddhiṃ ca rājendra tasmātsādhu samācara ||
english: Those who wish good for themselves should help their relatives prosper, and the growth of the family too, king of kings; so act rightly.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says honouring relatives will bring the king good, for even relatives without merit should be protected.
devanagari:
श्रेयसा योक्ष्यसे राजन्कुर्वाणो ज्ञातिसत्क्रियाम् ।
विगुणा ह्यपि संरक्ष्या ज्ञातयो भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
śreyasā yokṣyase rājankurvāṇo jñātisatkriyām |
viguṇā hyapi saṃrakṣyā jñātayo bharatarṣabha ||
english: You will be joined to good fortune, king, by honouring your relatives; for even relatives without virtues should be protected, bull of the Bharatas.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura asks how much more the virtuous Pandavas, seeking the king's favour, deserve it, and urges kindness to them.
devanagari:
किं पुनर्गुणवन्तस्ते त्वत्प्रसादाभिकाङ्क्षिणः ।
प्रसादं कुरु दीनानां पाण्डवानां विशां पते ॥
iast:
kiṃ punarguṇavantaste tvatprasādābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ |
prasādaṃ kuru dīnānāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ viśāṃ pate ||
english: How much more those who are virtuous and long for your favour! Show favour to the distressed Pandavas, lord of the people.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura urges giving the Pandavas some villages for their livelihood, so the king will win fame in the world.
devanagari:
दीयन्तां ग्रामकाः के चित्तेषां वृत्त्यर्थमीश्वर ।
एवं लोके यशःप्राप्तो भविष्यत्सि नराधिप ॥
iast:
dīyantāṃ grāmakāḥ ke citteṣāṃ vṛttyarthamīśvara |
evaṃ loke yaśaḥprāpto bhaviṣyatsi narādhipa ||
english: Let some villages be given to them for their livelihood, lord; in this way you will gain fame in the world, ruler of men.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura reminds the king that as an elder he must protect his sons, and that Vidura speaks for his good.
devanagari:
वृद्धेन हि त्वया कार्यं पुत्राणां तात रक्षणम् ।
मया चापि हितं वाच्यं विद्धि मां त्वद्धितैषिणम् ॥
iast:
vṛddhena hi tvayā kāryaṃ putrāṇāṃ tāta rakṣaṇam |
mayā cāpi hitaṃ vācyaṃ viddhi māṃ tvaddhitaiṣiṇam ||
english: You are old, and you must protect your sons, dear one. I too must say what is good for you; know me as one who wishes you well.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who wants well-being should not quarrel with relatives, but enjoy good things together with them.
devanagari:
ज्ञातिभिर्विग्रहस्तात न कर्तव्यो भवार्थिना ।
सुखानि सह भोज्यानि ज्ञातिभिर्भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
jñātibhirvigrahastāta na kartavyo bhavārthinā |
sukhāni saha bhojyāni jñātibhirbharatarṣabha ||
english: One who seeks well-being should not make war with relatives, dear one; pleasures should be enjoyed together with relatives, bull of the Bharatas.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says eating together, talking together and mutual affection belong with relatives, never hostility.
devanagari:
सम्भोजनं सङ्कथनं सम्प्रीतिश् च परस्परम् ।
ज्ञातिभिः सह कार्याणि न विरोधः कथं चन ॥
iast:
sambhojanaṃ saṅkathanaṃ samprītiś ca parasparam |
jñātibhiḥ saha kāryāṇi na virodhaḥ kathaṃ cana ||
english: Eating together, talking together and affection for one another should be shared with relatives, never hostility.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says relatives can rescue or drown one: the well-behaved rescue, the ill-behaved drown.
devanagari:
ज्ञातयस्तारयन्तीह ज्ञातयो मज्जयन्ति च ।
सुवृत्तास्तारयन्तीह दुर्वृत्ता मज्जयन्ति च ॥
iast:
jñātayastārayantīha jñātayo majjayanti ca |
suvṛttāstārayantīha durvṛttā majjayanti ca ||
english: Relatives carry one across here, and relatives drown one. The well-behaved carry one across; the ill-behaved drown one.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura urges the king to behave well towards the Pandavas; surrounded by them he will be unassailable by enemies.
devanagari:
सुवृत्तो भव राजेन्द्र पाण्डवान्प्रति मानद ।
अधर्षणीयः शत्रूणां तैर्वृतस्त्वं भविष्यसि ॥
iast:
suvṛtto bhava rājendra pāṇḍavānprati mānada |
adharṣaṇīyaḥ śatrūṇāṃ tairvṛtastvaṃ bhaviṣyasi ||
english: Behave well towards the Pandavas, king of kings, giver of honour. Surrounded by them, you will be beyond the reach of enemies.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says if a relative comes to a prosperous relative and suffers, the wealthy one bears the sin, like a hunter's poisoned arrow.
devanagari:
श्रीमन्तं ज्ञातिमासाद्य यो ज्ञातिरवसीदति ।
दिग्धहस्तं मृग इव स एनस्तस्य विन्दति ॥
iast:
śrīmantaṃ jñātimāsādya yo jñātiravasīdati |
digdhahastaṃ mṛga iva sa enastasya vindati ||
english: If a relative comes to a prosperous relative and still suffers, the prosperous one incurs his sin, as a hunter with a poisoned arrow incurs the deer's.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns the king he will later feel remorse on hearing that the Pandavas or his own sons are slain, and urges him to reflect.
devanagari:
पश्चादपि नरश्रेष्ठ तव तापो भविष्यति ।
तान्वा हतान्सुतान्वापि श्रुत्वा तदनुचिन्तय ॥
iast:
paścādapi naraśreṣṭha tava tāpo bhaviṣyati |
tānvā hatānsutānvāpi śrutvā tadanucintaya ||
english: Later on, best of men, remorse will come to you when you hear that they, or your sons, have been killed. Think on that.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says since life is uncertain, one should not begin any deed that will cause regret on one's deathbed.
devanagari:
येन खट्वां समारूढः परितप्येत कर्मणा ।
आदावेव न तत्कुर्यादध्रुवे जीविते सति ॥
iast:
yena khaṭvāṃ samārūḍhaḥ paritapyeta karmaṇā |
ādāveva na tatkuryādadhruve jīvite sati ||
english: Since life is uncertain, one should not do in the first place that deed for which one would grieve when lying on one's bed.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says no one except Shukra never errs; but setting right what remains lies with the wise.
devanagari:
न कश्चिन्नापनयते पुमानन्यत्र भार्गवात् ।
शेषसम्प्रतिपत्तिस्तु बुद्धिमत्स्वेव तिष्ठति ॥
iast:
na kaścinnāpanayate pumānanyatra bhārgavāt |
śeṣasampratipattistu buddhimatsveva tiṣṭhati ||
english: There is no one who never errs, except the Bhargava Shukra. But the setting right of what remains rests with the intelligent.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wrong Duryodhana did the Pandavas long ago must be undone by the king as the family's elder.
devanagari:
दुर्योधनेन यद्येतत्पापं तेषु पुरा कृतम् ।
त्वया तत्कुलवृद्धेन प्रत्यानेयं नरेश्वर ॥
iast:
duryodhanena yadyetatpāpaṃ teṣu purā kṛtam |
tvayā tatkulavṛddhena pratyāneyaṃ nareśvara ||
english: If Duryodhana did this wrong to them in the past, it must be set right by you, the elder of the family, lord of men.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says by restoring the Pandavas to their place, the king will be free of stain and honoured by the wise.
devanagari:
तांस्त्वं पदे प्रतिष्ठाप्य लोके विगतकल्मषः ।
भविष्यसि नरश्रेष्ठ पूजनीयो मनीषिणाम् ॥
iast:
tāṃstvaṃ pade pratiṣṭhāpya loke vigatakalmaṣaḥ |
bhaviṣyasi naraśreṣṭha pūjanīyo manīṣiṇām ||
english: By restoring them to their position, you will be free of stain in the world, best of men, and worthy of the honour of the wise.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who weighs the wise's sound words by their results and then acts on them stays long in good repute.
devanagari:
सुव्याहृतानि धीराणां फलतः प्रविचिन्त्य यः ।
अध्यवस्यति कार्येषु चिरं यशसि तिष्ठति ॥
iast:
suvyāhṛtāni dhīrāṇāṃ phalataḥ pravicintya yaḥ |
adhyavasyati kāryeṣu ciraṃ yaśasi tiṣṭhati ||
english: One who considers the well-spoken words of the wise in light of their results, and then resolves on what to do, remains long in good fame.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says humility destroys bad repute, effort destroys misfortune, forbearance always destroys anger, and good conduct destroys ill signs.
devanagari:
अवृत्तिं विनयो हन्ति हन्त्यनर्थं पराक्रमः ।
हन्ति नित्यं क्षमा क्रोधमाचारो हन्त्यलक्षणम् ॥
iast:
avṛttiṃ vinayo hanti hantyanarthaṃ parākramaḥ |
hanti nityaṃ kṣamā krodhamācāro hantyalakṣaṇam ||
english: Humility destroys disgrace; effort destroys misfortune; patience always destroys anger; good conduct destroys bad marks.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a family should be judged by its household, its rule, its home, its service, and its food and clothing.
devanagari:
परिच्छदेन क्षत्रेण वेश्मना परिचर्यया ।
परीक्षेत कुलं राजन्भोजनाच्छादनेन च ॥
iast:
paricchadena kṣatreṇa veśmanā paricaryayā |
parīkṣeta kulaṃ rājanbhojanācchādanena ca ||
english: One should examine a family, king, by its belongings, its rule, its dwelling, its service, and its food and clothing.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says friendship never wears out between two whose minds, secrets and understanding meet.
devanagari:
ययोश्चित्तेन वा चित्तं नैभृतं नैभृतेन वा ।
समेति प्रज्ञया प्रज्ञा तयोर्मैत्री न जीर्यते ॥
iast:
yayościttena vā cittaṃ naibhṛtaṃ naibhṛtena vā |
sameti prajñayā prajñā tayormaitrī na jīryate ||
english: When two people's minds meet, their secrets meet, and their understanding meets, their friendship does not wear out.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise should avoid the foolish and thoughtless like a well hidden by grass, for friendship with them perishes.
devanagari:
दुर्बुद्धिमकृतप्रज्ञं छन्नं कूपं तृणैरिव ।
विवर्जयीत मेधावी तस्मिन्मैत्री प्रणश्यति ॥
iast:
durbuddhimakṛtaprajñaṃ channaṃ kūpaṃ tṛṇairiva |
vivarjayīta medhāvī tasminmaitrī praṇaśyati ||
english: The intelligent person should avoid one of bad understanding and untrained mind, like a well covered with grass; friendship with such a person is destroyed.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise should not make friends with the arrogant, the foolish, the violent and reckless, or those who have left dharma.
devanagari:
अवलिप्तेषु मूर्खेषु रौद्रसाहसिकेषु च ।
तथैवापेत धर्मेषु न मैत्रीमाचरेद्बुधः ॥
iast:
avalipteṣu mūrkheṣu raudrasāhasikeṣu ca |
tathaivāpeta dharmeṣu na maitrīmācaredbudhaḥ ||
english: With the arrogant, with fools, with the fierce and reckless, and likewise with those who have abandoned dharma, the wise should not form friendship.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura describes the friend to seek: grateful, righteous, truthful, generous, loyal, self-controlled, steady, and one who never abandons you.
devanagari:
कृतज्ञं धार्मिकं सत्यमक्षुद्रं दृढभक्तिकम् ।
जितेन्द्रियं स्थितं स्थित्यां मित्रमत्यागि चेष्यते ॥
iast:
kṛtajñaṃ dhārmikaṃ satyamakṣudraṃ dṛḍhabhaktikam |
jitendriyaṃ sthitaṃ sthityāṃ mitramatyāgi ceṣyate ||
english: One who is grateful, righteous, truthful, not petty, firmly devoted, master of the senses, keeping within bounds, and who does not abandon a friend: such a friend is desired.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says total denial of the senses is no better than death, while indulging them excessively would ruin even the gods.
devanagari:
इन्द्रियाणामनुत्सर्गो मृत्युना न विशिष्यते ।
अत्यर्थं पुनरुत्सर्गः सादयेद्दैवतान्यपि ॥
iast:
indriyāṇāmanutsargo mṛtyunā na viśiṣyate |
atyarthaṃ punarutsargaḥ sādayeddaivatānyapi ||
english: Not letting the senses go at all is no different from death; but letting them go too far would ruin even the gods.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the wise call gentleness to all beings, freedom from envy, forbearance, steadiness and not slighting friends the things that lengthen life.
devanagari:
मार्दवं सर्वभूतानामनसूया क्षमा धृतिः ।
आयुष्याणि बुधाः प्राहुर्मित्राणां चाविमानना ॥
iast:
mārdavaṃ sarvabhūtānāmanasūyā kṣamā dhṛtiḥ |
āyuṣyāṇi budhāḥ prāhurmitrāṇāṃ cāvimānanā ||
english: Gentleness to all beings, freedom from envy, forgiveness, steadiness, and not insulting friends: the wise say these lengthen life.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who, with firm resolve, tries by good policy to recover what bad policy lost has a courageous person's vow.
devanagari:
अपनीतं सुनीतेन योऽर्थं प्रत्यानिनीषते ।
मतिमास्थाय सुदृढां तदकापुरुष व्रतम् ॥
iast:
apanītaṃ sunītena yo'rthaṃ pratyāninīṣate |
matimāsthāya sudṛḍhāṃ tadakāpuruṣa vratam ||
english: One who, holding to a firm resolve, seeks by good conduct to win back a gain lost through bad conduct: that is the vow of a person who is no coward.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who plans remedies for the future, is decisive in the present, and knows what remains from the past does not lose his goals.
devanagari:
आयत्यां प्रतिकारज्ञस्तदात्वे दृढनिश्चयः ।
अतीते कार्यशेषज्ञो नरोऽर्थैर्न प्रहीयते ॥
iast:
āyatyāṃ pratikārajñastadātve dṛḍhaniścayaḥ |
atīte kāryaśeṣajño naro'rthairna prahīyate ||
english: One who knows the remedy for the future, is firm in resolve in the present, and knows what remains to be done from the past, is not deprived of his aims.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says whatever one repeatedly does in deed, mind and speech carries one away, so one should practise what is good.
devanagari:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा यदभीक्ष्णं निषेवते ।
तदेवापहरत्येनं तस्मात्कल्याणमाचरेत् ॥
iast:
karmaṇā manasā vācā yadabhīkṣṇaṃ niṣevate |
tadevāpaharatyenaṃ tasmātkalyāṇamācaret ||
english: Whatever one repeatedly practises in action, mind and speech, that very thing carries one away; so one should practise what is good.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says touching auspicious things, discipline, learning, effort, straightforwardness and frequently seeing good people bring prosperity.
devanagari:
मङ्गलालम्भनं योगः श्रुतमुत्थानमार्जवम् ।
भूतिमेतानि कुर्वन्ति सतां चाभीक्ष्ण दर्शनम् ॥
iast:
maṅgalālambhanaṃ yogaḥ śrutamutthānamārjavam |
bhūtimetāni kurvanti satāṃ cābhīkṣṇa darśanam ||
english: Touching auspicious things, discipline, learning, effort, honesty, and often seeing good people: these bring prosperity.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says not losing heart is the root of fortune and of happiness when sorrow ends; the undiscouraged become great.
devanagari:
अनिर्वेदः श्रियो मूलं दुःखनाशे सुखस्य च ।
महान्भवत्यनिर्विण्णः सुखं चात्यन्तमश्नुते ॥
iast:
anirvedaḥ śriyo mūlaṃ duḥkhanāśe sukhasya ca |
mahānbhavatyanirviṇṇaḥ sukhaṃ cātyantamaśnute ||
english: Not losing heart is the root of fortune, and of happiness when sorrow ends. One who does not lose heart becomes great and enjoys lasting happiness.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says for a powerful person, nothing is more fortunate or beneficial than forgiveness, everywhere and always.
devanagari:
नातः श्रीमत्तरं किं चिदन्यत्पथ्यतमं तथा ।
प्रभ विष्णोर्यथा तात क्षमा सर्वत्र सर्वदा ॥
iast:
nātaḥ śrīmattaraṃ kiṃ cidanyatpathyatamaṃ tathā |
prabha viṣṇoryathā tāta kṣamā sarvatra sarvadā ||
english: For one who is powerful, dear one, there is nothing more glorious and nothing more wholesome than forgiveness, everywhere and always.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the weak should forgive everyone, the strong for dharma's sake; for one who sees gain and loss as equal, forgiveness always helps.
devanagari:
क्षमेदशक्तः सर्वस्य शक्तिमान्धर्मकारणात् ।
अर्थानर्थौ समौ यस्य तस्य नित्यं क्षमा हिता ॥
iast:
kṣamedaśaktaḥ sarvasya śaktimāndharmakāraṇāt |
arthānarthau samau yasya tasya nityaṃ kṣamā hitā ||
english: The powerless should forgive everyone; the powerful should forgive for the sake of dharma. For one to whom gain and loss are the same, forgiveness is always beneficial.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one may freely enjoy pleasures that cost neither dharma nor wealth, but should not take up foolish vows of denial.
devanagari:
यत्सुखं सेवमानोऽपि धर्मार्थाभ्यां न हीयते ।
कामं तदुपसेवेत न मूढ व्रतमाचरेत् ॥
iast:
yatsukhaṃ sevamāno'pi dharmārthābhyāṃ na hīyate |
kāmaṃ tadupaseveta na mūḍha vratamācaret ||
english: Whatever pleasure one can enjoy without losing dharma or wealth, one may freely enjoy; one should not practise the vow of a fool.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says fortune does not stay with the grief-stricken, the careless, unbelievers, the lazy, the undisciplined, or those without enthusiasm.
devanagari:
दुःखार्तेषु प्रमत्तेषु नास्तिकेष्वलसेषु च ।
न श्रीर्वसत्यदान्तेषु ये चोत्साह विवर्जिताः ॥
iast:
duḥkhārteṣu pramatteṣu nāstikeṣvalaseṣu ca |
na śrīrvasatyadānteṣu ye cotsāha vivarjitāḥ ||
english: Fortune does not dwell with those overcome by sorrow, the careless, unbelievers, the lazy, the undisciplined, and those without energy.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the ill-minded take an honest, modest person for weak and so attack him.
devanagari:
आर्जवेन नरं युक्तमार्जवात्सव्यपत्रपम् ।
अशक्तिमन्तं मन्यन्तो धर्षयन्ति कुबुद्धयः ॥
iast:
ārjavena naraṃ yuktamārjavātsavyapatrapam |
aśaktimantaṃ manyanto dharṣayanti kubuddhayaḥ ||
english: A person who is straightforward and, because of his straightforwardness, modest: the evil-minded think him powerless and attack him.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says fortune keeps away, as if afraid, from the excessively noble, over-generous, over-brave, over-ascetic and the proud of intellect.
devanagari:
अत्यार्यमतिदातारमतिशूरमतिव्रतम् ।
प्रज्ञाभिमानिनं चैव श्रीर्भयान्नोपसर्पति ॥
iast:
atyāryamatidātāramatiśūramativratam |
prajñābhimāninaṃ caiva śrīrbhayānnopasarpati ||
english: Fortune, as if out of fear, does not approach one who is too noble, too generous, too brave, too strict in vows, or proud of his wisdom.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names the fruits: of the Vedas, fire offerings; of learning, good conduct; of a wife, love and children; of wealth, giving and enjoying.
devanagari:
अग्निहोत्रफला वेदाः शीलवृत्तफलं श्रुतम् ।
रतिपुत्र फला दारा दत्तभुक्त फलं धनम् ॥
iast:
agnihotraphalā vedāḥ śīlavṛttaphalaṃ śrutam |
ratiputra phalā dārā dattabhukta phalaṃ dhanam ||
english: The fruit of the Vedas is the fire offering; the fruit of learning is good character and conduct; the fruit of a wife is love and sons; the fruit of wealth is giving and enjoying it.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who performs rites for the next world with wrongly gained wealth does not enjoy their fruit after death.
devanagari:
अधर्मोपार्जितैरर्थैर्यः करोत्यौर्ध्व देहिकम् ।
न स तस्य फलं प्रेत्य भुङ्क्तेऽर्थस्य दुरागमात् ॥
iast:
adharmopārjitairarthairyaḥ karotyaurdhva dehikam |
na sa tasya phalaṃ pretya bhuṅkte'rthasya durāgamāt ||
english: One who performs rites for the afterlife with wealth gained unrighteously does not enjoy their fruit after death, because the wealth came by a bad road.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says those with reserves feel no fear in wild forests and strongholds, in hard calamities, in panic or before raised weapons.
devanagari:
कानार वनदुर्गेषु कृच्छ्रास्वापत्सु सम्भ्रमे ।
उद्यतेषु च शस्त्रेषु नास्ति शेषवतां भयम् ॥
iast:
kānāra vanadurgeṣu kṛcchrāsvāpatsu sambhrame |
udyateṣu ca śastreṣu nāsti śeṣavatāṃ bhayam ||
english: In wildernesses, forests and fortresses, in hard calamities, in panic, and when weapons are raised, those who have something in reserve have no fear.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names the roots of prosperity: effort, restraint, skill, attentiveness, steadiness, memory, and beginning only after reflection.
devanagari:
उत्थानं संयमो दाक्ष्यमप्रमादो धृतिः स्मृतिः ।
समीक्ष्य च समारम्भो विद्धि मूलं भवस्य तत् ॥
iast:
utthānaṃ saṃyamo dākṣyamapramādo dhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ |
samīkṣya ca samārambho viddhi mūlaṃ bhavasya tat ||
english: Effort, self-restraint, skill, attentiveness, steadiness, memory, and starting things after careful thought: know these as the root of prosperity.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says austerity is the ascetic's strength, Brahman the knower's, violence the wicked's, and forgiveness the virtuous person's.
devanagari:
तपोबलं तापसानां ब्रह्म ब्रह्मविदां बलम् ।
हिंसा बलमसाधूनां क्षमागुणवतां बलम् ॥
iast:
tapobalaṃ tāpasānāṃ brahma brahmavidāṃ balam |
hiṃsā balamasādhūnāṃ kṣamāguṇavatāṃ balam ||
english: Austerity is the strength of ascetics; Brahman is the strength of those who know Brahman; violence is the strength of the wicked; forgiveness is the strength of the virtuous.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists eight things that do not break a fast, including water, roots, fruit, milk and medicine.
devanagari:
अष्टौ तान्यव्रतघ्नानि आपो मूलं फलं पयः ।
हविर्ब्राह्मण काम्या च गुरोर्वचनमौषधम् ॥
iast:
aṣṭau tānyavrataghnāni āpo mūlaṃ phalaṃ payaḥ |
havirbrāhmaṇa kāmyā ca gurorvacanamauṣadham ||
english: These eight do not break a vow: water, roots, fruit, milk, ghee, what a brahmin wishes, the teacher's word, and medicine.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura sums up dharma: do not do to another what is disagreeable to yourself; acting otherwise comes from desire.
devanagari:
न तत्परस्य सन्दध्यात्प्रतिकूलं यदात्मनः ।
सङ्ग्रहेणैष धर्मः स्यात्कामादन्यः प्रवर्तते ॥
iast:
na tatparasya sandadhyātpratikūlaṃ yadātmanaḥ |
saṅgraheṇaiṣa dharmaḥ syātkāmādanyaḥ pravartate ||
english: One should not do to another what is disagreeable to oneself. This, in brief, is dharma; other conduct springs from desire.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says conquer anger with calm, the wicked with goodness, the miser with giving, and falsehood with truth.
devanagari:
अक्रोधेन जयेत्क्रोधमसाधुं साधुना जयेत् ।
जयेत्कदर्यं दानेन जयेत्सत्येन चानृतम् ॥
iast:
akrodhena jayetkrodhamasādhuṃ sādhunā jayet |
jayetkadaryaṃ dānena jayetsatyena cānṛtam ||
english: Conquer anger with calm; conquer the wicked with goodness; conquer the miser with giving; and conquer falsehood with truth.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists people not to trust, including women, in the terms of his time, along with the deceitful, lazy, cowardly, violent, boastful, thieving and ungrateful.
devanagari:
स्त्री धूर्तकेऽलसे भीरौ चण्डे पुरुषमानिनि ।
चौरे कृतघ्ने विश्वासो न कार्यो न च नास्तिके ॥
iast:
strī dhūrtake'lase bhīrau caṇḍe puruṣamānini |
caure kṛtaghne viśvāso na kāryo na ca nāstike ||
english: Trust should not be placed in a woman, a cheat, a lazy person, a coward, a fierce person, one who boasts of his manliness, a thief, an ungrateful person, or an unbeliever.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says for one who habitually greets and serves elders, four things grow: reputation, life, fame and strength.
devanagari:
अभिवादनशीलस्य नित्यं वृद्धोपसेविनः ।
चत्वारि सम्प्रवर्धन्ते कीर्तिरायुर्यशोबलम् ॥
iast:
abhivādanaśīlasya nityaṃ vṛddhopasevinaḥ |
catvāri sampravardhante kīrtirāyuryaśobalam ||
english: For one who is in the habit of greeting respectfully and always serves the elderly, four things increase: reputation, life, fame and strength.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises not setting one's heart on gains that come through great suffering, by breaking dharma, or by bowing to an enemy.
devanagari:
अतिक्लेशेन येऽर्थाः स्युर्धर्मस्यातिक्रमेण च ।
अरेर्वा प्रणिपातेन मा स्म तेषु मनः कृथाः ॥
iast:
atikleśena ye'rthāḥ syurdharmasyātikrameṇa ca |
arervā praṇipātena mā sma teṣu manaḥ kṛthāḥ ||
english: Gains that come through excessive hardship, by violating dharma, or by bowing down to an enemy: do not set your mind on them.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the uneducated person, a childless couple, hungry people and a land without a ruler are to be pitied.
devanagari:
अविद्यः पुरुषः शोच्यः शोच्यं मिथुनमप्रजम् ।
निराहाराः प्रजाः शोच्याः शोच्यं राष्ट्रमराजकम् ॥
iast:
avidyaḥ puruṣaḥ śocyaḥ śocyaṃ mithunamaprajam |
nirāhārāḥ prajāḥ śocyāḥ śocyaṃ rāṣṭramarājakam ||
english: An uneducated person is to be pitied; a couple without children is to be pitied; people without food are to be pitied; a kingdom without a king is to be pitied.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names what wears things down, including the travel of the body and the mind's unrest, with a line on women in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
अध्वा जरा देहवतां पर्वतानां जलं जरा ।
असम्भोगो जरा स्त्रीणां वाक्षल्यं मनसो जरा ॥
iast:
adhvā jarā dehavatāṃ parvatānāṃ jalaṃ jarā |
asambhogo jarā strīṇāṃ vākṣalyaṃ manaso jarā ||
english: Travel is old age for embodied beings; water is old age for mountains; lack of enjoyment is old age for women; harsh words are old age for the mind.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura names what stains things, from neglected study to broken vows, with lines on women in the terms of his time.
devanagari:
अनाम्नाय मला वेदा ब्राह्मणस्याव्रतं मलम् ।
कौतूहलमला साध्वी विप्रवास मलाः स्त्रियः ॥
iast:
anāmnāya malā vedā brāhmaṇasyāvrataṃ malam |
kautūhalamalā sādhvī vipravāsa malāḥ striyaḥ ||
english: Not reciting is the stain of the Vedas; not keeping vows is the stain of a brahmin; curiosity is the stain of a virtuous woman; living away from home is the stain of women.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura gives a chain of impurities: silver is gold's dross, tin silver's, lead tin's, and of lead, mere dross.
devanagari:
सुवर्णस्य मलं रूप्यं रूप्यस्यापि मलं त्रपु ।
ज्ञेयं त्रपु मलं सीसं सीसस्यापि मलं मलम् ॥
iast:
suvarṇasya malaṃ rūpyaṃ rūpyasyāpi malaṃ trapu |
jñeyaṃ trapu malaṃ sīsaṃ sīsasyāpi malaṃ malam ||
english: Silver is the dross of gold, tin the dross of silver; lead is known as the dross of tin, and of lead the dross is dross.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says some appetites cannot be beaten by feeding them: sleep by sleeping, fire by fuel, drink by drinking; one line on women reflects his time.
devanagari:
न स्वप्नेन जयेन्निद्रां न कामेन स्त्रियं जयेत् ।
नेन्धनेन जयेदग्निं न पानेन सुरां जयेत् ॥
iast:
na svapnena jayennidrāṃ na kāmena striyaṃ jayet |
nendhanena jayedagniṃ na pānena surāṃ jayet ||
english: One cannot conquer sleep by sleeping, nor a woman by desire, nor fire by fuel, nor liquor by drinking.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says a life is fruitful when friends are won by giving, enemies defeated in battle, and wives won with food and drink.
devanagari:
यस्य दानजितं मित्रममित्रा युधि निर्जिताः ।
अन्नपानजिता दाराः सफलं तस्य जीवितम् ॥
iast:
yasya dānajitaṃ mitramamitrā yudhi nirjitāḥ |
annapānajitā dārāḥ saphalaṃ tasya jīvitam ||
english: One whose friends are won by gifts, whose enemies are conquered in battle, and whose wives are won by food and drink: his life is fruitful.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says people with thousands live, and people with hundreds live too; he urges Dhritarashtra to give up craving, since one can live anyhow.
devanagari:
सहस्रिणोऽपि जीवन्ति जीवन्ति शतिनस्तथा ।
धृतराष्ट्रं विमुञ्चेच्छां न कथं चिन्न जीव्यते ॥
iast:
sahasriṇo'pi jīvanti jīvanti śatinastathā |
dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ vimuñcecchāṃ na kathaṃ cinna jīvyate ||
english: Those with thousands live, and those with hundreds also live. Give up craving, Dhritarashtra; there is no way one cannot live.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says all the rice, barley, gold, cattle and women on earth would not satisfy one person; who sees this is not deluded.
devanagari:
यत्पृथिव्यां व्रीहि यवं हिरण्यं पशवः स्त्रियः ।
नालमेकस्य तत्सर्वमिति पश्यन्न मुह्यति ॥
iast:
yatpṛthivyāṃ vrīhi yavaṃ hiraṇyaṃ paśavaḥ striyaḥ |
nālamekasya tatsarvamiti paśyanna muhyati ||
english: All the rice, barley, gold, cattle and women on earth are not enough for even one person: one who sees this is not deluded.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura again urges the king to treat his own sons and Pandu's sons equally.
devanagari:
राजन्भूयो ब्रवीमि त्वां पुत्रेषु सममाचर ।
समता यदि ते राजन्स्वेषु पाण्डुसुतेषु च ॥
iast:
rājanbhūyo bravīmi tvāṃ putreṣu samamācara |
samatā yadi te rājansveṣu pāṇḍusuteṣu ca ||
english: King, I tell you again: act equally towards your sons, if you have equal regard, king, for your own sons and the sons of Pandu.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who, asked by good people, helps them freely to the limit of his power soon gains fame, for the good, pleased, bring happiness.
devanagari:
योऽभ्यर्थितः सद्भिरसज्जमानः
करोत्यर्थं शक्तिमहापयित्वा ।
क्षिप्रं यशस्तं समुपैति सन्तमलं
प्रसन्ना हि सुखाय सन्तः ॥
iast:
yo'bhyarthitaḥ sadbhirasajjamānaḥ
karotyarthaṃ śaktimahāpayitvā |
kṣipraṃ yaśastaṃ samupaiti santamalaṃ
prasannā hi sukhāya santaḥ ||
english: One who, asked by the good, helps them without hesitation and without holding back his strength, quickly gains fame; for the good, when pleased, are able to bring happiness.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who gives up even a great gain tied to wrongdoing, unprompted, sleeps happily, freed of sorrow like a snake shedding old skin.
devanagari:
महान्तमप्यर्थमधर्मयुक्तं
यः सन्त्यजत्यनुपाक्रुष्ट एव ।
सुखं स दुःखान्यवमुच्य शेते
जीर्णां त्वचं सर्प इवावमुच्य ॥
iast:
mahāntamapyarthamadharmayuktaṃ
yaḥ santyajatyanupākruṣṭa eva |
sukhaṃ sa duḥkhānyavamucya śete
jīrṇāṃ tvacaṃ sarpa ivāvamucya ||
english: One who gives up even a great gain joined to unrighteousness, without being reproached, sleeps happily, freed from sorrows, like a snake that has shed its old skin.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says lying to get ahead, slandering someone to the king, and persisting in falsehood with one's teacher equal killing a brahmin.
devanagari:
अनृतं च समुत्कर्षे राजगामि च पैशुनम् ।
गुरोश्चालीक निर्बन्धः समानि ब्रह्महत्यया ॥
iast:
anṛtaṃ ca samutkarṣe rājagāmi ca paiśunam |
guroścālīka nirbandhaḥ samāni brahmahatyayā ||
english: Lying for one's own advancement, slander that reaches the king, and persisting in falsehood towards one's teacher: these are equal to killing a brahmin.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says envy is a step to death, boasting kills fortune, and not listening, haste and self-praise are learning's three enemies.
devanagari:
असूयैक पदं मृत्युरतिवादः श्रियो वधः ।
अशुश्रूषा त्वरा श्लाघा विद्यायाः शत्रवस्त्रयः ॥
iast:
asūyaika padaṃ mṛtyurativādaḥ śriyo vadhaḥ |
aśuśrūṣā tvarā ślāghā vidyāyāḥ śatravastrayaḥ ||
english: Envy is one step from death; excessive talk is the killer of fortune. Not listening, hurry and self-praise are the three enemies of learning.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the comfort-seeker has no learning and the learner no comfort; one must give up one or the other.
devanagari:
सुखार्थिनः कुतो विद्या नास्ति विद्यार्थिनः सुखम् ।
सुखार्थी वा त्यजेद्विद्यां विद्यार्थी वा सुखं त्यजेत् ॥
iast:
sukhārthinaḥ kuto vidyā nāsti vidyārthinaḥ sukham |
sukhārthī vā tyajedvidyāṃ vidyārthī vā sukhaṃ tyajet ||
english: Where is learning for one who seeks comfort? There is no comfort for one who seeks learning. Let the comfort-seeker give up learning, or the learner give up comfort.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura gives images of insatiable things: fire is never satisfied with wood, the ocean with rivers, death with beings; one line on women reflects his time.
devanagari:
नाग्निस्तृप्यति काष्ठानां नापगानां महोदधिः ।
नान्तकः सर्वभूतानां न पुंसां वामलोचना ॥
iast:
nāgnistṛpyati kāṣṭhānāṃ nāpagānāṃ mahodadhiḥ |
nāntakaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ na puṃsāṃ vāmalocanā ||
english: Fire is never satisfied with logs, nor the great ocean with rivers, nor death with all beings, nor a beautiful-eyed woman with men.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says hope destroys steadiness, death prosperity, anger fortune, miserliness fame, neglect cattle, and one angry brahmin a kingdom.
devanagari:
आशा धृतिं हन्ति समृद्धिमन्तकः
क्रोधः श्रियं हन्ति यशः कदर्यता ।
अपालनं हन्ति पशूंश्च राजन्न्
एकः क्रुद्धो ब्राह्मणो हन्ति राष्ट्रम् ॥
iast:
āśā dhṛtiṃ hanti samṛddhimantakaḥ
krodhaḥ śriyaṃ hanti yaśaḥ kadaryatā |
apālanaṃ hanti paśūṃśca rājann
ekaḥ kruddho brāhmaṇo hanti rāṣṭram ||
english: Craving destroys steadiness; death destroys prosperity; anger destroys fortune; miserliness destroys fame; neglect destroys cattle, king; and one angry brahmin destroys a kingdom.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura lists things to keep at home always: goats, bronze, a chariot, honey, birds, a Vedic scholar, an elderly relative and a friend in hard times.
devanagari:
अजश्च कांस्यं च रथश्च नित्यं
मध्वाकर्षः शकुनिः श्रोत्रियश् च ।
वृद्धो ज्ञातिरवसन्नो वयस्य
एतानि ते सन्तु गृहे सदैव ॥
iast:
ajaśca kāṃsyaṃ ca rathaśca nityaṃ
madhvākarṣaḥ śakuniḥ śrotriyaś ca |
vṛddho jñātiravasanno vayasya
etāni te santu gṛhe sadaiva ||
english: Goats, bronze, a chariot, honey, a bird, a Vedic scholar, an aged relative and a friend fallen on hard times: may these always be in your house.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura continues the list of auspicious things for the home: goat and bull, sandal, lute, mirror, honey and ghee, conch, gold and more.
devanagari:
अजोक्षा चन्दनं वीणा आदर्शो मधुसर्पिषी ।
विषमौदुम्बरं शङ्खः स्वर्णं नाभिश्च रोचना ॥
iast:
ajokṣā candanaṃ vīṇā ādarśo madhusarpiṣī |
viṣamaudumbaraṃ śaṅkhaḥ svarṇaṃ nābhiśca rocanā ||
english: A goat and a bull, sandalwood, a lute, a mirror, honey and ghee, poison-curing fig wood, a conch, gold, musk and yellow pigment:
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says Manu declared these auspicious things should be kept at home for worship of gods and brahmins and for guests.
devanagari:
गृहे स्थापयितव्यानि धन्यानि मनुरब्रवीत् ।
देव ब्राह्मण पूजार्थमतिथीनां च भारत ॥
iast:
gṛhe sthāpayitavyāni dhanyāni manurabravīt |
deva brāhmaṇa pūjārthamatithīnāṃ ca bhārata ||
english: Manu said these auspicious things should be kept in the house, for the worship of gods and brahmins and for guests, Bharata.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura gives his highest teaching: never give up dharma out of desire, fear or greed, not even to save one's life.
devanagari:
इदं च त्वां सर्वपरं ब्रवीमि
पुण्यं पदं तात महाविशिष्टम् ।
न जातु कामान्न भयान्न लोभाद्
धर्मं त्यजेज्जीवितस्यापि हेतोः ॥
iast:
idaṃ ca tvāṃ sarvaparaṃ bravīmi
puṇyaṃ padaṃ tāta mahāviśiṣṭam |
na jātu kāmānna bhayānna lobhād
dharmaṃ tyajejjīvitasyāpi hetoḥ ||
english: And this I tell you, above all, dear one, the holy and supreme principle: never abandon dharma out of desire, fear or greed, not even for the sake of life.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says dharma and the self are eternal while pleasure, pain and the body pass; stand in the eternal and be content.
devanagari:
नित्यो धर्मः सुखदुःखे त्वनित्ये
नित्यो जीवो धातुरस्य त्वनित्यः ।
त्यक्त्वानित्यं प्रतितिष्ठस्व नित्ये
सन्तुष्य त्वं तोष परो हि लाभः ॥
iast:
nityo dharmaḥ sukhaduḥkhe tvanitye
nityo jīvo dhāturasya tvanityaḥ |
tyaktvānityaṃ pratitiṣṭhasva nitye
santuṣya tvaṃ toṣa paro hi lābhaḥ ||
english: Dharma is eternal; pleasure and pain are not. The soul is eternal; its body is not. Give up the impermanent and stand firm in the eternal. Be content, for contentment is the highest gain.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura points to mighty kings who ruled rich lands, then left their kingdoms and pleasures and passed under death's power.
devanagari:
महाबलान्पश्य मनानुभावान्
प्रशास्य भूमिं धनधान्य पूर्णाम् ।
राज्यानि हित्वा विपुलांश्च भोगान्
गतान्नरेन्द्रान्वशमन्तकस्य ॥
iast:
mahābalānpaśya manānubhāvān
praśāsya bhūmiṃ dhanadhānya pūrṇām |
rājyāni hitvā vipulāṃśca bhogān
gatānnarendrānvaśamantakasya ||
english: See the mighty and great-souled kings who ruled the earth, full of wealth and grain, and then, leaving their kingdoms and vast enjoyments, went under the power of death.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura describes how people carry out a dead son raised with hardship, and, weeping with loosened hair, cast him on the pyre like wood.
devanagari:
मृतं पुत्रं दुःखपुष्टं मनुष्या
उत्क्षिप्य राजन्स्वगृहान्निर्हरन्ति ।
तं मुक्तकेशाः करुणं रुदन्तश्
चितामध्ये काष्ठमिव क्षिपन्ति ॥
iast:
mṛtaṃ putraṃ duḥkhapuṣṭaṃ manuṣyā
utkṣipya rājansvagṛhānnirharanti |
taṃ muktakeśāḥ karuṇaṃ rudantaś
citāmadhye kāṣṭhamiva kṣipanti ||
english: A son raised through hardship dies, king, and people lift him and carry him out of the house; weeping piteously, hair loosened, they throw him onto the pyre like a piece of wood.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says others enjoy a dead man's wealth, birds and fire his body; he goes on with only his good and bad deeds.
devanagari:
अन्यो धनं प्रेतगतस्य भुङ्क्ते
वयांसि चाग्निश्च शरीरधातून् ।
द्वाभ्यामयं सह गच्छत्यमुत्र
पुण्येन पापेन च वेष्ट्यमानः ॥
iast:
anyo dhanaṃ pretagatasya bhuṅkte
vayāṃsi cāgniśca śarīradhātūn |
dvābhyāmayaṃ saha gacchatyamutra
puṇyena pāpena ca veṣṭyamānaḥ ||
english: Another enjoys the wealth of the departed; birds and fire enjoy the elements of his body. He goes to the other world with only two companions, wrapped in his merit and his sin.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says relatives, friends and sons turn back after leaving the dead at the fire; only one's own deeds follow.
devanagari:
उत्सृज्य विनिवर्तन्ते ज्ञातयः सुहृदः सुताः ।
अग्नौ प्रास्तं तु पुरुषं कर्मान्वेति स्वयं कृतम् ॥
iast:
utsṛjya vinivartante jñātayaḥ suhṛdaḥ sutāḥ |
agnau prāstaṃ tu puruṣaṃ karmānveti svayaṃ kṛtam ||
english: Relatives, friends and sons leave him and turn back; but the person thrown into the fire is followed by the deeds he himself has done.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura warns that a great darkness lies above this world and below the next, bewildering the senses, and urges the king not to be caught by it.
devanagari:
अस्माल्लोकादूर्ध्वममुष्य चाधो
महत्तमस्तिष्ठति ह्यन्धकारम् ।
तद्वै महामोहनमिन्द्रियाणां
बुध्यस्व मा त्वां प्रलभेत राजन् ॥
iast:
asmāllokādūrdhvamamuṣya cādho
mahattamastiṣṭhati hyandhakāram |
tadvai mahāmohanamindriyāṇāṃ
budhyasva mā tvāṃ pralabheta rājan ||
english: Above this world and below the next lies a great darkness, the great bewilderer of the senses. Understand this, king, so that it does not seize you.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says if the king can hear all these words and act on them, he will win the highest fame and have no fear here or hereafter.
devanagari:
इदं वचः शक्ष्यसि चेद्यथावन्
निशम्य सर्वं प्रतिपत्तुमेवम् ।
यशः परं प्राप्स्यसि जीवलोके
भयं न चामुत्र न चेह तेऽस्ति ॥
iast:
idaṃ vacaḥ śakṣyasi cedyathāvan
niśamya sarvaṃ pratipattumevam |
yaśaḥ paraṃ prāpsyasi jīvaloke
bhayaṃ na cāmutra na ceha te'sti ||
english: If you can hear all these words properly and act on them, you will win the highest fame in the world of the living, and there will be no fear for you either here or hereafter.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura calls the self a holy river with truth for water, steadiness for banks and self-control for waves; bathing in it purifies.
devanagari:
आत्मा नदी भारत पुण्यतीर्था
सत्योदका धृतिकूला दमोर्मिः ।
तस्यां स्नातः पूयते पुण्यकर्मा
पुण्यो ह्यात्मा नित्यमम्भोऽम्भ एव ॥
iast:
ātmā nadī bhārata puṇyatīrthā
satyodakā dhṛtikūlā damormiḥ |
tasyāṃ snātaḥ pūyate puṇyakarmā
puṇyo hyātmā nityamambho'mbha eva ||
english: The self is a river, Bharata, with holy bathing places: truth is its water, steadiness its banks, self-control its waves. One who does good, bathing in it, is purified; for the self is ever holy. Water is only water.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
