context: Vidura urges crossing the hard passages of birth on a boat of steadiness, across a river of five senses full of desire and anger like crocodiles.
devanagari:
कामक्रोधग्राहवतीं पञ्चेन्द्रिय जलां नदीम् ।
कृत्वा धृतिमयीं नावं जन्म दुर्गाणि सन्तर ॥
iast:
kāmakrodhagrāhavatīṃ pañcendriya jalāṃ nadīm |
kṛtvā dhṛtimayīṃ nāvaṃ janma durgāṇi santara ||
english: Making steadiness your boat, cross the hard passages of birth over the river whose waters are the five senses and whose crocodiles are desire and anger.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says one who honours and consults a relative senior in wisdom, dharma, learning or age about right and wrong action is never confused.
devanagari:
प्रज्ञा वृद्धं धर्मवृद्धं स्वबन्धुं
विद्या वृद्धं वयसा चापि वृद्धम् ।
कार्याकार्ये पूजयित्वा प्रसाद्य
यः सम्पृच्छेन्न स मुह्येत्कदा चित् ॥
iast:
prajñā vṛddhaṃ dharmavṛddhaṃ svabandhuṃ
vidyā vṛddhaṃ vayasā cāpi vṛddham |
kāryākārye pūjayitvā prasādya
yaḥ sampṛcchenna sa muhyetkadā cit ||
english: One who honours and pleases a relative grown in wisdom, in dharma, in learning or in age, and asks him about what should and should not be done, is never confused.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura advises guarding appetites with steadiness, hands and feet with the eyes, eyes and ears with the mind, and mind and speech with action.
devanagari:
धृत्या शिश्नोदरं रक्षेत्पाणिपादं च चक्षुषा ।
चक्षुः श्रोत्रे च मनसा मनो वाचं च कर्मणा ॥
iast:
dhṛtyā śiśnodaraṃ rakṣetpāṇipādaṃ ca cakṣuṣā |
cakṣuḥ śrotre ca manasā mano vācaṃ ca karmaṇā ||
english: With steadiness guard the sexual organ and the belly; with the eyes guard hands and feet; with the mind guard eyes and ears; with action guard mind and speech.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura describes the brahmin who keeps daily rites and study, avoids the fallen, speaks truth and serves his teacher, and so does not fall from Brahma's world.
devanagari:
नित्योदकी नित्ययज्ञोपवीती
नित्यस्वाध्यायी पतितान्न वर्जी ।
ऋतं ब्रुवन्गुरवे कर्म कुर्वन्
न ब्राह्मणश्च्यवते ब्रह्मलोकात् ॥
iast:
nityodakī nityayajñopavītī
nityasvādhyāyī patitānna varjī |
ṛtaṃ bruvangurave karma kurvan
na brāhmaṇaścyavate brahmalokāt ||
english: A brahmin who always performs the water rites, always wears the sacred thread, always studies, avoids the food of the fallen, speaks truth and does his teacher's work, does not fall from the world of Brahma.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the kshatriya who studies, keeps the fires, sacrifices, protects his people and dies in battle defending cows and brahmins reaches heaven.
devanagari:
अधीत्य वेदान्परिसंस्तीर्य चाग्नीन्
इष्ट्वा यज्ञैः पालयित्वा प्रजाश् च ।
गोब्राह्मणार्थे शस्त्रपूतान्तरात्मा
हतः सङ्ग्रामे क्षत्रियः स्वर्गमेति ॥
iast:
adhītya vedānparisaṃstīrya cāgnīn
iṣṭvā yajñaiḥ pālayitvā prajāś ca |
gobrāhmaṇārthe śastrapūtāntarātmā
hataḥ saṅgrāme kṣatriyaḥ svargameti ||
english: A kshatriya who has studied the Vedas, tended the fires, sacrificed, protected his subjects, and, his inner self purified by weapons, is killed in battle for the sake of cows and brahmins, goes to heaven.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the vaishya who studies, shares wealth in time with brahmins, kshatriyas and dependants, and keeps the three fires enjoys heaven.
devanagari:
वैश्योऽधीत्य ब्राह्मणान्क्षत्रियांश् च
धनैः काले संविभज्याश्रितांश् च ।
त्रेता पूतं धूममाघ्राय पुण्यं
प्रेत्य स्वर्गे देव सुखानि भुङ्क्ते ॥
iast:
vaiśyo'dhītya brāhmaṇānkṣatriyāṃś ca
dhanaiḥ kāle saṃvibhajyāśritāṃś ca |
tretā pūtaṃ dhūmamāghrāya puṇyaṃ
pretya svarge deva sukhāni bhuṅkte ||
english: A vaishya who has studied, and who in due time has shared his wealth with brahmins, kshatriyas and dependants, breathing the holy smoke of the three fires, enjoys divine happiness in heaven after death.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says the shudra who duly honours the other three classes, freed of sin, enjoys heaven after death, in the caste terms of his time.
devanagari:
ब्रह्मक्षत्रं वैश्य वर्णं च शूद्रः
क्रमेणैतान्न्यायतः पूजयानः ।
तुष्टेष्वेतेष्वव्यथो दग्धपापस्
त्यक्त्वा देहं स्वर्गसुखानि भुङ्क्ते ॥
iast:
brahmakṣatraṃ vaiśya varṇaṃ ca śūdraḥ
krameṇaitānnyāyataḥ pūjayānaḥ |
tuṣṭeṣveteṣvavyatho dagdhapāpas
tyaktvā dehaṃ svargasukhāni bhuṅkte ||
english: A shudra who rightly honours, in order, the brahmin, the kshatriya and the vaishya, when they are satisfied, free from pain and with his sins burned away, leaves the body and enjoys the joys of heaven.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Vidura
context: Vidura says he has told the dharma of the four classes, and the reason: Pandu's son is losing his warrior dharma, so the king should restore him to rule.
devanagari:
चातुर्वर्ण्यस्यैष धर्मस्तवोक्तो
हेतुं चात्र ब्रुवतो मे निबोध ।
क्षात्राद्धर्माद्धीयते पाण्डुपुत्रस्
तं त्वं राजन्राजधर्मे नियुङ्क्ष्व ॥
iast:
cāturvarṇyasyaiṣa dharmastavokto
hetuṃ cātra bruvato me nibodha |
kṣātrāddharmāddhīyate pāṇḍuputras
taṃ tvaṃ rājanrājadharme niyuṅkṣva ||
english: This dharma of the four classes has been told to you; now hear from me the reason. Pandu's son is falling away from kshatriya dharma; king, install him in the dharma of kings.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra agrees that Vidura's constant instruction is right, and says his own mind is the same as Vidura's words.
devanagari:
एवमेतद्यथा मां त्वमनुशासति नित्यदा ।
ममापि च मतिः सौम्य भवत्येवं यथात्थ माम् ॥
iast:
evametadyathā māṃ tvamanuśāsati nityadā |
mamāpi ca matiḥ saumya bhavatyevaṃ yathāttha mām ||
english: It is just as you always instruct me. My own mind too, gentle one, is just as you tell me.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra admits his resolve to favour the Pandavas always turns around again when he meets Duryodhana.
devanagari:
सा तु बुद्दिः कृताप्येवं पाण्डवान्रप्ति मे सदा ।
दुर्योधनं समासाद्य पुनर्विपरिवर्तते ॥
iast:
sā tu buddiḥ kṛtāpyevaṃ pāṇḍavānrapti me sadā |
duryodhanaṃ samāsādya punarviparivartate ||
english: But even though my mind is made up in this way towards the Pandavas, when I meet Duryodhana it turns around again.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain

speaker: Dhritarashtra
context: Dhritarashtra ends by saying no mortal can overcome fate; fate alone acts and human effort is pointless.
devanagari:
न दिष्टमभ्यतिक्रान्तुं शक्यं मर्त्येन केन चित् ।
दिष्टमेव कृतं मन्ये पौरुषं तु निरर्थकम् ॥
iast:
na diṣṭamabhyatikrāntuṃ śakyaṃ martyena kena cit |
diṣṭameva kṛtaṃ manye pauruṣaṃ tu nirarthakam ||
english: No mortal can overcome what fate has ordained. I think fate alone is what acts; human effort is useless.
licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikisource text); underlying Sanskrit work is public domain
